23604880DFE601316FDA68A86D17958E.description: Continue the above and apply knowledge of other disciplines in learning in and about the arts
comments:
Examples of this include:
  • using number sense in mathematics as an aid to understanding scales and intervals in music;
  • using research skills from history and social science to develop a monologue for a character from history;
  • using design skills and knowledge of physical science from science and technology/engineering to construct a balanced mobile sculpture.

2364C6B0DFE601316FE868A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe examples of how contemporary artists use computer technology in their work
comments: For example, students find out how software is used for animation, graphic design, theatrical lighting and sound design, choreography, or musical composition.

23647D20DFE601316FE768A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe examples of how artists make innovative uses of technologies and inventions
comments: For example, students research Matthew Brady's portrait photographs and Civil War battlefield photographs.

23642EC0DFE601316FE668A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe examples of how the discovery of new inventions and technologies, or the availability of new materials brought about changes in the arts in various time periods and cultures

23637DC0DFE601316FE468A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe characteristic features of genres and styles from a variety of world cultures and cite well-known artists associated with these styles

23633810DFE601316FE368A86D17958E.description: Identify American styles and genres of dance, music, theatre, or visual arts and architecture, describe their sources, trace their evolution, and cite well-known artists associated with these styles

2362F0A0DFE601316FE268A86D17958E.description: Concepts of Style, Stylistic Influence, and Stylistic Change

2362A870DFE601316FE168A86D17958E.description: Describe the function of cultural organizations and arts institutions such as museums, symphonies, repertory theatres, dance companies, and historical preservation organizations

23625C60DFE601316FE068A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe careers in at least one art form

236205F0DFE601316FDF68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the roles of artists in specific cultures and periods, and compare similarities and differences in these roles, considering aspects such as:
  • the conditions under which artists created, performed, and/or exhibited work and the status of artists;
  • the sources of support for the arts; and
  • the ways, such as apprenticeship or training, in which students learned the skills and knowledge that qualified them to produce or perform artistic work
comments: For example, students investigate how aspiring musicians learned playing and singing techniques in 19th century New England.

236131E0DFE601316FDD68A86D17958E.description: Describe how artistic production can shape and be influenced by the aesthetic preferences of a society

2360E850DFE601316FDC68A86D17958E.description: Interpret the meanings of artistic works by explaining how the subject matter and/or form reflect the events, ideas, religions, and customs of people living at a particular time in history
comments: For example, at the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston, students view John Singleton Copley's portrait of Paul Revere and examples of Revere's silverware. What do these works reveal about attitudes toward artistry in 18th century America?

23609CE0DFE601316FDB68A86D17958E.description: Purposes and Meanings in the Arts

235F20C0DFE601316FD768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a fundamental awareness of architectural styles and the ways that these have influenced painting and sculpture

235ED400DFE601316FD668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to describe the kinds of imagery used to represent subject matter and ideas, for example, literal representation, simplification, abstraction, or symbolism

235E8330DFE601316FD568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to recognize and describe the visual, spatial, and tactile characteristics of their own work and that of others

235DE340DFE601316FD368A86D17958E.description: Create and prepare artwork for group or individual public exhibitions

235D96B0DFE601316FD268A86D17958E.description: Maintain a portfolio of sketches and finished work

235D47E0DFE601316FD168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to articulate criteria for artistic work, describe personal style, assess and reflect on work orally and in writing, and to revise work based on criteria developed in the classroom

235CF200DFE601316FD068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to describe preliminary concepts verbally; to visualize concepts in clear schematic layouts; and to organize and complete projects

235C9BE0DFE601316FCF68A86D17958E.description: Produce work that shows an understanding of the concept of craftsmanship

235BEDE0DFE601316FCD68A86D17958E.description: Create artwork that shows knowledge of the ways in which architects, craftsmen, and designers develop abstract symbols by simplifying elements of the environment

comments: For example, students create works that convey paired concepts such as conflict and cooperation, happiness and grief, or excitement and repose.
235BA3D0DFE601316FCC68A86D17958E.description: Create artwork that employs the use of free form symbolic imagery that demonstrates personal invention, and/or conveys ideas and emotions

235B5730DFE601316FCB68A86D17958E.description: Create symbolic artwork by substituting symbols for objects, relationships, or ideas

235B1000DFE601316FCA68A86D17958E.description: Create 2D and 3D representational artwork from direct observation in order to develop skills of perception, discrimination, physical coordination, and memory of detail

23597FE0DFE601316FC568A86D17958E.description: For space and composition, create unified 2D and 3D compositions that demonstrate an understanding of balance, repetition, rhythm, scale, proportion, unity, harmony, and emphasis. Create 2D compositions that give the illusion of 3D space and volume

23591CB0DFE601316FC468A86D17958E.description:
For shape, form, and pattern, use and be able to identify an expanding and increasingly sophisticated array of shapes and forms, such as organic, geometric, positive and negative, or varieties of symmetry
  • Create complex patterns

235A6FB0DFE601316FC868A86D17958E.description: For texture, use and be able to differentiate between surface texture and the illusion of texture (visual texture)

235A1CD0DFE601316FC768A86D17958E.description: For line, use and be able to identify various types of line,
comments: for example in contour drawings, calligraphy, freehand studies from observation, memory, and imagination, and schematic studies

2359CC80DFE601316FC668A86D17958E.description:
For color, use and be able to identify hues, values, intermediate shades, tints, tones, complementary, analogous, and monochromatic colors
  • Demonstrate awareness of color by painting objective studies from life and free-form abstractions that employ relative properties of color

23587900DFE601316FC268A86D17958E.description: Maintain the workspace, materials, and tools responsibly and safely

23582E50DFE601316FC168A86D17958E.description: Use the appropriate vocabulary related to the methods, materials, and techniques students have learned and used in grades PreK–8

2357E190DFE601316FC068A86D17958E.description: Create artwork that demonstrates an awareness of the range and purpose of tools such as pens, brushes, markers, cameras, tools and equipment for printmaking and sculpture, and computers

235791D0DFE601316FBF68A86D17958E.description: Expand the repertoire of 2D and 3D art processes, techniques, and materials with a focus on the range of effects possible within each medium, such as: 2D – transparent and opaque media, wet, dry, stippled, blended, wash effects; relief printmaking effects; 3D – mobile and stabile forms, carved, molded, and constructed forms

23558830DFE601316FB868A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of assessment tools such as journals, rehearsal notes, video/audio tapes, rubrics, self, peer, and teacher evaluations to revise and refine their own or the group's work

235522F0DFE601316FB768A86D17958E.description: Give, accept, and use constructive criticism that identifies the specific steps needed to revise and refine their own or the group's work

2356AE00DFE601316FBC68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate theatre terminology to describe and analyze the strengths and weaknesses of their own or the group's work

23566660DFE601316FBB68A86D17958E.description: Identify and discuss artistic challenges and successful outcomes encountered during the creative and rehearsal process

23562030DFE601316FBA68A86D17958E.description: Articulate and justify possible criteria for critiquing classroom dramatizations and dramatic performances

2355D770DFE601316FB968A86D17958E.description: Continue to develop and refine audience behavior skills when attending informal and formal live performances

23522780DFE601316FAE68A86D17958E.description: Apply technical knowledge of safety procedures and practices in the theatre environment

2351DB30DFE601316FAD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the interrelationship between the technical aspects of production and the on-stage performers

comments: For example, students select a play from a particular historical period, genre, or style and conduct research using reference materials such as books, periodicals, museum collections, and the Internet to find appropriate examples of hairstyles, furnishings, decorative accessories, and clothing.
23518550DFE601316FAC68A86D17958E.description: Conduct research to inform the design of sets, costumes, sound, and lighting for a dramatic production.

23513F50DFE601316FAB68A86D17958E.description: Participate as a member of a technical crew or a management team for a mainstage production

2350F610DFE601316FAA68A86D17958E.description: Show appropriate respect for the safety and maintenance of the work space, tools, and equipment

23545D10DFE601316FB568A86D17958E.description: Describe characteristics of theatre technology and equipment based on a tour of a high school or professional theatre

2353EA70DFE601316FB468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the relationships among scenery, properties, lighting, sound, costumes, and make-up in creating a unified theatrical effect for a dramatic work

23539F70DFE601316FB368A86D17958E.description: Create a sound environment, composed, live, or recorded, for a dramatic work and explain how the aural elements meet the requirements of and enhance the overall effect of the text

23534D30DFE601316FB268A86D17958E.description: Draw renderings, floor plans, and/or build models of sets for a dramatic work and explain choices in using visual elements (line, shape/form, texture, color, space), and visual principles (unity, variety, harmony, balance, rhythm)

235301D0DFE601316FB168A86D17958E.description: As a member of a production crew, select and create elements of scenery, properties, lighting, and sound to signify environments, and costumes and makeup to suggest character

2352BAB0DFE601316FB068A86D17958E.description: Read and analyze a play for its technical requirements, identifying points in the script that require the addition of a technical element

23527140DFE601316FAF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and understand the roles and responsibilities of various technical personnel in creating and producing a theatrical performance

23505710DFE601316FA868A86D17958E.description: Rehearse and perform a variety of dramatic works for peers or invited audiences

234FFCB0DFE601316FA768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the purpose of the rehearsal process as a means of refining and revising work leading to a finished performance

234F9760DFE601316FA668A86D17958E.description: Identify and use appropriate vocabulary to describe kinds of stage spaces (e.g., proscenium, thrust, arena), stage directions, areas of the stage (e.g., upstage, downstage, stage right, stage left) and basic blocking techniques

234F44B0DFE601316FA568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe the distinct roles and responsibilities of the director, actors, stage manager, set and costume designers, and others involved in presenting a theatrical performance

234EF880DFE601316FA468A86D17958E.description: Read plays from a variety of cultures and historical periods, describe their themes, interpret their characters' intentions and motivations, and determine their staging requirements

234D0990DFE601316F9E68A86D17958E.description: Using the correct form and structure, write a series of dramatic scenes

234E44E0DFE601316FA268A86D17958E.description: Drawing on personal experience or research, write a monologue for an invented, literary, or historical character

234DEA90DFE601316FA168A86D17958E.description: Improvise characters, dialogue, and actions that focus on the development and resolution of dramatic conflicts

234DA0B0DFE601316FA068A86D17958E.description: Read plays and stories from a variety of cultures and historical periods and identify the characters, setting, plot, theme, and conflict

234D5820DFE601316F9F68A86D17958E.description: Identify literary characteristics of the dramatic script, including elements of dramatic structure, conventions, and format used in writing material for the stage; identify forms such as comedy and tragedy

234B7B80DFE601316F9968A86D17958E.description: In rehearsal and performance situations, perform as a productive and responsible member of an acting ensemble (i.e., demonstrate personal responsibility and commitment to a collaborative process)

234B2610DFE601316F9868A86D17958E.description: Describe and analyze, in written and oral form, characters' wants, needs, objectives, and personality characteristics

234ACEB0DFE601316F9768A86D17958E.description: Motivate character behavior by using recall of emotional experience as well as observation of the external world

234A6960DFE601316F9668A86D17958E.description: Use vocal acting skills such as breath control, diction, projection, inflection, rhythm, and pace to develop characterizations that suggest artistic choices

234C6CD0DFE601316F9C68A86D17958E.description: Use physical acting skills such as body alignment, control of isolated body parts, and rhythms to develop characterizations that suggest artistic choices

234C1730DFE601316F9B68A86D17958E.description: Make and justify choices on the selection and use of properties and costumes to support character dimensions

234BCA10DFE601316F9A68A86D17958E.description: Create and sustain a believable character throughout a scripted or improvised scene

23485E30DFE601316F9068A86D17958E.description: Listen to formal and informal performances with attention, showing understanding of the protocols of audience behavior appropriate to the style of the performance

23481830DFE601316F8F68A86D17958E.description: Interpret more complex music through movement

23498D00DFE601316F9368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic principles of meter, rhythm, tonality, intervals, chords, and harmonic progressions in an analysis of music

23492AB0DFE601316F9268A86D17958E.description: Describe specific music occurrences in a given aural example, using appropriate terminology

2348B080DFE601316F9168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the uses of elements in aural examples representing diverse genres and cultures

234662F0DFE601316F8968A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of traditional and nontraditional sound sources and electronic media when composing and arranging

23478B10DFE601316F8D68A86D17958E.description: Compose and arrange short pieces for voices or instruments within teacher-specified guidelines, using the elements of music to achieve unity and variety, tension and release, and balance

23473740DFE601316F8C68A86D17958E.description: Improvise short melodies, unaccompanied and over given rhythmic accompaniments, each in a consistent style, meter, and tonality

2346ED70DFE601316F8B68A86D17958E.description: Improvise melodic embellishments and simple rhythmic and melodic variations on given pentatonic melodies and melodies in major keys

2346A8F0DFE601316F8A68A86D17958E.description: Improvise and compose simple harmonic accompaniments

2344B9D0DFE601316F8468A86D17958E.description: Play by ear simple melodies on a melodic instrument and simple accompaniments on a harmonic instrument

2345BC00DFE601316F8768A86D17958E.description: Perform music representing diverse historical periods, genres, and cultures, with expression appropriate for the work being performed

23454E80DFE601316F8668A86D17958E.description: Perform with expression and technical accuracy on at least one string, wind, percussion, or classroom instrument, a repertoire of instrumental literature with a level of difficulty of 2, on a scale of 1 to 6 (level 3 for instrumental ensemble)

23450130DFE601316F8568A86D17958E.description: Perform on at least one instrument accurately and independently, alone and in small and large ensembles, with appropriate posture, playing position, and technique

234428F0DFE601316F8268A86D17958E.description: In a choral/instrumental ensemble or class: sight-read, accurately and expressively, music with a difficulty level of 2 on a scale of 1 to 6

2343DB90DFE601316F8168A86D17958E.description: Use standard notation to record their own musical ideas and those of others

23438700DFE601316F8068A86D17958E.description: Identify, define, and use standard notation symbols for pitch, rhythm, dynamics, tempo, articulation, and expression

23433B20DFE601316F7F68A86D17958E.description: Read and sing at sight simple melodies and intervals in both the treble and bass clefs

2342EFB0DFE601316F7E68A86D17958E.description: Read whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth, and dotted notes and rests in 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 3/8, 9/8, and alla breve meter signatures

23425FC0DFE601316F7C68A86D17958E.description: Sing music written in two and three parts (up to four parts in choral ensemble), with and without accompaniment

23421090DFE601316F7B68A86D17958E.description: Sing music representing diverse genres and cultures, with expression appropriate for the work being performed, and using a variety of languages

2341BEF0DFE601316F7A68A86D17958E.description: Sing with expression and technical accuracy a repertoire of vocal literature with a level of difficulty of 2, on a scale of 1 to 6 (level 3 for choral ensemble), including some songs performed by memory

23417830DFE601316F7968A86D17958E.description: Sing independently with increased accuracy, expanded breath control, and extended vocal range

23407F40DFE601316F7668A86D17958E.description: Understand the role of an audience for dance; discuss opinions about dances in a supportive and constructive way

23402910DFE601316F7568A86D17958E.description: Identify possible criteria for evaluating dance, such as skill of performers, originality of movement, visual and/or emotional impact, variety, contrast, and appropriateness of accompaniment

233FD160DFE601316F7468A86D17958E.description: Identify and discuss artistic challenges and successful outcomes encountered during the creative and rehearsal processes. Reflect upon the value of different solutions

233F8A90DFE601316F7368A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate dance terminology to describe and analyze their own work

233EFF60DFE601316F7168A86D17958E.description: Understand the purpose of the rehearsal process in refining and revising work leading to a finished performance

233EB7C0DFE601316F7068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate increased ability to work effectively alone, and to cooperate with a partner or in an ensemble

233E6D00DFE601316F6F68A86D17958E.description: Create or learn and perform a dance for invited guests or peers based on one of the following: a ritual from another culture; a traditional dance; work with a partner, group, or single choreographer. Identify and explain the circumstances and settings in which the dance would be performed

233E0FB0DFE601316F6E68A86D17958E.description: Improvise dances that range from free-form to structured studies; realize the potential of improvisation as a tool for the enrichment of individual and group expression

233D5B70DFE601316F6C68A86D17958E.description: Perform dances confidently, communicating the intention of the choreographer and the style of the dance

233D1610DFE601316F6B68A86D17958E.description: Perform a movement piece that communicates a topic of personal, social, or artistic significance and explain the movement choices

233CCF90DFE601316F6A68A86D17958E.description: Observe and explain how different accompaniment (music, abstract sounds, spoken text, lighting, and costuming) can affect and /or contribute to the meaning of a dance

233C8170DFE601316F6968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and articulate the difference between pantomime and gesture in dance; use gesture as a tool to enhance the expressive nature of movement

233ACA70DFE601316F6368A86D17958E.description: Record dances and choreography using pictorial symbols or other forms of notation

233A6F30DFE601316F6268A86D17958E.description: Describe and analyze, orally and in writing, the choreographic structure of variety of dances, using appropriate dance vocabulary

233A2750DFE601316F6168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the following partner skills in creating contrasting and complementary shapes: taking and supporting weight, countertension, and counterbalance

233BF3F0DFE601316F6768A86D17958E.description: Use scientific and/or mathematical concepts to create movement phrases

233BAE20DFE601316F6668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate compositional forms in short choreographed phrases, using AB, ABA, theme-variations, canon, rondos, story-telling, and narration

233B66A0DFE601316F6568A86D17958E.description: Create sequences and simple dances that demonstrate principles of unison, contrast, repetition, climax, abstraction, reordering, and chance

233B1A80DFE601316F6468A86D17958E.description: Use improvisation to generate movement for choreography

233996B0DFE601316F5F68A86D17958E.description: Continue to develop a positive body image

23393EE0DFE601316F5E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the movement styles of classical, theatrical, or traditional dance (such as ballet, modern, jazz, folk, and social dances) using appropriate dance vocabulary

2338E100DFE601316F5D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate increasing accuracy in memorizing and reproducing more complex movement phrases from a variety of traditional and contemporary dances

23388170DFE601316F5C68A86D17958E.description: Explore increasingly complex combinations of locomotor and non-locomotor movements that emphasize the elements of space, time, and force

23382B70DFE601316F5B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ability to move to changing rhythms, melodies, and non-musical sounds

2337C850DFE601316F5A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of alignment, articulation of body parts, initiation of movement, weight shift and balance, elevation and landing, and fall and recovery

document.title: Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework

27825BB0DFE6013176AC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the spread and influence of the Roman alphabet and the Latin language, the use of Latin as the language of education for more than 1,000 years, and the role of Latin and Greek in scientific and academic vocabulary. (H)

278213A0DFE6013176AB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the contribution of Roman civilization to law, literature, poetry, architecture, engineering, and technology (e.g., roads, bridges, arenas, baths, aqueducts, central heating, plumbing, and sanitation). (H)

2781BAA0DFE6013176AA68A86D17958E.description: Explain how inner forces (including the rise of autonomous military powers, political corruption, and economic and political instability) and external forces (shrinking trade, attacks, and invasions) led to the disintegration of the Roman Empire. (H, E)

27816B30DFE6013176A968A86D17958E.description:
Describe the origins of Christianity and its central features. (H)
  1. monotheism
  2. the belief in Jesus as the Messiah and God's son who redeemed humans from sin
  3. the concept of salvation
  4. belief in the Old and New Testament
  5. the lives and teachings of Jesus and Saint Paul
  6. the relationship of early Christians to officials of the Roman Empire

27811FF0DFE6013176A868A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics of slavery under the Romans. (H)

2780DAC0DFE6013176A768A86D17958E.description:
Describe the influence of Julius Caesar and Augustus in Rome's transition from a republic to an empire and explain the reasons for the growth and long life of the Roman Empire. (H, E)
  1. Military organization, tactics, and conquests; and decentralized administration
  2. the purpose and functions of taxes
  3. the promotion of economic growth through the use of a standard currency, road construction, and the protection of trade routes
  4. the benefits of a Pax Romana

27808960DFE6013176A668A86D17958E.description: Describe the government of the Roman Republic and its contribution to the development of democratic principles, including separation of powers, rule of law, representative government, and the notion of civic duty. (H, C)

277FEF60DFE6013176A468A86D17958E.description:
Explain the rise of the Roman Republic and the role of mythical and historical figures in Roman history. (H)
  1. Romulus and Remus
  2. Hannibal and the Carthaginian Wars
  3. Cicero
  4. Julius Caesar and Augustus
  5. Hadrian

27803900DFE6013176A568A86D17958E.description: Explain how the geographical location of ancient Rome contributed to the shaping of Roman society and the expansion of its political power in the Mediterranean region and beyond. (H, G, E)

277FACD0DFE6013176A368A86D17958E.description: On a historical map, identify ancient Rome and trace the extent of the Roman Empire to 500 AD/CE. (H, G)

277F69A0DFE6013176A268A86D17958E.description: The Roots of Western Civilization: Ancient Rome, c. 500 BC/BCE-500 AD/CE

277F2100DFE6013176A168A86D17958E.description:
Describe the purposes and functions of the lyceum, the gymnasium, and the Library of Alexandria, and identify the major accomplishments of the ancient Greeks. (H)
  1. Thales (science)
  2. Pythagoras and Euclid (mathematics)
  3. Hippocrates (medicine)
  4. Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle (philosophy)
  5. Herodotus, Thucydides, Homer, Aeschylus, Sophocles, Aristophanes, and Euripides (history, poetry, and drama)
  6. the Parthenon, the Acropolis, and the Temple of Apollo (architecture)
  7. the development of the first complete alphabet with symbols for consonants and vowels

277EC8A0DFE6013176A068A86D17958E.description: Explain why the city-states of Greece instituted a tradition of athletic competitions and describe the kinds of sports they featured. (H)

277E5E90DFE60131769F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the myths and stories of classical Greece; give examples of Greek gods and goddesses, heroes, and events, and where and how we see their names used today. (H)

277E11E0DFE60131769E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the rise of Alexander the Great and the spread of Greek culture. (H)

277DD180DFE60131769D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the causes, course, and consequences of the Peloponnesian Wars between Athens and Sparta. (H)

277D8ED0DFE60131769C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the causes, course, and consequences of the Persian Wars, including the origins of marathons. (H)

277D48C0DFE60131769B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the status of women and the functions of slaves in ancient Athens. (H)

277CFD00DFE60131769A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast life in Athens and Sparta. (H)

277CB540DFE60131769968A86D17958E.description:
Explain why the government of ancient Athens is considered the beginning of democracy and explain the democratic political concepts developed in ancient Greece. (H, C)
  1. the "polis" or city-state
  2. civic participation and voting rights
  3. legislative bodies
  4. constitution writing
  5. rule of law

277C6BB0DFE60131769868A86D17958E.description: Explain how the geographical location of ancient Athens and other city-states contributed to their role in maritime trade, their colonies in the Mediterranean, and the expansion of their cultural influence. (H, G, E)

277C23A0DFE60131769768A86D17958E.description: On a historical map of the Mediterranean area, locate Greece and trace the extent of its influence to 300 BC/BCE. On a modern map of the Mediterranean area, Europe, England, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent, locate England, France, Greece, Italy, Spain, and other countries in the Balkan peninsula, Crete, Egypt, India, the Middle East, Pakistan, and Turkey. (H, G)

277BDFE0DFE60131769668A86D17958E.description: The Roots of Western Civilization: Ancient Greece, c. 800-300 BC/BCE

277B9700DFE60131769568A86D17958E.description: Explain the expulsion/dispersion of the Jews to other lands (referred to as the Diaspora) after the destruction of the second temple in Jerusalem in 70 AD/CE, and the renaming of the country by the Romans. (H)

277B49F0DFE60131769468A86D17958E.description: Describe the unification of the tribes of Israel under Kings Saul, David, and Solomon, including David's founding of Jerusalem as his capital city in 1000 BC/BCE and the building of the first temple by Solomon. (H)

277B0560DFE60131769368A86D17958E.description:
Describe the monotheistic religion of the Israelites. (H)
  1. the belief that there is one God
  2. the Ten Commandments
  3. the emphasis on individual worth and personal responsibility
  4. the belief that all people must adhere to the same moral obligations, whether ruler or ruled
  5. the Hebrew Bible (Old Testament) as part of the history of early Israel.

277ABE50DFE60131769268A86D17958E.description: Identify the ancient Israelites, or Hebrews, and trace their migrations from Mesopotamia to the land called Canaan, and explain the role of Abraham and Moses in their history. (H, G)

277A7590DFE60131769168A86D17958E.description: On a historical map of the Mediterranean, locate Asia Minor, Greece and Mesopotamia, the kingdoms of the Hittites and ancient Israel, and Egypt. On a modern map, locate Egypt, Greece, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, the area governed by the Palestinian Authority, Syria, and Turkey. (G)

277A26A0DFE60131769068A86D17958E.description: The Roots of Western Civilization: Ancient Israel, c. 2000 BC/BCE-70 AD/CE

2779CDB0DFE60131768F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the Phoenicians as the successors to the Minoans in dominating maritime trade in the Mediterranean from c. 1000-300 BC/BCE. Describe how the Phoenician writing system was the first alphabet (with 22 symbols for consonants) and the precursor of the first complete alphabet developed by the ancient Greeks (with symbols representing both consonants and vowels). (H, E)

27797AD0DFE60131768E68A86D17958E.description: On a map of the ancient Mediterranean world, locate Greece, Asia Minor, Crete, Phoenicia, the Aegean, and the Red Sea. On a modern map, locate Greece, Crete, Turkey, Lebanon, and Syria. (G)

2778C7B0DFE60131768C68A86D17958E.description:
Summarize important achievements of Egyptian civilization. (H)
  1. the agricultural system
  2. the invention of a calendar
  3. monumental architecture and art such as the Pyramids and Sphinx at Giza
  4. hieroglyphic writing
  5. the invention of papyrus

27786650DFE60131768B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the polytheistic religion of ancient Egypt with respect to beliefs about death, the afterlife, mummification, and the roles of different deities. (H)

27781EA0DFE60131768A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of the pharaoh as god/king, the concept of dynasties, the importance of at least one Egyptian ruler, the relationship of pharaohs to peasants, and the role of slaves in ancient Egypt. (H, C)

2777D3E0DFE60131768968A86D17958E.description: Describe the kinds of evidence that have been used by archaeologists and historians to draw conclusions about the social and economic characteristics of Ancient Nubia (the Kingdom of Kush) and their relationship to the social and economic characteristics of Ancient Egypt. (H, G)

27778EF0DFE60131768868A86D17958E.description: On a historical map of the Mediterranean region, locate the Mediterranean and Red Seas, the Nile River and Delta, and the areas of ancient Nubia and Egypt. Identify the locations of ancient Upper and Lower Egypt and explain what the terms mean. On a modern map, identify the modern countries of Egypt and Sudan. (G)

27774BE0DFE60131768768A86D17958E.description: Egypt: An Ancient River Civilization, c. 3000-1200 BC/BCE

277707D0DFE60131768668A86D17958E.description: Describe who Hammurabi was and explain the basic principle of justice in Hammurabi's Code ("an eye for an eye"). (H, C, E)

2776C4B0DFE60131768568A86D17958E.description:
Describe the important achievements of Mesopotamian civilization. (H, C, E)
  1. its system of writing (and its importance in record keeping and tax collection)
  2. monumental architecture (the ziggurat)
  3. art (large relief sculpture, mosaics, and cylinder seals)

27767BF0DFE60131768468A86D17958E.description: Describe how irrigation, metalsmithing, slavery, the domestication of animals, and inventions such as the wheel, the sail, and the plow contributed to the growth of Mesopotamian civilizations. (H, E)

277628F0DFE60131768368A86D17958E.description: Identify polytheism (the belief that there are many gods) as the religious belief of the people in Mesopotamian civilizations. (H)

2775E2B0DFE60131768268A86D17958E.description: On a historical map, locate the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers and identify Sumer, Babylon, and Assyria as successive civilizations and empires in this region, and explain why the region is sometimes called "the Fertile Crescent." On a modern map of western Asia, identify the modern countries in the region (Iraq, Iran, and Turkey). (H, G, E)

2775A2E0DFE60131768168A86D17958E.description: Mesopotamia: Site of Several Ancient River Civilizations, c. 3500-1200 BC/BCE

27755DC0DFE60131768068A86D17958E.description:
Identify the characteristics of civilizations. (H, G, E)
  1. the presence of geographic boundaries and political institutions
  2. an economy that produces food surpluses
  3. a concentration of population in distinct areas or cities
  4. the existence of social classes
  5. developed systems of religion, learning, art, and architecture
  6. a system of record keeping

27750EC0DFE60131767F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the invention of agriculture related to settlement, population growth, and the emergence of civilization. (H)

2774BEE0DFE60131767E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of the invention of metallurgy and agriculture (the growing of crops and the domestication of animals). (H)

27746E80DFE60131767D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics of the hunter-gatherer societies of the Paleolithic Age (their use of tools and fire, basic hunting weapons, beads and other jewelry). (H)

27742F80DFE60131767C68A86D17958E.description: Identify sites in Africa where archaeologists have found evidence of the origins of modern human beings and describe what the archaeologists found. (G, H)

2773EED0DFE60131767B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the great climatic and environmental changes that shaped the earth and eventually permitted the growth of human life. (H)

2773AC60DFE60131767A68A86D17958E.description: Human Origins in Africa through the Neolithic Age

2772FD00DFE60131767868A86D17958E.description: Define and apply economic concepts learned in prekindergarten through grade 6: producers, consumers, goods, services, buyers, sellers, natural resources, taxes, specialization, savings, entrepreneur, prices, markets, scarcity, trade, barter, money, medium of exchange, supply, and demand. (E)

27726050DFE60131767668A86D17958E.description: Define and use correctly words and terms relating to government such as city-state, dynasty, kingdom, empire, republic, separation of powers, civic duty, rule of law, and military. (C)

2771DD00DFE60131767468A86D17958E.description: Describe ways of interpreting archaeological evidence from societies leaving no written records. (H)

277195B0DFE60131767368A86D17958E.description: Identify multiple causes and effects when explaining historical events. (H)

27713970DFE60131767268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between primary and secondary sources and describe how each kind of source is used in interpreting history. (H)

2770ECE0DFE60131767168A86D17958E.description: Construct and interpret timelines of events and civilizations studied. (H)

2770A8E0DFE60131767068A86D17958E.description: Use correctly the words or abbreviations for identifying time periods or dates in historical narratives (decade, age, era, century, millennium, AD/CE, BC/BCE, c., and circa). Identify in BC/BCE dates the higher number as indicating the older year (that is, 3000 BC/BCE is earlier than 2000 BC/BCE) (H)

277063E0DFE60131766F68A86D17958E.description: Compare information shown on modern and historical maps of the same region. (G)

276F85C0DFE60131766C68A86D17958E.description: Ancient and Classical Civilizations in the Mediterranean to the Fall of the Roman Empire: Ideas that Shaped History

document.title: Massachusetts Science and Technology/Engineering Curriculum Framework

21F12CC0DFE601316CD968A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain adaptive and assistive bioengineered products, e.g., food, bio-fuels, irradiation, integrated pest management.

21F0E4F0DFE601316CD868A86D17958E.description: Explain examples of adaptive or assistive devices, e.g., prosthetic devices, wheelchairs, eyeglasses, grab bars, hearing aids, lifts, braces.

21F04250DFE601316CD668A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain lift, drag, friction, thrust, and gravity in a vehicle or device, e.g., cars, boats, airplanes, rockets.

21EFFEB0DFE601316CD568A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe three subsystems of a transportation vehicle or device, i.e., structural, propulsion, guidance, suspension, control, and support.

21EFB980DFE601316CD468A86D17958E.description: Given a transportation problem, explain a possible solution using the universal systems model.

21EF7160DFE601316CD368A86D17958E.description: Identify and compare examples of transportation systems and devices that operate on or in each of the following: land, air, water, and space.

21EED480DFE601316CD168A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the effects of loads and structural shapes on bridges.

21EE7D80DFE601316CD068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the forces of tension, compression, torsion, bending, and shear affect the performance of bridges.

21EE3720DFE601316CCF68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe three major types of bridges (e.g., arch, beam, and suspension) and their appropriate uses (e.g., site, span, resources, and load).

21EDE040DFE601316CCE68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain parts of a structure, e.g., foundation, flooring, decking, wall, roofing systems.

21ED5100DFE601316CCC68A86D17958E.description: Explain basic processes in manufacturing systems, e.g., cutting, shaping, assembling, joining, finishing, quality control, and safety.

21ED0630DFE601316CCB68A86D17958E.description: Describe a manufacturing organization, e.g., corporate structure, research and development, production, marketing, quality control, distribution.

21ECADF0DFE601316CCA68A86D17958E.description: Explain and give examples of the impacts of interchangeable parts, components of mass-produced products, and the use of automation, e.g., robotics.

21EC65E0DFE601316CC968A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the manufacturing systems of custom and mass production.

21EBD850DFE601316CC768A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain how symbols and icons (e.g., international symbols and graphics) are used to communicate a message.

21EB9040DFE601316CC668A86D17958E.description: Identify and compare communication technologies and systems, i.e., audio, visual, printed, and mass communication.

21EB3B70DFE601316CC568A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the appropriate tools, machines, and electronic devices (e.g., drawing tools, computer-aided design, and cameras) used to produce and/or reproduce design solutions (e.g., engineering drawings, prototypes, and reports).

21EAE540DFE601316CC468A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the components of a communication system, i.e., source, encoder, transmitter, receiver, decoder, storage, retrieval, and destination.

21E80100DFE601316CBB68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the safe and proper use of measuring tools, hand tools, and machines (e.g., band saw, drill press, sander, hammer, screwdriver, pliers, tape measure, screws, nails, and other mechanical fasteners) needed to construct a prototype of an engineering design.

21E7B740DFE601316CBA68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain appropriate measuring tools, hand tools, and power tools used to hold, lift, carry, fasten, and separate, and explain their safe and proper use.

21E76100DFE601316CB968A86D17958E.description: Given a design task, identify appropriate materials (e.g., wood, paper, plastic, aggregates, ceramics, metals, solvents, adhesives) based on specific properties and characteristics (e.g., strength, hardness, and flexibility).

21EA3AA0DFE601316CC268A86D17958E.description: Identify the five elements of a universal systems model: goal, inputs, processes, outputs, and feedback.

21E9EDD0DFE601316CC168A86D17958E.description: Explain how such design features as size, shape, weight, function, and cost limitations would affect the construction of a given prototype.

21E99F90DFE601316CC068A86D17958E.description: Identify appropriate materials, tools, and machines needed to construct a prototype of a given engineering design.

21E92800DFE601316CBF68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the purpose of a given prototype.

21E8CF40DFE601316CBE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate methods of representing solutions to a design problem, e.g., sketches, orthographic projections, multiview drawings.

21E88B40DFE601316CBD68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the steps of the engineering design process, i.e., identify the need or problem, research the problem, develop possible solutions, select the best possible solution(s), construct a prototype, test and evaluate, communicate the solution(s), and redesign.

21F83780DFE601316CEF68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how heat moves in predictable ways, moving from warmer objects to cooler ones until they reach equilibrium.

21F7EB70DFE601316CEE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effect of heat on particle motion through a description of what happens to particles during a change in phase.

21F78D30DFE601316CED68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that heat is a form of energy and that temperature change results from adding or taking away heat from a system.

21F6E8C0DFE601316CEB68A86D17958E.description: Graph and interpret distance vs. time graphs for constant speed.

21F6A040DFE601316CEA68A86D17958E.description: Explain and give examples of how the motion of an object can be described by its position, direction of motion, and speed.

21F44840DFE601316CE368A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between physical changes and chemical changes.

21F61440DFE601316CE868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that a substance (element or compound) has a melting point and a boiling point, both of which are independent of the amount of the sample.

21F5BDD0DFE601316CE768A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between mixtures and pure substances.

21F567E0DFE601316CE668A86D17958E.description: Give basic examples of elements and compounds.

21F51A30DFE601316CE568A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between an atom (the smallest unit of an element that maintains the characteristics of that element) and a molecule (the smallest unit of a compound that maintains the characteristics of that compound).

21F4AF10DFE601316CE468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there are more than 100 elements that combine in a multitude of ways to produce compounds that make up all of the living and nonliving things that we encounter.

21F3AB30DFE601316CE168A86D17958E.description: Explain and give examples of how mass is conserved in a closed system.

21F36010DFE601316CE068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the measurement of volume and mass requires understanding of the sensitivity of measurement tools (e.g., rulers, graduated cylinders, balances) and knowledge and appropriate use of significant digits.

21F31960DFE601316CDF68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between volume and mass. Define density.

21F2D3C0DFE601316CDE68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between weight and mass, recognizing that weight is the amount of gravitational pull on an object.

21F22390DFE601316CDC68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between potential and kinetic energy. Identify situations where kinetic energy is transformed into potential energy and vice versa.

21E68B90DFE601316CB668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that biological evolution accounts for the diversity of species developed through gradual processes over many generations.

21E634F0DFE601316CB568A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which ecosystems have changed throughout geologic time in response to physical conditions, interactions among organisms, and the actions of humans. Describe how changes may be catastrophes such as volcanic eruptions or ice storms.

21E57590DFE601316CB368A86D17958E.description: Compare sexual reproduction (offspring inherit half of their genes from each parent) with asexual reproduction (offspring is an identical copy of the parent's cell).

21E52160DFE601316CB268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that hereditary information is contained in genes located in the chromosomes of each cell. A human cell contains about 30,000 different genes on 23 different chromosomes.

21E4D3E0DFE601316CB168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that every organism requires a set of instructions that specifies its traits. These instructions are stored in the organism's chromosomes. Heredity is the passage of these instructions from one generation to another.

21E44250DFE601316CAF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the general functions of the major systems of the human body (digestion, respiration, reproduction, circulation, excretion, protection from disease, and movement, control, and coordination) and describe ways that these systems interact with each other.

21E3F440DFE601316CAE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the hierarchical organization of multicellular organisms from cells to tissues to organs to systems to organisms.

21E35450DFE601316CAC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that within cells, many of the basic functions of organisms (e.g., extracting energy from food and getting rid of waste) are carried out. The way in which cells function is similar in all living organisms.

21E31020DFE601316CAB68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast plant and animal cells, including major organelles (cell membrane, cell wall, nucleus, cytoplasm, chloroplasts, mitochondria, vacuoles).

21E2CBB0DFE601316CAA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that all organisms are composed of cells, and that many organisms are single-celled (unicellular), e.g., bacteria, yeast. In these single-celled organisms, one cell must carry out all of the basic functions of life.

21E232E0DFE601316CA868A86D17958E.description: Classify organisms into the currently recognized kingdoms according to characteristics that they share. Be familiar with organisms from each kingdom.

21E19B60DFE601316CA668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that producers (plants that contain chlorophyll) use the energy from sunlight to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water through a process called photosynthesis. This food can be used immediately, stored for later use, or used by other organisms.

21E15430DFE601316CA568A86D17958E.description: Explain how dead plants and animals are broken down by other living organisms and how this process contributes to the system as a whole.

21E10D70DFE601316CA468A86D17958E.description: Explain the roles and relationships among producers, consumers, and decomposers in the process of energy transfer in a food web.

21E06E70DFE601316CA268A86D17958E.description: Give examples of ways in which organisms interact and have different functions within an ecosystem that enable the ecosystem to survive.

21DFC390DFE601316CA068A86D17958E.description: Relate the extinction of species to a mismatch of adaptation and the environment.

21DF7DF0DFE601316C9F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that evidence drawn from geology, fossils, and comparative anatomy provides the basis of the theory of evolution.

21DF35C0DFE601316C9E68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of ways in which genetic variation and environmental factors are causes of evolution and the diversity of organisms.

21DE4C00DFE601316C9B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship among the energy provided by the sun, the global patterns of atmospheric movement, and the temperature differences among water, land, and atmosphere.

21DDFA10DFE601316C9A68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate among radiation, conduction, and convection, the three mechanisms by which heat is transferred through the earth's system.

21DD9F50DFE601316C9968A86D17958E.description: Heat Transfer in the Earth System

21DD5600DFE601316C9868A86D17958E.description: Describe the layers of the earth, including the lithosphere, the hot convecting mantle, and the dense metallic core.

21DCBEB0DFE601316C9668A86D17958E.description: Recognize, interpret, and be able to create models of the earth's common physical features in various mapping representations, including contour maps.

21DB9860DFE601316C9268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the universe contains many billions of galaxies, and that each galaxy contains many billions of stars.

21DB50D0DFE601316C9168A86D17958E.description: Explain how the tilt of the earth and its revolution around the sun result in an uneven heating of the earth, which in turn causes the seasons.

21DB02C0DFE601316C9068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast properties and conditions of objects in the solar system (i.e., sun, planets, and moons) to those on Earth (i.e., gravitational force, distance from the sun, speed, movement, temperature, and atmospheric conditions).

21DC2920DFE601316C9468A86D17958E.description: Describe lunar and solar eclipses, the observed moon phases, and tides. Relate them to the relative positions of the earth, moon, and sun.

21DBE220DFE601316C9368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that gravity is a force that pulls all things on and near the earth toward the center of the earth. Gravity plays a major role in the formation of the planets, stars, and solar system and in determining their motions.

21DAA8F0DFE601316C8F68A86D17958E.description: The Earth in the Solar System

21DA5EB0DFE601316C8E68A86D17958E.description: Explain and give examples of how physical evidence, such as fossils and surface features of glaciation, supports theories that the earth has evolved over geologic time.

21DA12D0DFE601316C8D68A86D17958E.description: Describe and give examples of ways in which the earth's surface is built up and torn down by natural processes, including deposition of sediments, rock formation, erosion, and weathering.

21D9C290DFE601316C8C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the movement of the earth's crustal plates causes both slow changes in the earth's surface (e.g., formation of mountains and ocean basins) and rapid ones (e.g., volcanic eruptions and earthquakes).

document.title: Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework

28CA21A0DFE60131779268A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the course and consequences of America's recent diplomatic initiatives.(H, C)
  1. the invasion of Panama and the Persian Gulf War
  2. American intervention in Somalia, Haiti, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Kosovo
  3. the attempts to negotiate a settlement to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict
  4. America's response to the September 11, 2001, terrorist attack on the World Trade Center in New York City and on the Pentagon in Washington, D.C.

28C9CA30DFE60131779168A86D17958E.description:
Explain the importance of the 2000 presidential election. (H, C)
  1. the Supreme Court case, Bush v. Gore
  2. the growing influence of the Republican Party in the South and the consolidation of the Democratic Party's hold on the coasts

28C96870DFE60131779068A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the important domestic policies and events of the Clinton presidency. (H, E)
  1. the passage of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) in 1993
  2. President Clinton's welfare reform legislation and expansion of the earned income tax credit
  3. the first balanced budget in more than 25 years
  4. the election in 1994 of the first Republican majority in both the House and Senate in 40 years
  5. tax credits for higher education
  6. the causes and consequences of the impeachment of President Clinton in 1998

28C91880DFE60131778F68A86D17958E.description:
Describe some of the major economic and social trends of the late 20th century. (H, E)
  1. the computer and technological revolution of the 1980s and 1990s
  2. scientific and medical discoveries
  3. major immigration and demographic changes such as the rise in Asian and Hispanic immigration (both legal and illegal)
  4. the weakening of the nuclear family and the rise in divorce rates

28C8C3E0DFE60131778E68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the presidency of Ronald Reagan. (H, E)
  1. tax rate cuts
  2. anticommunist foreign and defense policies
  3. Supreme Court appointments
  4. the revitalization of the conservative movement during Reagan's tenure as President
  5. the replacement of striking air traffic controllers with non-union personnel

28C7FE40DFE60131778C68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the important domestic policies and events that took place during the presidencies of Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, and Nixon. (H)
  1. the space exploration program
  2. the assassination of President Kennedy
  3. Johnson's Great Society programs
  4. Nixon's appeal to "the silent majority"
  5. the anti-war and counter-cultural movements
  6. the creation of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 1970

21BEB360DFE601316C7268A86D17958E.description: Describe different ways in which a problem can be represented, e.g., sketches, diagrams, graphic organizers, and lists.

21BE73C0DFE601316C7168A86D17958E.description: Identify a problem that reflects the need for shelter, storage, or convenience.

21BDF060DFE601316C6F68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the difference between simple and complex machines, e.g., hand can opener that includes multiple gears, wheel, wedge, gear, and lever.

21BDAD10DFE601316C6E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the appropriate materials and tools (e.g., hammer, screwdriver, pliers, tape measure, screws, nails, and other mechanical fasteners) to construct a given prototype safely.

21BD66F0DFE601316C6D68A86D17958E.description: Identify materials used to accomplish a design task based on a specific property, e.g., strength, hardness, and flexibility.

21C56940DFE601316C8868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that light travels in a straight line until it strikes an object or travels from one medium to another, and that light can be reflected, refracted, and absorbed.

21C4E4B0DFE601316C8668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that sound is produced by vibrating objects and requires a medium through which to travel. Relate the rate of vibration to the pitch of the sound.

21C3DF80DFE601316C8368A86D17958E.description: Identify and classify objects and materials that a magnet will attract and objects and materials that a magnet will not attract.

21C42FA0DFE601316C8468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that magnets have poles that repel and attract each other.

21C353F0DFE601316C8168A86D17958E.description: Explain how electromagnets can be made, and give examples of how they can be used.

21C30AA0DFE601316C8068A86D17958E.description: Identify and classify objects and materials that conduct electricity and objects and materials that are insulators of electricity.

21C2A790DFE601316C7F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that electricity in circuits requires a complete loop through which an electrical current can pass, and that electricity can produce light, heat, and sound.

21C1F610DFE601316C7D68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how energy can be transferred from one form to another.

21C1AFC0DFE601316C7C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the basic forms of energy (light, sound, heat, electrical, and magnetic). Recognize that energy is the ability to cause motion or create change.

21C11D40DFE601316C7A68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between properties of objects (e.g., size, shape, weight) and properties of materials (e.g., color, texture, hardness).

21C08320DFE601316C7868A86D17958E.description: Describe how water can be changed from one state to another by adding or taking away heat.

21C03B70DFE601316C7768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast solids, liquids, and gases based on the basic properties of each of these states of matter.

21BC4FA0DFE601316C6A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how energy derived from the sun is used by plants to produce sugars (photosynthesis) and is transferred within a food chain from producers (plants) to consumers to decomposers.

21BAA8A0DFE601316C6468A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how organisms can cause changes in their environment to ensure survival. Explain how some of these changes may affect the ecosystem.

21BBC6B0DFE601316C6868A86D17958E.description: Recognize plant behaviors, such as the way seedlings' stems grow toward light and their roots grow downward in response to gravity. Recognize that many plants and animals can survive harsh environments because of seasonal behaviors, e.g., in winter, some trees shed leaves, some animals hibernate, and other animals migrate.

21BB8280DFE601316C6768A86D17958E.description: Describe how organisms meet some of their needs in an environment by using behaviors (patterns of activities) in response to information (stimuli) received from the environment. Recognize that some animal behaviors are instinctive (e.g., turtles burying their eggs), and others are learned (e.g., humans building fires for warmth, chimpanzees learning how to use tools).

21BB3600DFE601316C6668A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how changes in the environment (drought, cold) have caused some plants and animals to die or move to new locations (migration).

21BAE8A0DFE601316C6568A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how inherited characteristics may change over time as adaptations to changes in the environment that enable organisms to survive, e.g., shape of beak or feet, placement of eyes on head, length of neck, shape of teeth, color.

21BA25E0DFE601316C6268A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between observed characteristics of plants and animals that are fully inherited (e.g., color of flower, shape of leaves, color of eyes, number of appendages) and characteristics that are affected by the climate or environment (e.g., browning of leaves due to too much sun, language spoken).

21B9E0F0DFE601316C6168A86D17958E.description: Describe the major stages that characterize the life cycle of the frog and butterfly as they go through metamorphosis.

21B999A0DFE601316C6068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that plants and animals go through predictable life cycles that include birth, growth, development, reproduction, and death.

21B95090DFE601316C5F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the structures in plants (leaves, roots, flowers, stem, bark, wood) that are responsible for food production, support, water transport, reproduction, growth, and protection.

21B8BA60DFE601316C5D68A86D17958E.description: Classify plants and animals according to the physical characteristics that they share.

21B7DC50DFE601316C5A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the changes that occur in the observable shape of the moon over the course of a month.

21B78990DFE601316C5968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the earth revolves around (orbits) the sun in a year's time and that the earth rotates on its axis once approximately every 24 hours. Make connections between the rotation of the earth and day/night, and the apparent movement of the sun, moon, and stars across the sky.

21B71BB0DFE601316C5868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the earth is part of a system called the "solar system" that includes the sun (a star), planets, and many moons. The earth is the third planet from the sun in our solar system.

21B6B280DFE601316C5768A86D17958E.description: The Earth in the Solar System

21B64D00DFE601316C5668A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how the surface of the earth changes due to slow processes such as erosion and weathering, and rapid processes such as landslides, volcanic eruptions, and earthquakes.

21B5CC80DFE601316C5468A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how the cycling of water, both in and out of the atmosphere, has an effect on climate.

21B58910DFE601316C5368A86D17958E.description: Describe how water on earth cycles in different forms and in different locations, including underground and in the atmosphere.

21B4B530DFE601316C5068A86D17958E.description: Describe how global patterns such as the jet stream and water currents influence local weather in measurable terms such as temperature, wind direction and speed, and precipitation.

21B475A0DFE601316C4F68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the various forms of precipitation (rain, snow, sleet, and hail), making connections to the weather in a particular place and time.

21B43570DFE601316C4E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how air temperature, moisture, wind speed and direction, and precipitation make up the weather in a particular place and time.

21B3B1C0DFE601316C4C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and discuss the different properties of soil, including color, texture (size of particles), the ability to retain water, and the ability to support the growth of plants.

21B35D60DFE601316C4B68A86D17958E.description: Explain and give examples of the ways in which soil is formed (the weathering of rock by water and wind and from the decomposition of plant and animal remains).

21B2DA00DFE601316C4968A86D17958E.description: Identify the three categories of rocks (metamorphic, igneous, and sedimentary) based on how they are formed, and explain the natural and physical processes that create these rocks.

21B29380DFE601316C4868A86D17958E.description: Identify the physical properties of minerals (hardness, color, luster, cleavage, and streak), and explain how minerals can be tested for these different physical properties.

21B24F80DFE601316C4768A86D17958E.description: Give a simple explanation of what a mineral is and some examples, e.g., quartz, mica.

26CB37B0DFE60131756968A86D17958E.description: After reading or listening to a variety of true stories about individuals recognized for their achievements, describe and compare different ways people have achieved great distinction (e.g. scientific, professional, political, religious, commercial, military, athletic, or artistic). (H)

26CAF700DFE60131756868A86D17958E.description: With the help of the school librarian, identify and describe well-known sites, events, or landmarks in at least three different countries from which students' families come and explain why they are important. (H, G, C)

26CAB260DFE60131756768A86D17958E.description: With the help of the school librarian, give examples of traditions or customs from other countries that can be found in America today. (G, C)

26CA6330DFE60131756668A86D17958E.description: On a map of the world, locate the continent, regions, or countries from which students, their parents, guardians, grandparents, or other relatives or ancestors came. With the help of family members and the school librarian, describe traditional food, customs, sports and games, and music of the place they came from. (G, C)

26CA0C50DFE60131756568A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between a continent and a country and give examples of each. (G)

26C99130DFE60131756468A86D17958E.description: Locate major mountains or mountain ranges in the world such as the Andes, Alps, Himalayas, Mt. Everest, Mt. McKinley, and the Rocky Mountains. (G)

26C901E0DFE60131756268A86D17958E.description: Locate the oceans of the world: the Arctic, Atlantic, Indian, Pacific, and Southern Oceans. (G)

26C8C110DFE60131756168A86D17958E.description: Locate the current boundaries of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. (G)

26C87DF0DFE60131756068A86D17958E.description: On a map of the world, locate all of the continents: North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia, and Antarctica. (G)

26C7E3F0DFE60131755E68A86D17958E.description: Explain what buyers and sellers are and give examples of goods and services that are bought and sold in their community. (E)

26C786D0DFE60131755D68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of people in the school and community who are both producers and consumers. (E)

26C71020DFE60131755B68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of fictional characters or real people in the school or community who were good leaders and good citizens, and explain the qualities that made them admirable (e.g., honesty, dependability, modesty, trustworthiness, courage). (C)

26C6D4C0DFE60131755A68A86D17958E.description: Define and give examples of some of the rights and responsibilities that students as citizens have in the school (e.g., students have the right to vote in a class election and have the responsibility to follow school rules). (C)

26C65B50DFE60131755868A86D17958E.description: Read globes and maps and follow narrative accounts using them. (G, H)

26C616E0DFE60131755768A86D17958E.description: Describe how maps and globes depict geographical information in different ways. (G)

26C5CDC0DFE60131755668A86D17958E.description: Explain the information that historical timelines convey and then put in chronological order events in the student's life (e.g., the year he or she was born, started school, or moved to a new neighborhood) or in the history of countries studied. (H)

26C58F10DFE60131755568A86D17958E.description: Use correctly words and phrases related to time (now, in the past, in the future), changing historical periods (other times, other places), and causation (because, reasons). (H)

26C55090DFE60131755468A86D17958E.description: Use a calendar to identify days, weeks, months, years, and seasons. (H)

document.title: Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework

272A9090DFE6013175FA68A86D17958E.description:
Identify the key issues that contributed to the onset of the Civil War. (H, E)
  1. the debate over slavery and westward expansion
  2. diverging economic interests

272A4DF0DFE6013175F968A86D17958E.description:
Explain the reasons that pioneer moved west from the beginning to the middle of the 19th century, and describe their lives on the frontier. (H, G, C, E)
  1. wagon train journeys on the Oregon and Santa Fe Trails
  2. their settlements in the western territories

272A0B60DFE6013175F868A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of the China trade and the whaling industry to 19th century New England, and give examples of imports from China. (H)

2729C510DFE6013175F768A86D17958E.description:
Describe the causes of the war of 1812 and how events during the war contributed to a sense of American nationalism. (H)
  1. British restrictions on trade and impressment
  2. Major battles and events of the war, including the role of the USS Constitution, the burning of the Capitol and the White House, and the Battle of New Orleans

272980E0DFE6013175F668A86D17958E.description: Describe the significance and consequences of the abolition of slavery in the northern states after the Revolution and of the 1808 law that banned the importation of slaves into the United States. (H)

27293DE0DFE6013175F568A86D17958E.description: Describe the expedition of Lewis and Clark from 1803 to 1806. (H, E, G)

2728EBC0DFE6013175F468A86D17958E.description: Explain the events leading up to, and the significance of, the Louisiana Purchase of 1803. (H, C, E, G)

2728AB60DFE6013175F368A86D17958E.description: Identify the changes in voting qualifications between 1787 and 1820 (e.g., the abolition of property requirements), and compare who could vote in local, state, and national elections in the U.S. with who could vote in England, France, and Russia. (H, C)

27282720DFE6013175F168A86D17958E.description: Explain how American citizens were expected to participate in, monitor, and bring about changes in their government over time, and give examples of how they continue to do so today. (H, C)

2727E390DFE6013175F068A86D17958E.description: Identify the rights in the Bill of Rights and explain the reasons for its inclusion in the Constitution in 1791. (H, C)

2727A030DFE6013175EF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the three branches of the United States government as outlined by the Constitution, describe their functions and relationships, and identify what features of the Constitution were unique at the time (e.g., the presidency and the independent judiciary). (H, C)

27275810DFE6013175EE68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the basic political principles of American democracy and explain how the Constitution and the Bill of Rights reflect and preserve these principles. (C)
  1. individual rights and responsibilities
  2. equality
  3. the rule of law
  4. limited government
  5. representative democracy

27270700DFE6013175ED68A86D17958E.description: Describe the responsibilities of government at the federal, state, and local levels (e.g., protection of individual rights and the provision of services such as law enforcement and the building and funding of schools). (C)

2726C8E0DFE6013175EC68A86D17958E.description: The Principles and Institutions of American Constitutional Government

272687E0DFE6013175EB68A86D17958E.description:
Identify the various leaders of the Constitutional Convention and describe the major issues they debated. (H, E, C)
  1. distribution of political power
  2. rights of individuals
  3. rights of states
  4. the Great Compromise
  5. slavery

27264410DFE6013175EA68A86D17958E.description: Describe Shays's Rebellion of 1786-1787 and explain why it was one of the crucial events leading to the Constitutional Convention. (H, E, C)

2725F460DFE6013175E968A86D17958E.description: Explain the reasons for the adoption of the Articles of Confederation in 1781 and for its later failure. (H, C)

27259A80DFE6013175E868A86D17958E.description: Identify the Constitution of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, including its date, its primary author (John Adams), and the basic rights it gives to citizens of the Commonwealth. (C)

27253370DFE6013175E768A86D17958E.description:

  1. John Adams
  2. Benjamin Franklin
  3. King George III
  4. Alexander Hamilton
  5. Thomas Jefferson
  6. James Madison
  7. George Washington

  3. Saratoga (1777)
  4. Valley Forge (1777-1778)
  5. Yorktown (1781)

27243B50DFE6013175E468A86D17958E.description: The Revolution and the Formation of a Federal Government under the Constitution, 1775-1789

2723EA00DFE6013175E368A86D17958E.description:

  1. Sugar Act (1764)

2723A8E0DFE6013175E268A86D17958E.description:
Explain the development of colonial governments and describe how these developments contributed to the Revolution. (H, G, E, C)
  1. legislative bodies
  2. town meetings
  3. charters on individual freedom and rights

272368F0DFE6013175E168A86D17958E.description: Identify the founders and the reasons for the establishment of educational institutions in the colonies (grammar schools and colleges such as Harvard and the College of William and Mary). (H)

27232880DFE6013175E068A86D17958E.description: Explain the causes of the establishment of slavery in North America. Explain the importance of maritime commerce in the development of the economy of colonial Massachusetts, using the services of historical societies and museums as needed. (H, E)

27225D90DFE6013175DD68A86D17958E.description: The Political, Intellectual, and Economic Growth of the Colonies, 1700-1775

  4. England's strong economic, intellectual, and military position

2721CC80DFE6013175DB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the links between the political principles and practices developed in ancient Greece and such political institutions and practices as written constitutions and town meetings of the Puritans. (H, C)

27218760DFE6013175DA68A86D17958E.description:

  1. Lord Baltimore in Maryland

271FB190DFE6013175D468A86D17958E.description: Describe the earliest explorations of the New World by the Vikings, the period and locations of their explorations, and the evidence for them. (H, G)

271F5BC0DFE6013175D368A86D17958E.description: Pre-Columbian Civilizations of the New World and European Exploration, Colonization, and Settlement to 1700

271EA0A0DFE6013175D168A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how changes in supply and demand affected prices in colonial history (e.g., fur, lumber, fish, and meat). (E, H)

271E61F0DFE6013175D068A86D17958E.description: Define profit and describe how profit is an incentive for entrepreneurs. (E)

271E2260DFE6013175CF68A86D17958E.description: Define what an entrepreneur is (a person who has started a business seeking a profit) and give examples from colonial history of an entrepreneur (e.g., Peter Faneuil and Benjamin Franklin). (E)

271DE210DFE6013175CE68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of the ways people save their money and explain the advantages and disadvantages of each. (E)

271CCED0DFE6013175CA68A86D17958E.description: Explain the structure of the student's city or town government. (C)

271D5EB0DFE6013175CC68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of the responsibilities and powers associated with major federal and state officials (the President, chief justice of the U.S. Supreme Court, governor, state senators, and state representatives). (C)

271D12F0DFE6013175CB68A86D17958E.description: Define and use correctly words related to government: citizen, suffrage, rights, representation, federal, state, county, and municipal. (C)

271C4DF0DFE6013175C868A86D17958E.description: Compare maps of the modern world with historical maps of the world before the Age of Exploration, and describe the changes in 16th and 17th century maps of the world. (G, H, E)

271C0A10DFE6013175C768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between political and topographical maps and identify specialized maps that show information such as population, income, or climate change. (G, H, E)

271BC650DFE6013175C668A86D17958E.description: Identify the location of the North and South Poles, the equator, the prime meridian, Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western Hemispheres. (G)

271B81C0DFE6013175C568A86D17958E.description: Use maps and globes to identify absolute locations (latitude and longitude). (G)

271B3700DFE6013175C468A86D17958E.description: Observe and identify details in cartoons, photographs, charts, and graphs relating to an historical narrative. (H, E, C)

271AAEE0DFE6013175C268A86D17958E.description: Identify different ways of dating historical narratives (17th century, seventeenth century, 1600s, colonial period). (H)
