document.title: Massachusetts Science and Technology/Engineering Curriculum Framework

225C1CE0DFE601316DD368A86D17958E.description:
Communicate and apply the results of scientific investigations.
  • Develop descriptions of and explanations for scientific concepts that were a focus of one or more investigations.
  • Review information, explain statistical analysis, and summarize data collected and analyzed as the result of an investigation.
  • Explain diagrams and charts that represent relationships of variables.
  • Construct a reasoned argument and respond appropriately to critical comments and questions.
  • Use language and vocabulary appropriately, speak clearly and logically, and use appropriate technology (e.g., presentation software) and other tools to present findings.
  • Use and refine scientific models that simulate physical processes or phenomena.

225BB340DFE601316DD268A86D17958E.description:
Analyze and interpret results of scientific investigations.
  • Present relationships between and among variables in appropriate forms.
    • Represent data and relationships between and among variables in charts and graphs.
    • Use appropriate technology (e.g., graphing software) and other tools.
  • Use mathematical operations to analyze and interpret data results.
  • Assess the reliability of data and identify reasons for inconsistent results, such as sources of error or uncontrolled conditions.
  • Use results of an experiment to develop a conclusion to an investigation that addresses the initial questions and supports or refutes the stated hypothesis.
  • State questions raised by an experiment that may require further investigation.

225B4FC0DFE601316DD168A86D17958E.description:
Design and conduct scientific investigations.
  • Articulate and explain the major concepts being investigated and the purpose of an investigation.
  • Select required materials, equipment, and conditions for conducting an experiment.
  • Identify independent and dependent variables.
  • Write procedures that are clear and replicable.
  • Employ appropriate methods for accurately and consistently
    • making observations
    • making and recording measurements at appropriate levels of precision
    • collecting data or evidence in an organized way
  • Properly use instruments, equipment, and materials (e.g., scales, probeware, meter sticks, microscopes, computers) including set-up, calibration (if required), technique, maintenance, and storage.
  • Follow safety guidelines.

225AEEE0DFE601316DD068A86D17958E.description:
Make observations, raise questions, and formulate hypotheses.
  • Observe the world from a scientific perspective.
  • Pose questions and form hypotheses based on personal observations, scientific articles, experiments, and knowledge.
  • Read, interpret, and examine the credibility and validity of scientific claims in different sources of information, such as scientific articles, advertisements, or media stories.

225A2E20DFE601316DCE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the electromagnetic spectrum in terms of frequency and wavelength, and identify the locations of radio waves, microwaves, infrared radiation, visible light (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet), ultraviolet rays, x-rays, and gamma rays on the spectrum.

2259D850DFE601316DCD68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that electromagnetic waves are transverse waves and travel at the speed of light through a vacuum.

2258FB40DFE601316DCB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that moving electric charges produce magnetic forces and moving magnets produce electric forces. Recognize that the interplay of electric and magnetic forces is the basis for electric motors, generators, and other technologies.

225889E0DFE601316DCA68A86D17958E.description: Explain how electric current is a flow of charge caused by a potential difference (voltage), and how power is equal to current multiplied by voltage.

225830C0DFE601316DC968A86D17958E.description: Describe conceptually the attractive or repulsive forces between objects relative to their charges and the distance between them (Coulomb's law).

2257DD40DFE601316DC868A86D17958E.description: Analyze simple arrangements of electrical components in both series and parallel circuits. Recognize symbols and understand the functions of common circuit elements (battery, connecting wire, switch, fuse, resistance) in a schematic diagram.

22578C70DFE601316DC768A86D17958E.description: Develop qualitative and quantitative understandings of current, voltage, resistance, and the connections among them (Ohm's law).

22573AF0DFE601316DC668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that an electric charge tends to be static on insulators and can move on and in conductors. Explain that energy can produce a separation of charges.

22568760DFE601316DC468A86D17958E.description: Describe the apparent change in frequency of waves due to the motion of a source or a receiver (the Doppler effect).

22563200DFE601316DC368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that mechanical waves generally move faster through a solid than through a liquid and faster through a liquid than through a gas.

2255D330DFE601316DC268A86D17958E.description: Describe qualitatively the basic principles of reflection and refraction of waves.

22557700DFE601316DC168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between the two types of mechanical waves, transverse and longitudinal.

22551760DFE601316DC068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between mechanical and electromagnetic waves.

2254BA70DFE601316DBF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the measurable properties of waves (velocity, frequency, wavelength, amplitude, period) and explain the relationships among them. Recognize examples of simple harmonic motion.

22541460DFE601316DBD68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships among temperature changes in a substance, the amount of heat transferred, the amount (mass) of the substance, and the specific heat of the substance.

2253B220DFE601316DBC68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between average molecular kinetic energy and temperature. Recognize that energy is absorbed when a substance changes from a solid to a liquid to a gas, and that energy is released when a substance changes from a gas to a liquid to a solid. Explain the relationships among evaporation, condensation, cooling, and warming.

22532E00DFE601316DBB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how heat energy will move from a higher temperature to a lower temperature until equilibrium is reached.

2252C780DFE601316DBA68A86D17958E.description: Explain how heat energy is transferred by convection, conduction, and radiation.

22521ED0DFE601316DB868A86D17958E.description: Provide and interpret examples showing that linear momentum is the product of mass and velocity, and is always conserved (law of conservation of momentum). Calculate the momentum of an object.

2251CBD0DFE601316DB768A86D17958E.description: Describe both qualitatively and quantitatively the concept of power as work done per unit time.

225176D0DFE601316DB668A86D17958E.description: Describe both qualitatively and quantitatively how work can be expressed as a change in mechanical energy.

22511280DFE601316DB568A86D17958E.description: Interpret and provide examples of how energy can be converted from gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy and vice versa.

2250B580DFE601316DB468A86D17958E.description: Interpret and provide examples that illustrate the law of conservation of energy.

22500050DFE601316DB268A86D17958E.description: Describe conceptually the forces involved in circular motion.

224FACD0DFE601316DB168A86D17958E.description: Describe Newton's law of universal gravitation in terms of the attraction between two objects, their masses, and the distance between them.

224F5180DFE601316DB068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish qualitatively between static and kinetic friction, and describe their effects on the motion of objects.

224F0170DFE601316DAF68A86D17958E.description: Use a free-body force diagram to show forces acting on a system consisting of a pair of interacting objects. For a diagram with only co-linear forces, determine the net force acting on a system and between the objects.

224EB120DFE601316DAE68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and apply Newton's three laws of motion.

224E5EF0DFE601316DAD68A86D17958E.description: Create and interpret graphs of 1-dimensional motion, such as position vs. time, distance vs. time, speed vs. time, velocity vs. time, and acceleration vs. time where acceleration is constant.

224E0790DFE601316DAC68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between displacement, distance, velocity, speed, and acceleration. Solve problems involving displacement, distance, velocity, speed, and constant acceleration.

224DA8A0DFE601316DAB68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast vector quantities (e.g., displacement, velocity, acceleration force, linear momentum) and scalar quantities (e.g., distance, speed, energy, mass, work).

22392950DFE601316D7168A86D17958E.description:
Redesign
  • Modify the solution(s) based on information gathered during the tests and presentation

2238D7A0DFE601316D7068A86D17958E.description:
Communicate the solution(s)
  • Make an engineering presentation that includes a discussion of how the solution(s) best meet(s) the needs of the initial problem or need
  • Discuss societal impact and tradeoffs of the solution(s)

223883C0DFE601316D6F68A86D17958E.description:
Test and evaluate the solution(s)
  • Does it work?
  • Does it meet the original design constraints?

223829D0DFE601316D6E68A86D17958E.description:
Construct one or more prototypes and/or models
  • Model the selected solution(s) in two and three dimensions

2237D3E0DFE601316D6D68A86D17958E.description:
Select the best possible solution(s)
  • Determine which solution(s) best meet(s) the original requirements

22377CF0DFE601316D6C68A86D17958E.description:
Develop possible solution(s)
  • Brainstorm possible solution(s)
  • Draw on mathematics and science
  • Articulate the possible solution(s) in two and three dimensions
  • Refine the possible solution(s)

22372310DFE601316D6B68A86D17958E.description:
Research the need or problem
  • Examine current state of the issue and current solution(s)
  • Explore other options via the Internet, library, interviews, etc.

22367120DFE601316D6968A86D17958E.description: Steps of the Engineering Design Process

22361FC0DFE601316D6868A86D17958E.description: Describe the advantages of using robotics in the automation of manufacturing processes (e.g., increased production, improved quality, safety).

2235CE10DFE601316D6768A86D17958E.description: Identify the criteria necessary to select safe tools and procedures for a manufacturing process (e.g., properties of materials, required tolerances, end-uses).

22357CD0DFE601316D6668A86D17958E.description: Describe the manufacturing processes of casting and molding, forming, separating, conditioning, assembling, and finishing.

2234CA00DFE601316D6468A86D17958E.description: Explain the application of electromagnetic signals in fiber optic technologies, including critical angle and total internal reflection.

22346300DFE601316D6368A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the applications of laser and fiber optic technologies (e.g., telephone systems, cable television, photography).

22340500DFE601316D6268A86D17958E.description: Explain how the various components (source, encoder, transmitter, receiver, decoder, destination, storage, and retrieval) and processes of a communication system function.

2233B320DFE601316D6168A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between digital and analog signals. Describe how communication devices employ digital and analog technologies (e.g., computers, cell phones).

22335FE0DFE601316D6068A86D17958E.description: Explain how information travels through the following media: electrical wire, optical fiber, air, and space.

2232AA60DFE601316D5E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC), and give examples of each.

223247E0DFE601316D5D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that resistance is affected by external factors (e.g., temperature).

2231DE00DFE601316D5C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships among voltage, current, and resistance in a simple circuit, using Ohm's law.

223165E0DFE601316D5B68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the components of a circuit, including sources, conductors, circuit breakers, fuses, controllers, and loads. Examples of some controllers are switches, relays, diodes, and variable resistors.

22310B20DFE601316D5A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how to measure and calculate voltage, current, resistance, and power consumption in a series circuit and in a parallel circuit. Identify the instruments used to measure voltage, current, power consumption, and resistance.

22306B40DFE601316D5868A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain alternatives to nonrenewable energies (e.g., wind and solar energy conversion systems).

22301960DFE601316D5768A86D17958E.description: Explain how environmental conditions such as wind, solar angle, and temperature influence the design of buildings.

222FC5A0DFE601316D5668A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how conduction, convection, and radiation are considered in the selection of materials for buildings and in the design of a heating system.

222F6D90DFE601316D5568A86D17958E.description: Differentiate among conduction, convection, and radiation in a thermal system (e.g., heating and cooling a house, cooking).

222EC7F0DFE601316D5368A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain sources of resistance (e.g., 45° elbow, 90° elbow, changes in diameter) for water moving through a pipe.

222E7410DFE601316D5268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the velocity of a liquid moving in a pipe varies inversely with changes in the cross-sectional area of the pipe.

222E1E60DFE601316D5168A86D17958E.description: Calculate and describe the ability of a hydraulic system to multiply distance, multiply force, and effect directional change.

222DBA30DFE601316D5068A86D17958E.description: Explain the differences and similarities between hydraulic and pneumatic systems, and explain how each relates to manufacturing and transportation systems.

222D6280DFE601316D4F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the basic differences between open fluid systems (e.g., irrigation, forced hot air system, air compressors) and closed fluid systems (e.g., forced hot water system, hydraulic brakes).

222CA490DFE601316D4D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the purposes of zoning laws and building codes in the design and use of structures.

222C3500DFE601316D4C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and demonstrate the safe and proper use of common hand tools, power tools, and measurement devices used in construction.

222BC490DFE601316D4B68A86D17958E.description: Calculate the resultant force(s) for a combination of live loads and dead loads.

222B71A0DFE601316D4A68A86D17958E.description: Explain Bernoulli's principle and its effect on structures such as buildings and bridges.

222B1B90DFE601316D4968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among tension, compression, shear, and torsion, and explain how they relate to the selection of materials in structures.

222AC400DFE601316D4868A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the engineering properties of materials used in structures (e.g., elasticity, plasticity, R value, density, strength).

2229FE30DFE601316D4668A86D17958E.description: Interpret plans, diagrams, and working drawings in the construction of prototypes or models.

2229ABF0DFE601316D4568A86D17958E.description: Interpret and apply scale and proportion to orthographic projections and pictorial drawings (e.g., ¼" = 1'0", 1 cm = 1 m).

22295300DFE601316D4468A86D17958E.description: Produce and analyze multi-view drawings (orthographic projections) and pictorial drawings (isometric, oblique, perspective), using various techniques.

2228FD30DFE601316D4368A86D17958E.description: Understand that the engineering design process is used in the solution of problems and the advancement of society. Identify examples of technologies, objects, and processes that have been modified to advance society, and explain why and how they were modified.

2228A3B0DFE601316D4268A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the steps of the engineering design process: identify the problem, research the problem, develop possible solutions, select the best possible solution(s), construct prototypes and/or models, test and evaluate, communicate the solutions, and redesign.

221B40D0DFE601316D1C68A86D17958E.description:
Communicate and apply the results of scientific investigations.
  • Develop descriptions of and explanations for scientific concepts that were a focus of one or more investigations.
  • Review information, explain statistical analysis, and summarize data collected and analyzed as the result of an investigation.
  • Explain diagrams and charts that represent relationships of variables.
  • Construct a reasoned argument and respond appropriately to critical comments and questions.
  • Use language and vocabulary appropriately, speak clearly and logically, and use appropriate technology (e.g., presentation software) and other tools to present findings.
  • Use and refine scientific models that simulate physical processes or phenomena.

221AB810DFE601316D1B68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze and interpret results of scientific investigations.
  • Present relationships between and among variables in appropriate forms.
    • Represent data and relationships between and among variables in charts and graphs.
    • Use appropriate technology (e.g., graphing software) and other tools.
  • Use mathematical operations to analyze and interpret data results.
  • Assess the reliability of data and identify reasons for inconsistent results, such as sources of error or uncontrolled conditions.
  • Use results of an experiment to develop a conclusion to an investigation that addresses the initial questions and supports or refutes the stated hypothesis.
  • State questions raised by an experiment that may require further investigation.

221A5880DFE601316D1A68A86D17958E.description:
Design and conduct scientific investigations.
  • Articulate and explain the major concepts being investigated and the purpose of an investigation.
  • Select required materials, equipment, and conditions for conducting an experiment.
  • Identify independent and dependent variables.
  • Write procedures that are clear and replicable.
  • Employ appropriate methods for accurately and consistently
    • making observations
    • making and recording measurements at appropriate levels of precision
    • collecting data or evidence in an organized way
  • Properly use instruments, equipment, and materials (e.g., scales, probeware, meter sticks, microscopes, computers) including set-up, calibration (if required), technique, maintenance, and storage.
  • Follow safety guidelines.

221A0040DFE601316D1968A86D17958E.description:
Make observations, raise questions, and formulate hypotheses.
  • Observe the world from a scientific perspective.
  • Pose questions and form hypotheses based on personal observations, scientific articles, experiments, and knowledge.
  • Read, interpret, and examine the credibility and validity of scientific claims in different sources of information, such as scientific articles, advertisements, or media stories.

22195950DFE601316D1768A86D17958E.description: Explain how water, carbon, and nitrogen cycle between abiotic resources and organic matter in an ecosystem, and how oxygen cycles through photosynthesis and respiration.

22190830DFE601316D1668A86D17958E.description: Use a food web to identify and distinguish producers, consumers, and decomposers, and explain the transfer of energy through trophic levels. Describe how relationships among organisms (predation, parasitism, competition, commensalism, mutualism) add to the complexity of biological communities.

2218B740DFE601316D1568A86D17958E.description: Analyze changes in population size and biodiversity (speciation and extinction) that result from the following: natural causes, changes in climate, human activity, and the introduction of invasive, non-native species.

221862A0DFE601316D1468A86D17958E.description: Explain how birth, death, immigration, and emigration influence population size.

2217B4D0DFE601316D1268A86D17958E.description: Explain how evolution through natural selection can result in changes in biodiversity through the increase or decrease of genetic diversity within a population.

22176300DFE601316D1168A86D17958E.description: Describe species as reproductively distinct groups of organisms. Recognize that species are further classified into a hierarchical taxonomic system (kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species) based on morphological, behavioral, and molecular similarities. Describe the role that geographic isolation can play in speciation.

22171120DFE601316D1068A86D17958E.description: Explain how evolution is demonstrated by evidence from the fossil record, comparative anatomy, genetics, molecular biology, and examples of natural selection.

22165B00DFE601316D0E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the body's systems interact to maintain homeostasis. Describe the basic function of a physiological feedback loop.

2215FC90DFE601316D0D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that communication among cells is required for coordination of body functions. The nerves communicate with electrochemical signals, hormones circulate through the blood, and some cells produce signals to communicate only with nearby cells.

22159BD0DFE601316D0C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the sexual reproductive system allows organisms to produce offspring that receive half of their genetic information from their mother and half from their father, and that sexually produced offspring resemble, but are not identical to, either of their parents.

221534C0DFE601316D0B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the muscular/skeletal system (skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscles, bones, cartilage, ligaments, tendons) works with other systems to support the body and allow for movement. Recognize that bones produce blood cells.

2214DB50DFE601316D0A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the nervous system (brain, spinal cord, sensory neurons, motor neurons) mediates communication among different parts of the body and mediates the body's interactions with the environment. Identify the basic unit of the nervous system, the neuron, and explain generally how it works.

22147C90DFE601316D0968A86D17958E.description: Explain how the respiratory system (nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, lungs, alveoli) provides exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

22142610DFE601316D0868A86D17958E.description: Explain how the circulatory system (heart, arteries, veins, capillaries, red blood cells) transports nutrients and oxygen to cells and removes cell wastes. Describe how the kidneys and the liver are closely associated with the circulatory system as they perform the excretory function of removing waste from the blood. Recognize that kidneys remove nitrogenous wastes, and the liver removes many toxic compounds from blood.

2213C310DFE601316D0768A86D17958E.description: Explain generally how the digestive system (mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small and large intestines, rectum) converts macromolecules from food into smaller molecules that can be used by cells for energy and for repair and growth.

2212F440DFE601316D0568A86D17958E.description: Use a Punnett Square to determine the probabilities for genotype and phenotype combinations in monohybrid crosses.

22128900DFE601316D0468A86D17958E.description: Describe how Mendel's laws of segregation and independent assortment can be observed through patterns of inheritance (e.g., dihybrid crosses).

22123060DFE601316D0368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among observed inheritance patterns caused by several types of genetic traits (dominant, recessive, codominant, sex-linked, polygenic, incomplete dominance, multiple alleles).

2211D260DFE601316D0268A86D17958E.description: Explain how mutations in the DNA sequence of a gene may or may not result in phenotypic change in an organism. Explain how mutations in gametes may result in phenotypic changes in offspring.

22118090DFE601316D0168A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic process of DNA replication and how it relates to the transmission and conservation of the genetic code. Explain the basic processes of transcription and translation, and how they result in the expression of genes. Distinguish among the end products of replication, transcription, and translation.

22112330DFE601316D0068A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic structure (double helix, sugar/phosphate backbone, linked by complementary nucleotide pairs) of DNA, and describe its function in genetic inheritance.

22105370DFE601316CFE68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a virus and a cell in terms of genetic material and reproduction.

220FFBF0DFE601316CFD68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the process of meiosis results in the formation of haploid cells. Explain the importance of this process in sexual reproduction, and how gametes form diploid zygotes in the process of fertilization.

220F9C70DFE601316CFC68A86D17958E.description: Describe the cell cycle and the process of mitosis. Explain the role of mitosis in the formation of new cells, and its importance in maintaining chromosome number during asexual reproduction.

220F2180DFE601316CFB68A86D17958E.description: Explain the important role that ATP serves in metabolism.

220EC5C0DFE601316CFA68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reactants, products, and basic purposes of photosynthesis and cellular respiration. Explain the interrelated nature of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in the cells of photosynthetic organisms.

220E7270DFE601316CF968A86D17958E.description: Use cellular evidence (e.g., cell structure, cell number, cell reproduction) and modes of nutrition to describe the six kingdoms (Archaebacteria, Eubacteria, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia).

220E1D30DFE601316CF868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast, at the cellular level, the general structures and degrees of complexity of prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

220DC050DFE601316CF768A86D17958E.description: Relate cell parts/organelles (plasma membrane, nuclear envelope, nucleus, nucleolus, cytoplasm, mitochondrion, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosome, ribosome, vacuole, cell wall, chloroplast, cytoskeleton, centriole, cilium, flagellum, pseudopod) to their functions. Explain the role of cell membranes as a highly selective barrier (diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion, active transport).

220D0940DFE601316CF568A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of enzymes as catalysts that lower the activation energy of biochemical reactions. Identify factors, such as pH and temperature, that have an effect on enzymes.

220CB590DFE601316CF468A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic molecular structures and primary functions of the four major categories of organic molecules (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids).

220C5F30DFE601316CF368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that biological organisms are composed primarily of very few elements. The six most common are C, H, N, O, P, and S.

224AC200DFE601316DA368A86D17958E.description: Describe oxidation and reduction reactions and give some everyday examples, such as fuel burning and corrosion. Assign oxidation numbers in a reaction.

224A1980DFE601316DA168A86D17958E.description: Relate hydrogen ion concentrations to the pH scale and to acidic, basic, and neutral solutions. Compare and contrast the strengths of various common acids and bases (e.g., vinegar, baking soda, soap, citrus juice).

2249BB10DFE601316DA068A86D17958E.description: Define the Arrhenius theory of acids and bases in terms of the presence of hydronium and hydroxide ions in water and the Bronsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases in terms of proton donors and acceptors.

22495400DFE601316D9F68A86D17958E.description: Acids and Bases and Oxidation-Reduction Reactions

224900B0DFE601316D9E68A86D17958E.description: Predict the shift in equilibrium when a system is subjected to a stress (LeChatelier's principle) and identify the factors that can cause a shift in equilibrium (concentration, pressure, volume, temperature).

2248ADD0DFE601316D9D68A86D17958E.description: Identify the factors that affect the rate of a chemical reaction (temperature, mixing, concentration, particle size, surface area, catalyst).

22484BE0DFE601316D9C68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast qualitatively the properties of solutions and pure solvents (colligative properties such as boiling point and freezing point).

2247E970DFE601316D9B68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the factors that affect the rate of dissolving (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area, pressure, mixing).

22479A10DFE601316D9A68A86D17958E.description: Calculate concentration in terms of molarity. Use molarity to perform solution dilution and solution stoichiometry.

22474A50DFE601316D9968A86D17958E.description: Describe the process by which solutes dissolve in solvents.

2246F670DFE601316D9868A86D17958E.description: Solutions, Rates of Reaction, and Equilibrium

2246A020DFE601316D9768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there is a natural tendency for systems to move in a direction of disorder or randomness (entropy).

22464D90DFE601316D9668A86D17958E.description: Describe the law of conservation of energy. Explain the difference between an endothermic process and an exothermic process.

2245FC60DFE601316D9568A86D17958E.description: Using the kinetic molecular theory, describe and contrast the properties of gases, liquids, and solids. Explain, at the molecular level, the behavior of matter as it undergoes phase transitions.

2245ADE0DFE601316D9468A86D17958E.description: Perform calculations using the ideal gas law. Understand the molar volume at 273 K and 1 atmosphere (STP).

22455D10DFE601316D9368A86D17958E.description: Using the kinetic molecular theory, explain the behavior of gases and the relationship between pressure and volume (Boyle's law), volume and temperature (Charles's law), pressure and temperature (Gay-Lussac's law), and the number of particles in a gas sample (Avogadro's hypothesis). 2244B2D0DFE601316D9168A86D17958E.description: Calculate percent yield in a chemical reaction.

224460F0DFE601316D9068A86D17958E.description: Calculate the mass-to-mass stoichiometry for a chemical reaction.

22440270DFE601316D8F68A86D17958E.description: Determine percent compositions, empirical formulas, and molecular formulas.

2243A550DFE601316D8E68A86D17958E.description: Use the mole concept to determine number of particles and molar mass for elements and compounds.

22434690DFE601316D8D68A86D17958E.description: Classify chemical reactions as synthesis (combination), decomposition, single displacement (replacement), double displacement, and combustion.

2242E960DFE601316D8C68A86D17958E.description: Balance chemical equations by applying the laws of conservation of mass and constant composition (definite proportions).

22421910DFE601316D8A68A86D17958E.description: Name and write the chemical formulas for simple ionic and molecular compounds, including those that contain the polyatomic ions: ammonium, carbonate, hydroxide, nitrate, phosphate, and sulfate.

2241BCE0DFE601316D8968A86D17958E.description: Identify how hydrogen bonding in water affects a variety of physical, chemical, and biological phenomena (e.g., surface tension, capillary action, density, boiling point).

22415800DFE601316D8868A86D17958E.description: Use valence-shell electron-pair repulsion theory (VSEPR) to predict the molecular geometry (linear, trigonal planar, and tetrahedral) of simple molecules.

22410840DFE601316D8768A86D17958E.description: Use electronegativity to explain the difference between polar and nonpolar covalent bonds.

2240B9E0DFE601316D8668A86D17958E.description: Draw Lewis dot structures for simple molecules and ionic compounds.

22406AF0DFE601316D8568A86D17958E.description: Explain how atoms combine to form compounds through both ionic and covalent bonding. Predict chemical formulas based on the number of valence electrons.

223FC5C0DFE601316D8368A86D17958E.description: Identify trends on the periodic table (ionization energy, electronegativity, and relative sizes of atoms and ions).

223F6810DFE601316D8268A86D17958E.description: Relate the position of an element on the periodic table to its electron configuration and compare its reactivity to the reactivity of other elements in the table.

223F0C40DFE601316D8168A86D17958E.description: Use the periodic table to identify the three classes of elements: metals, nonmetals, and metalloids.

223EA990DFE601316D8068A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship of an element's position on the periodic table to its atomic number. Identify families (groups) and periods on the periodic table.

223DF2F0DFE601316D7E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.

223D9270DFE601316D7D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the process of radioactive decay by using nuclear equations, and explain the concept of half-life for an isotope (for example, C-14 is a powerful tool in determining the age of objects).

223D1890DFE601316D7C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the three main types of radioactive decay (alpha, beta, and gamma) and compare their properties (composition, mass, charge, and penetrating power).

223CB080DFE601316D7B68A86D17958E.description: Write the electron configurations for the first twenty elements of the periodic table.

223C5F10DFE601316D7A68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and apply the laws of conservation of mass, constant composition (definite proportions), and multiple proportions.

223C0960DFE601316D7968A86D17958E.description: Describe Rutherford's "gold foil" experiment that led to the discovery of the nuclear atom. Identify the major components (protons, neutrons, and electrons) of the nuclear atom and explain how they interact.

223BAED0DFE601316D7868A86D17958E.description: Recognize discoveries from Dalton (atomic theory), Thomson (the electron), Rutherford (the nucleus), and Bohr (planetary model of atom), and understand how each discovery leads to modern theory.

223B0800DFE601316D7668A86D17958E.description: Describe the three normal states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) in terms of energy, particle motion, and phase transitions.

223AB540DFE601316D7568A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between pure substances (elements and compounds) and mixtures. Differentiate between heterogeneous and homogeneous mixtures.

223A5AB0DFE601316D7468A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain physical properties (e.g., density, melting point, boiling point, conductivity, malleability) and chemical properties (e.g., the ability to form new substances). Distinguish between chemical and physical changes.

22278030DFE601316D3F68A86D17958E.description:
Communicate and apply the results of scientific investigations.
  • Develop descriptions of and explanations for scientific concepts that were a focus of one or more investigations.
  • Review information, explain statistical analysis, and summarize data collected and analyzed as the result of an investigation.
  • Explain diagrams and charts that represent relationships of variables.
  • Construct a reasoned argument and respond appropriately to critical comments and questions.
  • Use language and vocabulary appropriately, speak clearly and logically, and use appropriate technology (e.g., presentation software) and other tools to present findings.
  • Use and refine scientific models that simulate physical processes or phenomena.

22271510DFE601316D3E68A86D17958E.description:
Analyze and interpret results of scientific investigations.
  • Present relationships between and among variables in appropriate forms.
  • Represent data and relationships between and among variables in charts and graphs.
  • Use appropriate technology (e.g., graphing software) and other tools.
  • Use mathematical operations to analyze and interpret data results.
  • Assess the reliability of data and identify reasons for inconsistent results, such as sources of error or uncontrolled conditions.
  • Use results of an experiment to develop a conclusion to an investigation that addresses the initial questions and supports or refutes the stated hypothesis.
  • State questions raised by an experiment that may require further investigation.

2226ACA0DFE601316D3D68A86D17958E.description:
Design and conduct scientific investigations.
  • Articulate and explain the major concepts being investigated and the purpose of an investigation.
  • Select required materials, equipment, and conditions for conducting an experiment.
  • Identify independent and dependent variables.
  • Write procedures that are clear and replicable.
  • Employ appropriate methods for accurately and consistently
    • making observations
    • making and recording measurements at appropriate levels of precision
    • collecting data or evidence in an organized way
  • Properly use instruments, equipment, and materials (e.g., scales, probeware, meter sticks, microscopes, computers) including set-up, calibration (if required), technique, maintenance, and storage.
  • Follow safety guidelines.

22265400DFE601316D3C68A86D17958E.description:
Make observations, raise questions, and formulate hypotheses.
  • Observe the world from a scientific perspective.
  • Pose questions and form hypotheses based on personal observations, scientific articles, experiments, and knowledge.
  • Read, interpret, and examine the credibility and validity of scientific claims in different sources of information, such as scientific articles, advertisements, or media stories.

2225A960DFE601316D3A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Sun, Earth, and solar system formed from a nebula of dust and gas in a spiral arm of the Milky Way Galaxy about 4.6 billion years ago.

222551C0DFE601316D3968A86D17958E.description: Describe the influence of gravity and inertia on the rotation and revolution of orbiting bodies. Explain the Sun-Earth-moon relationships (e.g., day, year, solar/lunar eclipses, tides).

2224F380DFE601316D3868A86D17958E.description: Explain the Big Bang Theory and discuss the evidence that supports it, such as background radiation and relativistic Doppler effect (i.e., "red shift").

22249E20DFE601316D3768A86D17958E.description: The Origin and Evolution of the Universe

22216280DFE601316D2E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the Richter scale of earthquake magnitude and the relative damage that is incurred by earthquakes of a given magnitude.

22210F70DFE601316D2D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how seismic data are used to reveal Earth's interior structure and to locate earthquake epicenters.

2220B800DFE601316D2C68A86D17958E.description: Relate earthquakes, volcanic activity, tsunamis, mountain building, and tectonic uplift to plate movements.

22244440DFE601316D3668A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between convection currents in Earth's mantle and the motion of the lithospheric plates.

2223E330DFE601316D3568A86D17958E.description: Trace the development of a lithospheric plate from its growth at a divergent boundary (mid-ocean ridge) to its destruction at a convergent boundary (subduction zone). Recognize that alternating magnetic polarity is recorded in rock at mid-ocean ridges.

22238910DFE601316D3468A86D17958E.description: Describe the absolute and relative dating methods used to measure geologic time, such as index fossils, radioactive dating, law of superposition, and crosscutting relationships.

22232190DFE601316D3368A86D17958E.description: Describe the rock cycle, and the processes that are responsible for the formation of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks. Compare the physical properties of these rock types and the physical properties of common rock-forming minerals.

2222C5B0DFE601316D3268A86D17958E.description: Describe the processes of the hydrologic cycle, including evaporation, condensation, precipitation, surface runoff and groundwater percolation, infiltration, and transpiration.

22226A90DFE601316D3168A86D17958E.description: Explain how water flows into and through a watershed. Explain the roles of aquifers, wells, porosity, permeability, water table, and runoff.

22206260DFE601316D2B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how physical and chemical weathering leads to erosion and the formation of soils and sediments, and creates various types of landscapes. Give examples that show the effects of physical and chemical weathering on the environment.

221FC1F0DFE601316D2968A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects on the environment and on the carbon cycle of using both renewable and nonrenewable sources of energy.

221F6760DFE601316D2868A86D17958E.description: Recognize, describe, and compare renewable energy resources (e.g., solar, wind, water, biomass) and nonrenewable energy resources (e.g., fossil fuels, nuclear energy).

221F18B0DFE601316D2768A86D17958E.description: Energy Resources in the Earth System

221EC960DFE601316D2668A86D17958E.description: Read, interpret, and analyze a combination of ground-based observations, satellite data, and computer models to demonstrate Earth systems and their interconnections.

221E7930DFE601316D2568A86D17958E.description: Explain the dynamics of oceanic currents, including upwelling, deep-water currents, the Labrador Current and the Gulf Stream, and their relationship to global circulation within the marine environment and climate.

221E27D0DFE601316D2468A86D17958E.description: Describe the various conditions associated with frontal boundaries and cyclonic storms (e.g., thunderstorms, winter storms [nor'easters], hurricanes, tornadoes) and their impact on human affairs, including storm preparations.

221DC530DFE601316D2368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the revolution of Earth around the Sun and the inclination of Earth on its axis cause Earth's seasonal variations (equinoxes and solstices).

221D5A30DFE601316D2268A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how the unequal heating of Earth and the Coriolis effect influence global circulation patterns, and show how they impact Massachusetts weather and climate (e.g., global winds, convection cells, land/sea breezes, mountain/valley breezes).

221D0090DFE601316D2168A86D17958E.description: Explain how the transfer of energy through radiation, conduction, and convection contributes to global atmospheric processes, such as storms, winds, and currents.

221CB160DFE601316D2068A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics of electromagnetic radiation and give examples of its impact on life and Earth's systems.

221C60D0DFE601316D1F68A86D17958E.description: Identify Earth's principal sources of internal and external energy, such as radioactive decay, gravity, and solar energy.

221C0E20DFE601316D1E68A86D17958E.description: Matter and Energy in the Earth System

221BB4F0DFE601316D1D68A86D17958E.description: Earth and Space Science High School Course

document.title: Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework

2706D1A0DFE6013175BD68A86D17958E.description: Identify when the countries in the Caribbean and in Central America became independent nations and explain how independence was achieved. (H, G)

270687E0DFE6013175BC68A86D17958E.description: Identify the different languages used in different countries in the Caribbean region today (e.g., Spanish in Cuba, French in Haiti, English in Barbados and Jamaica). (H)

270638E0DFE6013175BB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the climate and major natural resources of Central America and the Caribbean Islands and explain their relationship to the economy of those regions. (G, E)

2705F5F0DFE6013175BA68A86D17958E.description: On a map of North and South America, locate the Isthmus of Panama which divides North from South America. Use a map key to locate islands, countries, and major cities of Central America and the Caribbean Islands. (G, E)

2705ACF0DFE6013175B968A86D17958E.description: Optional Standards for Central America and the Caribbean Islands

270564D0DFE6013175B868A86D17958E.description: Identify when Mexico became an independent nation and describe how independence was achieved. (H, G)

270505A0DFE6013175B768A86D17958E.description: Identify the language, major religion, and peoples of Mexico. (H)

2704BD90DFE6013175B668A86D17958E.description: Describe the climate, major physical characteristics, and major natural resources of Mexico and explain their relationship to the Mexican economy. (G)

27047000DFE6013175B568A86D17958E.description: On a map of North America, locate Mexico and its major cities. (G)

2703E940DFE6013175B368A86D17958E.description: Identify the major language groups in Canada, their geographic location, and the relations among them. (H, G)

27039B30DFE6013175B268A86D17958E.description: Identify the location of at least two Native American tribes in Canada (e.g., Kwakiutl and Micmac) and the Inuit nation and describe their major social features. (H, G)

27034F70DFE6013175B168A86D17958E.description: Identify when Canada became an independent nation and explain how independence was achieved. (H, G)

2702EEF0DFE6013175B068A86D17958E.description: Describe the major ethnic and religious groups of modern CanadA. (G, H, C, E)

2702AD80DFE6013175AF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the climate, major physical characteristics, and major natural resources of Canada and explain their relationship to settlement, trade, and the Canadian economy. (G, E)

270267E0DFE6013175AE68A86D17958E.description: On a map of North America, locate Canada, its provinces, and major cities. (G)

2701D8A0DFE6013175AC68A86D17958E.description: Identify major immigrant groups that live in Massachusetts and where they now live in large numbers (e.g., English, Irish, Italians, French Canadians, Armenians, Greeks, Portuguese, Haitians, and Vietnamese). (H, G)

270182C0DFE6013175AB68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the diverse nature of the American people by identifying the distinctive contributions to American culture of:
  1. several indigenous peoples in different areas of the country (e.g., Navajo, Seminoles, Sioux, Hawaiians, and Inuits).
  2. African Americans, including an explanation of their early concentration in the South because of slavery and the Great Migration to northern cities in the 20th century, and recent African immigrant groups (e.g., Ethiopian) and where they tended to settle in large numbers.
  3. major European immigrant groups who have come to America, locating their countries of origin and where they tended to settle in large numbers (e.g., English, Germans, Italians, Scots, Irish, Jews, Poles, and Scandinavians).
  4. major Spanish-speaking (e.g., Cubans, Mexicans) and Asian (e.g., Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese) immigrant groups who have come to America in the 19th and 20th centuries, locating their countries of origin and where they tended to settle in large numbers. (H, G)

27014440DFE6013175AA68A86D17958E.description: Identify the five different European countries (France, Spain, England, Russia, and the Netherlands) that influenced different regions of the present United States at the time the New World was being explored and describe how their influence can be traced to place names, architectural features, and language. (H, G)

27010570DFE6013175A968A86D17958E.description: Identify major monuments and historical sites in and around Washington, D.C. (e.g., the Jefferson and Lincoln Memorials, the Smithsonian Museums, the Library of Congress, the White House, the Capitol, the Washington Monument, the National Archives, Arlington National Cemetery, the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, the Iwo Jima Memorial, and Mount Vernon). (G)

2700C670DFE6013175A868A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe unique features of the United States (e.g., the Everglades, the Grand Canyon, Mount Rushmore, the Redwood Forest, Yellowstone National Park, and Yosemite National Park). (G)

270085E0DFE6013175A768A86D17958E.description: Describe the climate, major physical features, and major natural resources in each region. (G)

27004350DFE6013175A668A86D17958E.description: Identify the states, state capitals, and major cities in each region. (G)

26FFFF00DFE6013175A568A86D17958E.description: On a map of North America, locate the current boundaries of the United States (including Alaska and Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico). Locate the states of the Midwest, Northeast, Southeast, Southwest, and West regions of the United States, in addition to the six states of New England. (G)

26FFA8C0DFE6013175A468A86D17958E.description: On a map of the world, locate North America. On a map of North America, locate the United States, the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, Gulf of Mexico, Mississippi and Rio Grande Rivers, the Great Lakes, Hudson Bay, and the Rocky and Appalachian Mountain ranges. (G)

26FEE600DFE6013175A168A86D17958E.description: After visiting a museum, listening to a museum educator in school, or conducting research in the library, describe an animal, person, building, or design depicted in an ancient Chinese work of art. (H, G)

26FEA2C0DFE6013175A068A86D17958E.description: Describe how the First Emperor unified China by subduing warring factions, seizing land, centralizing government, imposing strict rules, and creating with the use of slave labor large state building projects for irrigation, transportation, and defense (e.g., the Great Wall). (H, C, E)

26FE6150DFE60131759F68A86D17958E.description: Identify who Confucius was and describe his writings on good government, codes of proper conduct, and relationships between parent and child, friend and friend, husband and wife, and subject and ruler. (H, C)

26FE1F00DFE60131759E68A86D17958E.description: Describe important technologies of China such as bronze casting, silk manufacture, and gunpowder. (H, E)

26FDD250DFE60131759D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the ideographic writing system used by the Chinese (characters, which are symbols for concepts/ideas) and how it differs from an alphabetic writing system. (H)

26FD8970DFE60131759C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the topography and climate of eastern Asia, including the importance of mountain ranges and deserts, and explain how geography influenced the growth of Chinese civilization. (G, E)

26FD38E0DFE60131759B68A86D17958E.description: On a map of Asia, locate China, the Huang He (Yellow) River and Chang Jiang (Yangtze) Rivers, and the Himalayan Mountains. (G)

26FCEA20DFE60131759A68A86D17958E.description: Optional Standards for Ancient China, c. 3000-200 BC/BCE

26FC3980DFE60131759868A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how the interaction of buyers and sellers influences the prices of goods and services in markets. (E)

26FBD010DFE60131759768A86D17958E.description: Give examples of limited and unlimited resources and explain how scarcity compels people and communities to make choices about goods and services, giving up some things to get other things. (E)

26FB8E50DFE60131759668A86D17958E.description: Define and give examples of natural resources in the United States. (E)

26FB1120DFE60131759468A86D17958E.description: Give examples of the different ways immigrants can become citizens of the United States. (C)

26FACF20DFE60131759368A86D17958E.description: Give examples of the major rights that immigrants have acquired as citizens of the United States (e.g., the right to vote, and freedom of religion, speech, assembly, and petition). (C)

26FA3BF0DFE60131759168A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe national historic sites and describe their function and significance. (H, C)

26F9FC70DFE60131759068A86D17958E.description: Interpret a map using information from its title, compass rose, scale, and legend. (G)

26F9BBE0DFE60131758F68A86D17958E.description: Use map and globe skills to determine absolute locations (latitude and longitude) of places studied. (G)

26F8D5F0DFE60131758C68A86D17958E.description: North American Geography with Optional Standards for One Early Civilization

22DE7FF0DFE601316EC968A86D17958E.description: Integrate knowledge of dance, music, theatre, and visual arts and apply the arts to learning other disciplines
comments:
Examples of this include:
  • using visual arts skills to illustrate understanding of a story read in English language arts or foreign languages;
  • memorizing and singing American folk songs to enhance understanding of history and geography;
  • using short dance sequences to clarify concepts in mathematics.

22E21C80DFE601316ED468A86D17958E.description:
When using art materials or handling and viewing artifacts or musical instruments, ask and answer questions such as
  • "What is this made of?"
  • "How does this instrument produce sound?"
  • "Would I design this differently?"
  • "Who first thought of making something like this?"
comments: For example, students examine a variety of percussion instruments, experiment with the different sounds they make, and learn about the cultures in which they were made.

22E15410DFE601316ED268A86D17958E.description: Perform or create works inspired by historical or cultural styles

22E10B60DFE601316ED168A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristic features of the visual arts of world civilizations such as styles of ancient Egypt and Africa, China, Mesopotamia, Greece, Rome, and the Medieval period in Europe

22E0BF60DFE601316ED068A86D17958E.description:
Identify characteristic features of the performing and visual arts of native populations and immigrant groups to America, such as
  • styles of North American native cultures of the East Coast, Plains, Southwest, and Northwest;
  • styles of folk and fine arts of immigrant groups from European, African, Latin American, Asian, and Middle Eastern countries
comments: For example, students look at examples of Native American clay containers from the Southwest, and wooden containers from the Northwest and compare the similarities and differences in form and decoration.

22E073D0DFE601316ECF68A86D17958E.description: Concepts of Style, Stylistic Influence, and Stylistic Change

22E02040DFE601316ECE68A86D17958E.description: Investigate how artists create their work; read about, view films about, or interview artists such as choreographers, dancers, composers, singers, instrumentalists, actors, storytellers, playwrights, illustrators, painters, sculptors, craftspeople, or architects
comments: For example, teachers invite an illustrator of children's books to school to show how she creates her illustrations.

22DF8540DFE601316ECC68A86D17958E.description: Investigate uses and meanings of examples of the arts in children's daily lives, homes, and communities
comments: For example, children learn and teach other children songs in languages other than English; interview parents and community members about dances, songs, images, and stories that are part of their family and cultural heritage.

22DF22C0DFE601316ECB68A86D17958E.description: When viewing or listening to examples of visual arts, architecture, music, dance, storytelling, and theatre, ask and answer questions such as, "What is the artist trying to say?" "Who made this, and why?" "How does this work make me feel?"

22DECD30DFE601316ECA68A86D17958E.description: Purposes and Meanings in the Arts

22DDA380DFE601316EC668A86D17958E.description: Explain strengths and weaknesses in their own work, and share comments constructively and supportively within the group

22DD58D0DFE601316EC568A86D17958E.description: Describe similarities and differences in works, and present personal responses to the subject matter, materials, techniques, and use of design elements in artworks

22DD0060DFE601316EC468A86D17958E.description: Classify artworks into general categories, such as painting, printmaking, collage, sculpture, pottery, textiles, architecture, photography, and film

22DCA6B0DFE601316EC368A86D17958E.description: In the course of making and viewing art, learn ways of discussing it, such as by making a list of all of the images seen in an artwork (visual inventory); and identifying kinds of color, line, texture, shapes, and forms in the work

22DC07A0DFE601316EC168A86D17958E.description: As a class, develop and use criteria for informal classroom discussions about art

22DBC460DFE601316EC068A86D17958E.description: Select works for exhibition and work as a group to create a display

22DB7FA0DFE601316EBF68A86D17958E.description: Select a work or works created during the year and discuss them with a parent, classmate, or teacher, explaining how the work was made, and why it was chosen for discussion
comments: For example, a first grader chooses a painting and tells how she mixed the colors, and talks about the decisions she made.

For example, students draw members of a family from memory; illustrate a character in a folktale or play; build a clay model of an ideal place to play; or make images that convey ideas such as friendship.
22DAF2C0DFE601316EBD68A86D17958E.description: Create 2D and 3D artwork from memory or imagination to tell a story or embody an idea or fantasy

22DA9E90DFE601316EBC68A86D17958E.description: Create 2D and 3D expressive artwork that explores abstraction
comments: For example, a student simplifies an image by making decisions about essential colors, lines, or textures.

22DA5520DFE601316EBB68A86D17958E.description: Create 2D and 3D artwork from direct observation
comments: For example, students draw a still life of flowers or fruit, action studies of their classmates in sports poses, or sketches of the class pet having a snack or a nap.

22D9BEF0DFE601316EB968A86D17958E.description:
For space and composition, explore composition by creating artwork with a center of interest, repetition, and/or balance
  • Demonstrate an understanding of foreground, middle ground, and background
  • Define and identify occurrences of balance, rhythm, repetition, variety, and emphasis

22D97060DFE601316EB868A86D17958E.description:
For pattern and symmetry, explore the use of patterns and symmetrical shapes in 2D and 3D works
  • Identify patterns and symmetrical forms and shapes in the environment and artwork.
  • Explain and demonstrate ways in which patterns and symmetrical shapes may be made
comments: For example, a student folds and cuts paper to achieve symmetry, or makes printed patterns.

22D920E0DFE601316EB768A86D17958E.description:
For shape and form, explore the use of shapes and forms in 2D and 3D works
  • Identify simple shapes of different sizes, for example, circles, squares, triangles, and forms, for example, spheres, cones, cubes, in the environment and in artwork

22D8B920DFE601316EB668A86D17958E.description:
For texture, explore the use of textures in 2D and 3D works
  • Identify a wide variety of types of textures, for example, smooth, rough, and bumpy, in the environment and in artwork
  • Create representations of textures in drawings, paintings, rubbings, or relief

22D87060DFE601316EB568A86D17958E.description:
For line, explore the use of line in 2D and 3D works
  • Identify a wide variety of types of lines in the environment and in artwork
comments: For example, students take a walk around the school and note jagged, straight, curved, thick, and thin lines.

22D82560DFE601316EB468A86D17958E.description:
For color, explore and experiment with the use of color in dry and wet media
  • Identify primary and secondary colors and gradations of black, white and gray in the environment and artwork
  • Explore how color can convey mood and emotion
comments: For example, students mix light and dark values of colors or predict the results of overlapping and blending primary colors.

22D79040DFE601316EB268A86D17958E.description: Learn to take care of materials and tools and to use them safely

22D739C0DFE601316EB168A86D17958E.description: Learn and use appropriate vocabulary related to methods, materials, and techniques

22D6F490DFE601316EB068A86D17958E.description: Create artwork in a variety of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) media, for example: 2D – drawing, painting, collage, printmaking, weaving; 3D – plastic (malleable) materials such as clay and paper, wood, or found objects for assemblage and construction

22D6B0C0DFE601316EAF68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of materials and media, for example, crayons, chalk, paint, clay, various kinds of papers, textiles, and yarns, and understand how to use them to produce different visual effects

22D5E010DFE601316EAC68A86D17958E.description: Give and accept constructive and supportive feedback

22D59350DFE601316EAB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe strengths and weakness of their own work (grades 3 and 4 only)

22D535D0DFE601316EAA68A86D17958E.description: Articulate reasons for particular emotional responses to and personal preferences about classroom dramatizations and dramatic performances

22D4E070DFE601316EA968A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the visual, aural, oral, and kinetic details of classroom dramatizations and dramatic performances

22D48AC0DFE601316EA868A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate audience skills of observing attentively and responding appropriately in classroom presentations, rehearsals, and live performance settings

22D3C3C0DFE601316EA668A86D17958E.description: Visualize environments and arrange the physical playing space to communicate mood, time, and locale

22D372D0DFE601316EA568A86D17958E.description: Collect, make, or borrow materials that could be used for scenery, properties (props), costumes, sound effects, and lighting for informal classroom presentations

26E62EE0DFE60131758A68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of tax-supported facilities and services provided by their local government, such as public schools, parks, recreational facilities, police and fire departments, and libraries. (E)

26E5ED30DFE60131758968A86D17958E.description: Give examples of goods and services provided by their local businesses and industries. (E)

26E5AA40DFE60131758868A86D17958E.description: Explain how objects or artifacts of everyday life in the past tell us how ordinary people lived and how everyday life has changed. Draw on the services of the local historical society and local museums as needed. (H, G, E)

26E56940DFE60131758768A86D17958E.description: Identify when the students' own town or city was founded, and describe the different groups of people who have settled in the community since its founding. (H, G)

26E52A80DFE60131758668A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of the stars and stripes in the American flag, and describe official procedures for the care and display of the flag. (C)

26E4DFC0DFE60131758568A86D17958E.description: Identify historic buildings, monuments, or sites in the area and explain their purpose and significance. (H, C)

26E4A0F0DFE60131758468A86D17958E.description: On a map of Massachusetts, locate the class's home town or city and its local geographic features and landmarks. (G)

26E418E0DFE60131758268A86D17958E.description:
After reading a biography of a person from Massachusetts in one of the following categories, summarize the person's life and achievements. (H, C)
  1. science and technology (e.g., Alexander Graham Bell, Nathaniel Bowditch, Robert Goddard, John Hayes Hammond, Edwin Land, Samuel Morse)
  2. the arts (e.g., Henry Adams, Louisa May Alcott, John Singleton Copley, Emily Dickinson, Ralph Waldo Emerson, Theodore Geisel, Nathaniel Hawthorne, Oliver Wendell Holmes, Frederick Law Olmsted, Norman Rockwell, Henry David Thoreau, Phyllis Wheatley)
  3. business (e.g., William Filene, Amos Lawrence, Francis Cabot Lowell, An Wang);
  4. education, journalism, and health (e.g., Clara Barton, Horace Mann, William Monroe Trotter)
  5. political leadership (e.g., John Adams, John Quincy Adams, Susan B. Anthony, Edward Brooke, Benjamin Franklin, John F. Kennedy, Paul Revere)

26E3CCA0DFE60131758168A86D17958E.description: Identify the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, and the Bill of Rights as key American documents. (C)

26E380F0DFE60131758068A86D17958E.description:
Explain important political, economic, and military developments leading to and during the American Revolution. (H, C)
  1. the growth of towns and cities in Massachusetts before the Revolution
  2. the Boston Tea Party
  3. the beginning of the Revolution at Lexington and Concord
  4. the Battle of Bunker Hill
  5. Revolutionary leaders such as John Adams, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, and Paul Revere

26E33240DFE60131757F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Puritans and Pilgrims differed and identify early leaders in Massachusetts, such as John Winthrop; describe the daily life, education, and work of the Puritans in the Massachusetts Bay Colony. (H, E, C)

26E2E2A0DFE60131757E68A86D17958E.description:
Identify who the Pilgrims were and explain why they left Europe to seek religious freedom; describe their journey and their early years in the Plymouth Colony. (H, G, C, E)
  1. the purpose of the Mayflower Compact and its principles of self-government
  2. challenges in settling in America
  3. events leading to the first Thanksgiving

26E2A2B0DFE60131757D68A86D17958E.description: Identify the Wampanoags and their leaders at the time the Pilgrims arrived, and describe their way of life. (H, G)

26E26660DFE60131757C68A86D17958E.description: On a map of the United States, locate the New England states (Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Vermont, New Hampshire, Maine) and the Atlantic Ocean. On a map of Massachusetts, locate major cities and towns, Cape Ann, Cape Cod, the Connecticut River, the Merrimack River, the Charles River, and the Berkshire Hills.(G)

26E0EE30DFE60131757768A86D17958E.description: Define barter, give examples of bartering (e.g., trading baseball cards with each other), and explain how money makes it easier for people to get things they want. (E)

26E1A700DFE60131757968A86D17958E.description: Define specialization in jobs and businesses and give examples of specialized businesses in the community. (E)

26E15FE0DFE60131757868A86D17958E.description: Define what a tax is and the purposes for taxes, and with the help of their teachers and parents, give examples of different kinds of taxes (e.g., property, sales, or income taxes). (E)

26E04340DFE60131757568A86D17958E.description: Give examples of the different ways people in a community can influence their local government (e.g., by voting, running for office, or participating in meetings). (C)

26DFFF90DFE60131757468A86D17958E.description: Give examples of why it is necessary for communities to have governments (e.g., governments provide order and protect rights). (C)

26DF7390DFE60131757268A86D17958E.description: Describe the difference between a contemporary map of their city or town and the map of their city or town in the 18th, 19th , or early 20th century. (H, G)

26DF25F0DFE60131757168A86D17958E.description: Use cardinal directions, map scales, legends, and titles to locate places on contemporary maps of New England, Massachusetts, and the local community. (G)

26DEE4A0DFE60131757068A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe local or regional historic artifacts and sites and generate questions about their function, construction, and significance. (H)

26DEA0D0DFE60131756F68A86D17958E.description: Observe visual sources such as historic paintings, photographs, or illustrations that accompany historical narratives, and describe details such as clothing, setting, or action. (H)

26DE5FA0DFE60131756E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of time periods or dates in historical narratives (decade, century, 1600s, 1776) and use them correctly in speaking and writing. (H)

269480E0DFE60131752C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the location and features of places in the immediate neighborhood of the student's home or school. (G)

2693F490DFE60131752A68A86D17958E.description: Put events in their own and their families' lives in temporal order. (H)

  1. Columbus Day

  4. Presidents' Day

26932840DFE60131752768A86D17958E.description: Give examples of how family members, friends, or acquaintances use money directly or indirectly (e.g., credit card or check) to buy things they want. (E)

2692C4E0DFE60131752668A86D17958E.description: Use words relating to work, such as jobs, money, buying, and selling. (E)

269234F0DFE60131752468A86D17958E.description: Give examples that show the meaning of the following concepts: authority, fairness, justice, responsibility, and rules. (C)

2691B270DFE60131752268A86D17958E.description: Tell or show what a map is and what a globe is. (G)

26914F60DFE60131752168A86D17958E.description: Use correctly words and phrases that indicate location and direction, such as up, down, near, far, left, right, straight, back, behind, and in front of. (G)

2690EC90DFE60131752068A86D17958E.description: Use correctly the word because in the context of stories or personal experiences. (H)

2690A4A0DFE60131751F68A86D17958E.description: Use correctly words and phrases related to chronology and time (now, long ago, before, after; morning, afternoon, night; today, tomorrow, yesterday; last or next week, month, year; and present, past, and future tenses of verbs). (H)

26905CD0DFE60131751E68A86D17958E.description: Identify sequential actions, such as first, next, last, in stories and use them to describe personal experiences. (H)

document.title: Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework

299C1C80DFE6013178F968A86D17958E.description: Practice civic skills and dispositions by participating in activities such as simulated public hearings, mock trials, and debates.

299B9E40DFE6013178F868A86D17958E.description: Together with other students, identify a significant public policy issue in the community, gather information about that issue, fairly evaluate the various points of view and competing interests, examine ways of participating in the decision making process about the issue, and draft a position paper on how the issue should be resolved.

299B34E0DFE6013178F768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the arguments that evaluate the functions and values of voluntary participation by citizens in the civil associations that constitute civil society.

299AD990DFE6013178F668A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate decisions about rights of individuals in landmark cases of the United States Supreme Court such as Whitney v. California (1927), Stromberg v. California (1931), Near v. Minnesota (1931), Brandenburg v. Ohio (1969), Texas v. Johnson (1989), and Reno v. American Civil Liberties Union (1997).

299A7EE0DFE6013178F568A86D17958E.description: Identify specific ways for individuals to serve their communities and participate responsibly in civil society and the political process at local, state, and national levels of government.

299A1F30DFE6013178F468A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the meaning and importance of civic dispositions or virtues that contribute to the preservation and improvement of civil society and government.

2999AB60DFE6013178F368A86D17958E.description: Research the platforms of political parties and candidates for state or local government and explain how citizens in the United States participate in public elections as voters and supporters of candidates for public office.

29991A30DFE6013178F268A86D17958E.description: Describe how citizens can monitor and influence local, state, and national government as individuals and members of interest groups.

2998BFF0DFE6013178F168A86D17958E.description: Describe roles of citizens in Massachusetts and the United States, including voting in public elections, participating in voluntary associations to promote the common good, and participating in political activities to influence public policy decisions of government.

29986130DFE6013178F068A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning and responsibilities of citizenship in the United States and Massachusetts.

29980060DFE6013178EF68A86D17958E.description: Roles of Citizens in the United States: Students will explain the idea of citizenship in the United States, describe the roles of United States citizens, and identify and explain the rights and responsibilities of United States citizens. They will also examine civic dispositions conducive to the maintenance and improvement of civil society and government, and describe and demonstrate how citizens can participate responsibly and effectively in the civic and political life of the United States.

299799B0DFE6013178EE68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate, take, and defend a position about whether or not the United States should promote the spread of democracy throughout the world, or in certain parts of the world, or not at all.

299722E0DFE6013178ED68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of sources, including newspapers, magazines, and the internet to identify significant world political, demographic, and environmental developments. Analyze ways that these developments may affect United States foreign policy in specific regions of the world.

2996B100DFE6013178EC68A86D17958E.description: Explain and evaluate participation by the United States government in international organizations.

29964420DFE6013178EB68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate among various governmental and nongovernmental international organizations, and describe their purposes and functions.

2995E880DFE6013178EA68A86D17958E.description: Examine the different forces that influence U.S. foreign policy, including business and labor organizations, interest groups, public opinion, and ethnic and religious organizations.

29958150DFE6013178E968A86D17958E.description: Describe the tools used to carry out United States foreign policy.

29952510DFE6013178E868A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain powers that the United States Constitution gives to the President and Congress in the area of foreign affairs

2994C5E0DFE6013178E768A86D17958E.description: Analyze reasons for conflict among nation states, such as competition for resources and territory, differences in system of government, and religious or ethnic conflicts.

29946640DFE6013178E668A86D17958E.description: Describe how the world is divided politically, and give examples of the ways nation states interact, including trade, tourism, diplomacy, treaties and agreements, and military action.

2993F5D0DFE6013178E568A86D17958E.description: The Relationship of the United States to Other Nations in World Affairs: Students will analyze the interactions between the United States and other nations and evaluate the role of the United States in world affairs.

29937620DFE6013178E468A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate decisions by the United States Supreme Court about the constitutional principle of federalism in cases such as McCulloch v. Maryland (1819), Texas v. White (1869), Alden v. Maine (1999).

29931DE0DFE6013178E368A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate decisions by the United States Supreme Court about the constitutional principles of separation of powers and checks and balances in such landmark cases as Marbury v. Madison (1803), Baker v. Carr (1962), United States v. Nixon (1974), City of Boerne, Texas v. Flores (1997), and Clinton v. City of New York (1998).

2992C2C0DFE6013178E268A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of sources, including newspapers and internet web sites, to identify current state and local legislative issues and examine the influence on the legislative process of political parties, interest groups, grass roots organizations, lobbyists, public opinion, the news media, and individual voters.

29926990DFE6013178E168A86D17958E.description: Compare core documents associated with the protection of individual rights, including the Bill of Rights, the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, and Article I of the Massachusetts Constitution.

29920D30DFE6013178E068A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between a town and a city form of government in Massachusetts, including the difference between a representative and an open-town meeting.

2991AD70DFE6013178DF68A86D17958E.description: Explain the formal process of how a bill becomes a law and define the terms initiative and referendum.

29915120DFE6013178DE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the legal, fiscal, and operational relationships between state and local governments in Massachusetts.

2990F770DFE6013178DD68A86D17958E.description: Trace the evolution of political parties in the American governmental system, and analyze their functions in elections and government at national and state levels of the federal system.

29909C70DFE6013178DC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the functions of departments or agencies of the executive branch in the governments of the United States and the state of Massachusetts.

29903D60DFE6013178DB68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the enumerated and implied powers in the United States Constitution and the Massachusetts Constitution.

298FCF30DFE6013178DA68A86D17958E.description: Explain the functions of the courts of law in the governments of the United States and the state of Massachusetts with emphasis on the principles of judicial review and an independent judiciary.

298F5EF0DFE6013178D968A86D17958E.description: Explain the constitutional principles of federalism, separation of powers among three branches of government, the system of checks and balances, republican government or representative democracy, and popular sovereignty. Provide examples of these principles in the governments of the United States and the state of Massachusetts.

298EE890DFE6013178D868A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe provisions of the United States Constitution and the Massachusetts Constitution that define and distribute powers and authority of the federal or state government.

298E7A60DFE6013178D768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast governments that are unitary, confederate, and federal.

298DE4F0DFE6013178D668A86D17958E.description: Purposes, Principles, and Institutions of Government in the United States of America: Students will explain how purposes, principles, and institutions of government for the American people are established in the United States Constitution and reflected in the Massachusetts Constitution. They will also describe the structures and functions of American constitutional government at national, state, and local levels, and practice skills of citizenship in relationship to their constitutional government.

298D7780DFE6013178D568A86D17958E.description: Analyze and explain ideas about liberty, equality, and justice in American society using documents such as in Reverend Martin Luther King's "I Have A Dream" speech and Letter from Birmingham City Jail (1963), and compare King's ideas to those in such founding-era documents as the Virginia Declaration of Rights (1776), the Declaration of Independence (1776), Massachusetts Declaration of Rights (1780), and the Federalist Papers (1788)

298D18F0DFE6013178D468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast ideas on government of the Federalists and the Anti-Federalists during their debates on ratification of the U.S. Constitution (1787–1788).
