229A1F50DFE601316E4868A86D17958E.description: Integrate knowledge of dance, music, theatre, and visual arts and apply the arts to learning other disciplines
comments:
Examples of this include:
  • using visual arts skills to illustrate understanding of a story read in English language arts or foreign languages;
  • memorizing and singing American folk songs to enhance understanding of history and geography;
  • using short dance sequences to clarify concepts in mathematics.
For example, students examine a variety of percussion instruments, experiment with the different sounds they make, and learn about the cultures in which they were made.
229D9E10DFE601316E5368A86D17958E.description:
When using art materials or handling and viewing artifacts or musical instruments, ask and answer questions such as
  • "What is this made of?"
  • "How does this instrument produce sound?"
  • "Would I design this differently?"
  • "Who first thought of making something like this?"

  • styles of folk and fine arts of immigrant groups from European, African, Latin American, Asian, and Middle Eastern countries
comments: For example, students look at examples of Native American clay containers from the Southwest, and wooden containers from the Northwest and compare the similarities and differences in form and decoration.

229C0240DFE601316E4E68A86D17958E.description: Concepts of Style, Stylistic Influence, and Stylistic Change

229ACEE0DFE601316E4A68A86D17958E.description: When viewing or listening to examples of visual arts, architecture, music, dance, storytelling, and theatre, ask and answer questions such as, "What is the artist trying to say?" "Who made this, and why?" "How does this work make me feel?"

document.title: Massachusetts Curriculum Framework for English Language Arts and Literacy

8140B8C2A99740E88B77F48BEEF4CC9A.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

ABDC5C33FED54F2F87B14BAA0B228887.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

1064E6269D334F1F8A1853C4B63F5B10.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

795DD4DD5CC5431CB34EA08DC05700C4.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

7D27979BCDED4042847599F3C9153410.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

9FF4F409B5D940E79255E5443904467D.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

029619456E2844CA8991E2BD38439FF7.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

F0278CE6AFB3488BA418E51758846D27.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

DDB09DDC77D943278E8CF38E70EFD464.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

83B980CA54254DBB969BF86D20A05D41.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

2193DF200AB54C99BE1760B3831BC6E1.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

9910F402F4FE4E05A21EF02A18934DB2.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

63B99E4259F641D294EE6AE20A86C345.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

9A31285BE87E41B9A86F184B294CE8BC.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

81149488BEDC473497B08468FCF1945A.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

0ACFEB1D60FC4974ACFFD0384997CFD3.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

95CC6215A02A4FB1B7F22A6C04BE0A24.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

6AE19B9C84B544D1B8F571765BBC6BE4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

25694F3C26CB46D6B5DA70AFB89C68D6.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

3A7595B8E4F54D4BAA6EFDE3A6131602.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

5ACBA172C51A4479AEFA4838C8211180.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

8343CE9D9B3142868CF55BFE2BCDAF1B.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

0D8291D399C9419C84DE99B131203FC5.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

3FE8F4CC74074BB585E9CC5E41E3410A.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

7759AC784F9C48588384EBCE8B525AF3.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

B223ED067B9A42AAB89C8D8CB2DB2CCC.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1E463A9A53D840E9B09BF631B9EA03B2.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

8B4F4845E71145899D6369D0A9900360.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

27253BE2A7CC4028A8292639B4FEC165.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

890F1766728B47C086EFDEE8378BA562.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

6E29FD1EE348441881F5942407BFCF02.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EE9CDEC40F0448528E21CB82A99D6D70.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

CA820A0D150646D4A558E5388E67A6C8.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

2AFE1A7966D54F4ABA5C8BBDE7648CF9.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

CB98BFE870E04A5E9B4DCC508DFEB11C.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

CC1B8710531749FF84101C137756A0A2.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

1B9A605621364D69A0241D21E65C38A4.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

0C45F80C5ADB4B4D8CBC53568736F403.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

529813BB12834337AF27D5700922B5F9.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

CBC23F76585F4C8D8EF032D87AB99CA3.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

D36C470E0F8743F891B0F90384022ABC.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

DCBB58D729DC4842A581F66D4543C4DB.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

F2C26515B7C44EF396CBA86EA36CDB87.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

728B25B99E0B455585D4FFB2C6B3820B.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

FAFE48EF998C45DC8480FB878783B9FF.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

B58886D0728542669460162C67C1A91D.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

5A11C80BBDCA48ABBAD59F3E4BB96B87.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

313790A7C23D49358791D77D8E94559C.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

828A470B2C914AAFAE0C3BC11FA108E2.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

A3DB4CEA06DF4713BB096EDF108F537E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

442B53110CCF4B25BDD967C8423A7382.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

308D717B00FC40D198637D0681EC06FD.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

56526F0A9DA54C98A9482C70867B2592.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

598A51030C4742A38C05F129E3DC16AD.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

44242783FF3E468190C84306FBA73BA2.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

B3E79D9A0D434580B8955EABBC64C9E2.description: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.

FE2EB567914442D6A11AD0615225DD77.description: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.

8A9B18694FDB4CC7A52600CF2CFCB13F.description: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

10B62A711975471492CF9A9848AE203C.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

14289699E09F4BE68B8EAECCEE094CDA.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

7E581E8570F642289ABB6CF83E71F5BC.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.

210B7180F14546838B0DCEBBDDC1ACA3.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

E09422C492C649369A3FD4AA48985DC7.description: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.

5B090C040E134B498552C2B5436A8920.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

182E9E71B13A42FCBAB98953F446AB92.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

91F73DEB662448C293FCF93FD6853A59.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.

3B21F01B9E964439B6162AFF1B5A0EA1.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

312696B6A04F4911B9003F4D47F31F9F.description: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.

877BCAFE45AF4C938549BB1A5F2BE334.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.

9EE8833031D9475C81021A7198EBB44D.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7446672F408C44A88CF3A5D0AEF482B1.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

5310C52F753B424CA78DCF17DE4FD261.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

CCA56514B1E44F778B5B8C0EC3D46117.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

3723B83796C64375A0561DEAD9017F51.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

17A0E1C4566E401BAC61D7372AC10314.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

EF5EFD4E8C4C42389ED904ABEEE5C6D7.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

2BE7091A44DA464794F6E49ABA1A1FB7.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

50616BF876DC4A9293DAB99C549D3196.description: Write fiction, personal reflections, poetry, and scripts that demonstrate awareness of literary concepts and genres.

52B4C0DBD2114D4298A8A5E98D74C353.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

601C71A566584EEDAB929DE52A656D2C.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7396E6C5187A46688A31A6168F1682E7.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

EA9711AFE50547B2B63FECECE17F4B67.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

9FA558B1997B46CB94AD144F9215C0F1.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

21F325E72B4B4A1FAEE7D708FD58B7FD.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

F6CCC6C46F284D75A216AAAD3ACA62B1.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

6D23218B32604BCCAE0BACE6EA02742A.description: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.

1DCFE5DA02394DE0B8226861B5DA5406.description: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.

7A344C36624741B1A3D828AA8F8137F1.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

06229BFFEC934D8C80997E181FE6F204.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

44292335EC3344F99083AC63AB62408E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.

0E13700C0CD0424BB05AF5B1D7D901FA.description: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).

010C8DF708AF44EF866CAC1913729A0F.description: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

81EAFC372B0747CAABC7F81CBB7D31E1.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.

4E315B398A34402DA9100925897EE3C8.description: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.

D26FC03428B1481CA7B25765F1EBCC90.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

E7640AED6F6D4DC8829325C0BBBF77DF.description: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

793FC8FBB4494F9EA015DC1C2C0EBB41.description: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

A8E9A3F2902E4CFAA0006656DECBA959.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

A0349E8257D2445C885CACC58ECDCEAB.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

DDA49AA0A89344CA94381AAFE4DC035A.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

87DADB6941374909B07F466AEF85CB07.description: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).

9ECA5E8674954B16A1BF9EF31BFE75D7.description: Identify elements of fiction (e.g., characters, setting, plot, problem, solution) and elements of poetry (e.g., rhyme, rhythm, figurative language, alliteration, onomatopoeia).

49941F70F61B47D69F8C7E8157815BDF.description: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).

2DF825719B704675A150A4638C343C27.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.

697ECDF5C4974046B18778090CC61B5C.description: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.

E95A50C78F2243EB9B1F0C99C3D23B27.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.

B8F804AAF40B4FC8AE1B10E23044BA68.description: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.

69B10F639D2C45FD9E89E4F691F22BB6.description: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.

6059F7FE3C5C4CF28B6335C3880F3E53.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

FD14E301ED104D46AC7E0F3BB2C12E34.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

293E8A5EE053469B902F3DB34A9474DA.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

913FD3EFF3F44B7A856850FCB8B258A9.description: Analyze the meanings of literary texts by drawing on knowledge of literary concepts and genres.

0D015A5FAE5446D58096F61426DD4656.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

9171966B58F1472FB9486C1902FE2E31.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

DC050B56642946BB98475384C7AFAFAC.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

B7129B8F0988460C9253A7484B9A15E2.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

17431ACE665E4112A63598D69BEDB019.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

E1F883D2866E40E1989F399025CB96CD.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

87F87DBAE6A44431B8991B9C0768B1C6.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

C529A875AE0947058F152753097512F4.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

D2B1C5240AB8423885FF5A1C1D7DBE26.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Massachusetts Technology Literacy Standards and Expectations

252C9210DFE60131725968A86D17958E.description: Communicate with other students and other classes using appropriate technology, including e-mail if the district allows it.

252D1600DFE60131725B68A86D17958E.description: Use teacher-developed guidelines to evaluate multimedia presentations for organization, content, design, presentation, and appropriate use of citations.

252CD550DFE60131725A68A86D17958E.description: Create projects that use text and various forms of graphics, audio, and video (with proper citations) to communicate ideas.

252BE930DFE60131725768A86D17958E.description: Use online tools (e.g., e-mail, online discussion forums, blogs, and wikis) to gather and share information collaboratively with other students, if the district allows it.

252B9540DFE60131725668A86D17958E.description: Use content-specific technology tools (e.g., environmental probes, sensors, measuring devices, simulations) to gather and analyze data.

252B5730DFE60131725568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate Internet resources in terms of their usefulness for research.

252B16D0DFE60131725468A86D17958E.description: Perform basic searches on databases (e.g., library card catalogue, encyclopedia) to locate information, using two or more key words and techniques to refine and limit such searches.

252AD6D0DFE60131725368A86D17958E.description: Locate, download, and organize content from digital media collections for specific purposes, citing sources.

252A51D0DFE60131725168A86D17958E.description: Use spreadsheets and other applications to make predictions, solve problems, and draw conclusions.

252A0120DFE60131725068A86D17958E.description: With teacher direction, use appropriate technology tools (e.g., graphic organizer) to define problems and propose hypotheses.

252971A0DFE60131724E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to use technology for research, critical thinking, problem solving, decision making, communication, collaboration, creativity, and innovation.

25292D80DFE60131724D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how hardware and applications can enable people with disabilities to learn.

2528E790DFE60131724C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that some Web sites and search engines may include sponsored commercial links.

2528A230DFE60131724B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze media messages and determine if their purpose is to inform, persuade, or entertain

25285E60DFE60131724A68A86D17958E.description: Work collaboratively online with other students under teacher supervision.

25280D50DFE60131724968A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which technology is used in the workplace and in society.

25272120DFE60131724668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and demonstrate ergonomically sound and safe use of equipment.

2526D4D0DFE60131724568A86D17958E.description: Identify cyber bullying and describe strategies to deal with such a situation.

25268A70DFE60131724468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate safe e-mail practices, recognition of the potentially public exposure of e-mail and appropriate e-mail etiquette (if the district allows student e-mail use).

252629E0DFE60131724368A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the strategies used for the safe and efficient use of computers (e.g., passwords, virus protection software, spam filters, popup blockers).

25276D70DFE60131724768A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe the potential risks and dangers associated with various forms of online communications.

8D46E31B56C54372AEE7248197024EBB.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

4F8AEBE93A2B47DBB37B4C0BF63AAB8E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

4E3CEEB3961E48CD9CD03E9B220CF2D8.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

9E71833D89A94AD6BADAA77EA4FF9482.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

8F09711C431C44E0BBDEDB9FE2DCE45C.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

CB9333C85C2F4A97B1C5DEEAFA59106E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
187C115CE0DA4007A34AA3379AC20A5E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

8931A77C5E124A9FBE894247F05633CD.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

CB2AEAEDDFC1416B9E66B08D00F11A82.description: Explain the purpose of friendship in different stages of the life cycle and describe how friends can support one another in making healthy decisions

C4F12A4D8EC748B5BEA0D3EA6D4E64EF.description: Through the study of Peer Relationships students will

68BA88DD8FAC4312AAD88B3AE76EB400.description: Explain the importance of communication in setting limits in a sexual relationship

17FF25A4D2C64E5394E44BD59D97FADF.description: Describe the influence of the larger social group on individual conduct (such as giving comfort, solving problems, and controlling deviant behavior through enforcing laws and the development of good character in the members of society)

2812819671E4407FB0DB72FF03ED5E7D.description: Contrast the emotional impact on long-term relationships of positive communication (such as active listening, praise, and humor) with negative communication (such as teasing, name calling, bullying)

3FFBB84FDEFD420E8A4F6FA00C0E925F.description: Identify techniques for handling anger and resolving conflicts in the family, friendships, and the workplace, including seeking help from professional and community organizations and faith-based groups

AF7F4973EB3844E8BE0B41121E6E6F74.description: Through the study of Communication students will

comments: Students will learn that relationships with others are an integral part of the human life experience and the factors that contribute to healthy interpersonal relationships, and will acquire skills to enhance and make many of these relationships more fulfilling through commitment and communication.

24E5EBD0DFE6013171C568A86D17958E.description: Identify laws related to child abuse
comments: (Law and Policy. Connects with History & Social Science: Civics and Government)

24E4DA10DFE6013171C268A86D17958E.description: Identify the traits of a healthy family (such as responsibility, communication, trust, loyalty, respect, commitment, love, affirmation, and self-reliance) and explain the interdependence and independence of family members

24E532D0DFE6013171C368A86D17958E.description: Explain the functions, purposes, and social significance of family from various historical periods, including modern times
comments: Students view films that show changes in families in the last 50 years and identify what constants appear (e.g., caring for each other) and what changes appear evident (e.g., role changes in household and parenting tasks)

24E48F90DFE6013171C168A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Decision Making students will

24E44330DFE6013171C068A86D17958E.description: Describe parental practices that encourage literacy in young children
comments: Design a pamphlet summarizing research and activities for parents to promote literacy in their young children. Have an early childhood specialist evaluate the pamphlet and provide feedback to students

24E3F120DFE6013171BF68A86D17958E.description: Describe considerations relevant to becoming a parent (including the various ways of becoming a parent such as foster parenting, adoption, and stepparenting)

24E39A20DFE6013171BE68A86D17958E.description: Identify desirable character traits (such as love, respectfulness, generosity, kindness, and forgiveness) and describe the development of good character, including the role of parents and family in the moral development of children

24E350A0DFE6013171BD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the consequences of teen parenting from the perspectives of the teen mother, teen father, and the parents of the teens

24E30690DFE6013171BC68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate various types of discipline parents might use with children of different ages

24E2B6E0DFE6013171BB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the child-rearing skills (including emotional maturity to nurture children and knowledge of child development stages) and the financial resources needed for parenting
comments: In supervised small groups, students respond to the developmental and health needs of young children in a child care setting and evaluate skills with the supervisor

24E26170DFE6013171BA68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Parenting students will

24E210B0DFE6013171B968A86D17958E.description: Identify steps for getting support or help, including identifying resources for families whose members have special health needs

24E1BA90DFE6013171B868A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Supports students will

comments: Students will gain knowledge about the significance of the family on individuals and society, and will learn skills to support the family, balance work and family life, be an effective parent, and nurture the development of children.

24E117E0DFE6013171B668A86D17958E.description: Explain positive techniques for handling difficult decisions
comments: Students review Department of Public Health pamphlets on working teens and resources, then invite a speaker from this agency to address various conflict resolution strategies in the workplace

24E0C740DFE6013171B568A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which decision-making is influenced by sound character, family, and personal beliefs

24E07C00DFE6013171B468A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Decision Making students will

24E02940DFE6013171B368A86D17958E.description: Identify common mental health disorders (for example, anxiety, schizophrenia, and mood, including depression and bipolar) and treatments (for example, psychological, biomedical)

24DFD390DFE6013171B268A86D17958E.description: Describe the signs of destructive behavior, and identify intervention strategies and kinds of professional intervention
comments: Working with the school counselors, students discuss signs of suicide and to whom to go to for help

24DF87D0DFE6013171B168A86D17958E.description: Describe the influence of gender on identity and self-concept
comments: Students have a class discussion on the influence of group stereotypes about gender roles on identity and self-concept

24DF3C90DFE6013171B068A86D17958E.description: Describe theories of personality development, including identity formation, and differentiate among the concepts of ideal self, public self, and private self

24DEF090DFE6013171AF68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Identity students will

24DEA240DFE6013171AE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze research on health behaviors and brain chemistry and emotional functioning
comments: Students evaluate the latest research on eating breakfast and mood

24DE4F20DFE6013171AD68A86D17958E.description: Identify the factors that help people deal with grief

24DDE670DFE6013171AC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze healthy ways to express emotions and to cope with feelings, including the common causes of stress, its effects on the body, and managing stress

24DD8BA0DFE6013171AB68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Feelings and Emotions students will

comments: Students will acquire knowledge about emotions and physical health, the management of emotions, personality and character development, and social awareness; and will learn skills to promote self-acceptance, make decisions, and cope with stress, including suicide prevention.

Social and Emotional Health includes those aspects of health that are particularly unique to human beings, namely being aware of ourselves, both as individuals and as members of social groups. The knowledge and skills presented in this Strand address and support our ability to interact with others in positive and socially acceptable ways.

24DC6B40DFE6013171A868A86D17958E.description: Explain the laws and relevant court rulings concerning rights about consensual sexual relationships and reproduction (e.g., Roe v. Wade, Bowers v. Hardwick)
comments: (Law and Policy. Connects with History & Social Science: Civics & Government)

24DC1310DFE6013171A768A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain laws about reproductive services
comments: (Law and Policy. Connects with History & Social Science: Civics & Government)

24DB7F10DFE6013171A568A86D17958E.description: Identify resources available for treatment of reproductive health problems

24DB35E0DFE6013171A468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the impact of HIV/AIDS on the community, medical resources, and family

24DAE960DFE6013171A368A86D17958E.description: Identify and distinguish among types and degrees of sexual risk (pregnancy, sexual assault, STIs, including HIV/AIDS)

24DA9960DFE6013171A268A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of communication and setting limits in a sexual relationship

24DA47A0DFE6013171A168A86D17958E.description: Describe proper prenatal care and identify types of birth defects

24D9F7E0DFE6013171A068A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of examination of both genders for HIV and STIs before conception and the risks and precautions of delivery when HIV and STIs are present

24D99840DFE60131719F68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Wellness students will

24D94430DFE60131719E68A86D17958E.description: Identify possible determinants of sexual orientation and analyze the weight of each in light of available research

24D8EDC0DFE60131719D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the effectiveness and consequences of various pregnancy, HIV, and STI prevention methods, including abstinence
comments: Students identify ways to prevent pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections

24D82AE0DFE60131719B68A86D17958E.description: Identify the stages of the male and female reproductive systems over the life cycle

24D7DB00DFE60131719A68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Development students will

comments: Students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to make effective personal decisions that promote their emotional, sexual, and reproductive health.

24D72730DFE60131719868A86D17958E.description: Identify how social and cultural messages about food and eating influence nutrition choices
comments: Students develop and deliver a presentation to the school health advisory council on the links promoted by the media to teens between smoking and nutrition choices, such as weight management

24D6B790DFE60131719768A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze dietary plans, costs, and long-term outcomes of weight management programs

24D667C0DFE60131719668A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Social Influences students will

24D614A0DFE60131719568A86D17958E.description: Identify and practice resource management skills needed to maintain and improve nutritional health
comments: Working within a budget, students plan a week of nutritious meals for a family of four. Prepare one of these meals and evaluate for nutritional value, taste, and aesthetic appeal

24D54720DFE60131719368A86D17958E.description: Identify the effects of food preparation techniques on the nutritional value of the food

24D4D390DFE60131719268A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Safe and Adequate Food Supply students will

24D463E0DFE60131719168A86D17958E.description: Describe the nutritional needs and outcomes associated with life stages (prenatal through late adulthood)

24D3FE30DFE60131719068A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships among dietary intake (including nutritional supplements), eating behaviors, physical activity, and emotional health
comments: Students develop an exercise schedule and plan and prepare a menu for a meal that includes foods for people who need to gain or lose weight

24D38BC0DFE60131718F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how food choices are influenced by availability, individual and family preferences, media, and background, and identify healthy foods within various social groups

24D32840DFE60131718E68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Improving Nutrition students will

comments: Students will gain the knowledge and skills to select a diet that supports health and reduces the risk of illness and future chronic diseases.

24D25350DFE60131718C68A86D17958E.description: Define the functions of leadership in team sports (increasing motivation, efficiency, and satisfaction)
comments: Students participate in an adventure activity in which they must work together to accomplish a group goal. At completion, based upon observations and student performance, self-report on contributions

24D1DBF0DFE60131718B68A86D17958E.description: Apply safe practices, rules, procedures, and sportsmanship etiquette in physical activity settings, including how to anticipate potentially dangerous consequences and outcomes of participation in physical activity

24D15170DFE60131718A68A86D17958E.description: Understand how activity participation patterns are likely to change throughout life and identify strategies to deal with those changes, including a plan for life-long wellness

24D0D7F0DFE60131718968A86D17958E.description: Identify life-management skills and protective factors that contribute to achieving personal wellness health goals, including researching, evaluating, and implementing strategies to manage personal wellness, monitor progress, and revise plans
comments: Students work with school health services to create personal risk profiles. After completing the forms, use research-based strategies to develop a plan to reduce risks identified. Implement the plan, determine points at which to monitor, do the monitoring, revise plan, and assess at a later point

24D06820DFE60131718868A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Personal and Social Competency students will

24CFFB50DFE60131718768A86D17958E.description: Meet developmentally appropriate health-related fitness benchmarks

24CF88D0DFE60131718668A86D17958E.description: Students participate daily in any physical activity and keep a journal for one-month recording specifics (such as aerobic endurance, flexibility, and strength) and description of physical and psychological states before, during, and after participation. At the end of the month, summarize with personal recommendations regarding the amount and regularity of activity, as well as beliefs about future commitment to a daily or weekly schedule of exercise

24CF1C20DFE60131718568A86D17958E.description: Identify the components of physical fitness and the factors involved in planning and evaluating fitness programs for individuals at different stages of the life cycle

24CEAEC0DFE60131718468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate exercises in strength training, cardiovascular activities, and flexibility training

24CE3F80DFE60131718368A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Fitness students will

24CDDE70DFE60131718268A86D17958E.description: Apply concepts about sequential motor learning and development, biomechanics, exercise physiology, and sports psychology

24CD7EC0DFE60131718168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate activities for warming up and cooling down before and after aerobic exercise

24CD1FA0DFE60131718068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate developmentally appropriate competence (basic skills, strategies, and rules) in many and proficiency in a few movement forms and motor skills (team sports, aquatics, individual/dual sports, outdoor pursuits, self-defense, dance, and gymnastics)

24CCC600DFE60131717F68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Motor Skill Development students will

comments: Students will, by repeated practice, acquire and refine a variety of manipulative, locomotor, and non-locomotor movement skills, and will utilize principles of training and conditioning, will learn biomechanics and exercise physiology, and will apply the concept of wellness to their lives.

24CC1740DFE60131717D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how both heredity (including congenital factors) and the environment influence growth and development

249A95C0DFE60131717C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the growth patterns and body changes within human beings throughout the life cycle (from prenatal through late adulthood), including critical periods in growth and development
comments: For example, students design a dietary and/or exercise plan for each stage of life, giving a rationale for the choices

249A3180DFE60131717B68A86D17958E.description: Through the study of the Life Cycle students will

2499C230DFE60131717A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of behavior and environment on failure of body systems (nervous, muscular, skeletal, circulatory, respiratory, endocrine, and excretory systems)
comments: For example, students design a maze or circuitry system that represents the human body. Include both obstacles and enhancements to functioning

249969B0DFE60131717968A86D17958E.description: Through the study of Body Systems students will

comments: Students will learn the basic characteristics of physical growth and development, including body functions and systems throughout the life cycle, and will acquire skills to promote and maintain positive growth and development.

Physical Health includes those aspects of health that are often the most salient in our immediate lives and related closely to the natural progression inherent in human development. The knowledge and skills presented are the foundation for individual control over many of the factors related to a healthy lifestyle. The areas covered share common goals in their emphasis and focus on building and maintaining healthy habits.

document.title: Massachusetts Curriculum Framework for English Language Arts and Literacy

D801E58241A64AD7BE18E7E6B5BFD3CC.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

3BA14B9431CC44819C8F5DEC0CF6088A.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

3E3895D09B0842F994F5045F9575FA39.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

ACDFBF198E9D4F89AE4DF99EE1A0FD1C.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

629BEC640A6C4914B91219B656D184F0.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

BD54566A9F0B49128BBE2991CCA1254B.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

5E563743922B4722B4E285C1F880E84F.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

3AF85A4277354F5D84B7CE3A4931E5A1.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

812E5E8ECD8545478B00E103320BBBE1.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DED7568A24BD49B8B5F7C4E2C5E8F8FB.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

935AB82FFF3649D2B7A9D1B4A5A41983.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

25022CCF79184CAEAC187458DA714379.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

94DA11DF967E4B1092798C8E1F675C7B.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

985770559FF34C76BCA083C60E3072DC.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.

352A1BB7984B41F9949209F595AE81D0.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

21E073C170B14EF0B9D2772106CD03B7.description: Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

F449D559ACBC42C9916AD3660FD29658.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

5633AF58C1634D68897FACF6EE0221F9.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

5EE76C2E1F29471EB4FB98D89535768B.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

301DD7FCD04A46BDBD10301CF041F4E4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

F16C1CAA68AC4C4B98BBD8BA6EE68921.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7810B6B85E10495D9298FE118A604AE5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

10FEF3E98A7541618850CAF02ED9B725.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

EAB7314564604C1A9E900E2D16C7E569.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

B8B6F08602B64E2C92EE7A25D42D5A80.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

6347B7DBC1DF4F749A2A5B7728369E4D.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

38CA8AC8AE7C4514ADFE656A715D5461.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

0C81140713C8422AA6A919DEBE69C85A.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

609A1466BA1C4FCA805803F34D78F61B.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.

BB44A48094F749BAB0E85F66D3C205AC.description: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

33357A8116004DA894AA27FF1E91EC36.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

0AF2FAAD5C444CEAA426603164ECA551.description: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.

73C296CA71414BA9BB960AF98373255E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.

9ECD516289FC4CA6BB80EBCD3982F950.description: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

F14622CA120A4FAFA3886024B7B41234.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

7CDA5A7EB7794869A650B1866124FF2D.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

DBEBFA9CFA344074BC129BEFD1061C9D.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

4AD5B5293AB2405581C516D96DFFC423.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

21CB861997D54239B67D2A8906F5B37A.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

2B0307DCABB7470386F01BDDE378A687.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

F6567FE3FBFA4CA3BB1228BDA20C730F.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

203A43ACB1D34EC28E5D9443C8D503CA.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

62F40C6B07EA438C8488A327797CE6B4.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

E3DC2E2EDA034C89927C23F23BD6B2F3.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

64AA460BF8794067A0686022D52B8EB9.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

E414684AA9F84839A0F405912EE11F18.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4829FFC48767493A9B2751A80E4DC85F.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

28BFBB3F537E4089B567AF514FE52A9F.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

A4A3820FED104977BC472AF84E0D6D9B.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4C630433C3CC452499BC14DD3809B909.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

3F7341FB130C4C2FA3BE1982AB7E679A.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

79F78CE8B4BB4E9BA5677C7A77B02308.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

679E9D043FBC4DE78F3242C5635C8000.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

CA8C799F68DE4E088B98CA79875A0258.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

5FDBD147AEB14DF689CB665F0800B0D7.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

E621D49657F1445F8841445D80597740.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

19E7DE52AB054822B7E5E320B45C3107.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

44BDD452A6E246829C133E37DF5BFE0E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

6179FD2611D94BA09928E2BE59BE9B54.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

22151187D008490F9A7287EC19D2C030.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

5CFD5D5C07D14A6AAFD3D278BBA0BE9D.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

53F47D91120F499C8125F9F79568AF1E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

4B75D59F06374D77B45595EF7EEAF732.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

6A6FE9101B1A423EB9D23F9435B1BD81.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

18016302A66D437C9184E4FC0B6D5A7A.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

A5A6E978EC094E1DA9703DCA71B292F9.description: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

79CB5819264D4056A54D98E25F2D1ACD.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

E555C559E8A146AE9182B46383448FB7.description: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not").

26741FFBA8C64FBEBAA06527F32CAC42.description: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres [e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories] in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics").

6DD089543B484B90991E0CC7A87C1142.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

064B7E361B354F60A19E100C8D2FC410.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.

FF9281C45D734241BD803822862F0FE2.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

A861ED105D9C4C4CB8AED0622FA76AE8.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4A46FB1C631E41298601DC0F113FF15B.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of three pages in a single sitting.

CCBE7FB263F54A2EAEDD5277E9390D31.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

277F0D71ADFC441CBEEF406DF46FF238.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
