Clarification Statements:
  • Examples of areas to compare can include temperate forest, desert, tropical rain forest, grassland, arctic, and aquatic.
  • Specific animal and plant names in specific areas are not expected.

8BE01A18E401435091092D36D14B9B5C.description: Develop and use models to compare how plants and animals depend on their surroundings and other living things to meet their needs in the places they live.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Animals need food, water, air, shelter, and favorable temperature; plants need sufficient light, water, minerals, favorable temperature, and animals or other mechanisms to disperse seeds.

ABE3B2727DBB416195CBA42F76FB9C00.description: Observe how blowing wind and flowing water can move Earth materials from one place to another and change the shape of a landform.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Examples of types of landforms can include hills, valleys, river banks, and dunes.

54E01028EF5144159AD57D27FD929283.description: Use examples obtained from informational sources to explain that water is found in the ocean, rivers and streams, lakes and ponds, and may be solid or liquid.

F61DCBBD8D1A4587B596A7EEA2636AF7.description: Map the shapes and types of landforms and bodies of water in an area.
comments:
Clarification Statements:
  • Examples of types of landforms can include hills, valleys, river banks, and dunes.
  • Examples of water bodies can include streams, ponds, bays, and rivers.
  • Quantitative scaling in models or contour mapping is not expected.

43AF6C11BDF14501AEB5D4C70DD02917.description: Investigate and compare the effectiveness of multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
comments:
Clarification Statements:
  • Solutions to be compared could include different designs of dikes and windbreaks to hold back wind and water, and different designs for using shrubs, grass, and trees to hold back the land.
  • Solutions can be generated or provided.

F878F5119B9F4584A5D7DE2F4A8069EF.description: Evaluate relevant design features that must be considered in building a model or prototype of a solution to a given design problem.

F5B5E13AC96043FA89AC18F8D27E1B5B.description: Plan and carry out tests of one or more design features of a given model or prototype in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify which features need to be improved. Apply the results of tests to redesign a model or prototype.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Examples of design features can include materials, size, shape, and weight.

7401703115384EAFA60A53212771A364.description: Develop and compare multiple ways to transfer information through encoding, sending, receiving, and decoding a pattern.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Examples of solutions could include drums sending coded information through sound waves, using a grid of 1s and 0s representing black and white to send information about a picture, and using Morse code to send text.

693E15CFC699453D884B9EC8F78A909A.description: Develop a model to describe that light must reflect off an object and enter the eye for the object to be seen.
comments:
State Assessment Boundary:
  • Specific colors reflected and seen, the cellular mechanisms of vision, angles of incidence and reflection, or how the retina works are not expected in state assessment.

A1D77FF8AB874D9A90FE4E2700A7A7C9.description: Develop a model of a simple mechanical wave (including sound) to communicate that waves (a) are regular patterns of motion along which energy travels, and (b) can cause objects to move.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Examples of models could include diagrams, analogies, and physical models.
State Assessment Boundary:
  • Interference effects, electromagnetic waves, or non-periodic waves are not expected in state assessment.

9C23B97D5C964D649B8A381066586E0F.description: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

02AFBC5C9CB54612A32001F8CF0F5EFB.description: Apply scientific principles of energy and motion to test and refine a device that converts kinetic energy to electrical energy or uses stored energy to cause motion or produce light or sound.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Sources of stored energy can include water in a bucket or a weight suspended at a height, and a battery.

EB51BB4A52C4445F92EBCD11CB2B9F92.description: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Changes in energy can include a change in the object's motion, position, and the generation of heat and/or sound.
State Assessment Boundary:
  • Analysis of forces or quantitative measurements of energy are not expected in state assessment.

302444EA33684723AA3DFAA79FF6A2E3.description: Make observations to show that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Evidence of energy being transferred can include vibrations felt a small distance from a source, a solar-powered toy that moves when placed in direct light, warming a metal object on one end and observing the other end getting warm, and a wire carrying electric energy from a battery to light a bulb.
State Assessment Boundary:
  • Quantitative measurements of energy are not expected in state assessment.

3FA738D36FAD43679E90EBCBFD9A1882.description: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
comments:
State Assessment Boundaries:
  • State assessment will be limited to analysis of kinetic energy.
  • Accounting for mass, quantitative measures of changes in the speed of an object, or any precise or quantitative definition of energy are not expected in state assessment.

25846EF441494A5D97000E64A1BB1C54.description: Construct an argument that animals and plants have internal and external structures that support their survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
comments:
Clarification Statements:
  • Animal structures can include legs, wings, fins, feathers, trunks, claws, horns, antennae, eyes, ears, nose, heart, stomach, lung, brain, and skin.
  • Plant structures can include leaves, roots, stems, bark, branches, flowers, fruit, and seeds.
State Assessment Boundary:
  • State assessment will be limited to macroscopic structures.

E2852304065F4AE4854A03077EE2C574.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

E99709ABA7024F6C9D01A6B00972B980.description: Evaluate different solutions to reduce the impacts of a natural event such as an earthquake, blizzard, or flood on humans.
comments:
Clarification Statement:
  • Examples of solutions could include an earthquake-resistant building or a constructed wetland to mediate flooding.

42939F01FFCF41ADA78F06F9777DA215.description: Obtain information to describe that energy and fuels humans use are derived from natural resources and that some energy and fuel sources are renewable and some are not.
comments:
Clarification Statements:
  • Examples of renewable energy resources could include wind energy, water behind dams, tides, and sunlight.
  • Non-renewable energy resources are fossil fuels and nuclear materials.

71E2064315B9415FB72907FAD304F226.description: Analyze and interpret maps of Earth's mountain ranges, deep ocean trenches, volcanoes, and earthquake epicenters to describe patterns of these features and their locations relative to boundaries between continents and oceans.

03815C09A6F34374880EFB8E1F3FD74C.description: Make observations and collect data to provide evidence that rocks, soils, and sediments are broken into smaller pieces through mechanical weathering and moved around through erosion by water, ice, wind, and vegetation.
comments:
Clarification Statements:
  • Mechanical weathering processes can include frost wedging, abrasion, and tree root wedging.
  • Erosion can include movement by blowing wind, flowing water, and moving ice.
State Assessment Boundary:
  • Chemical processes are not expected in state assessment.

F00FA1BAA1B142CC836D0C13BFDF9116.description: Use evidence from a given landscape that includes simple landforms and rock layers to support a claim about the role of erosion or deposition in the formation of the landscape over long periods of time.
comments:
Clarification Statements:
  • Examples of evidence and claims could include rock layers with shell fossils above rock layers with plant fossils and no shells, indicating a change from deposition on land to deposition in water over time; and, a canyon with rock layers in the walls and a river in the bottom, indicating that a river eroded the rock over time.
  • Examples of simple landforms can include valleys, hills, mountains, plains, and canyons.
  • Focus should be on relative time.
State Assessment Boundary:
  • Specific details of the mechanisms of rock formation or specific rock formations and layers are not expected in state assessment.

document.title: Massachusetts Digital Literacy and Computer Science Curriculum Framework

40FD46B29ABB4B83941A911673A528BD.description: Individually and collaboratively use data from a simulation to answer a question.

C1E4F50E23824F038BFFB0D3E74171D7.description: Identify the concepts, features, and behaviors illustrated by a simulation (e.g., object motion, weather, ecosystem, predator/prey) and those that were not included.

FC41E7FC801C4C80946A0D647FBDE6DB.description: Individually and collaboratively create a simple model of a system (e.g., water cycle, solar system) and explain what the model shows and does not show.

C7FD335E2DF945C1808A3CA04DB9D803.description: Recognize that programs need known starting values (e.g., set initial score to zero in a game).

2932B42E24474EFCB5926C11E9DCC9C5.description: Use interactive debugging to detect and correct simple program errors.

2774F365543640798A04071CBCA7737D.description: Use arithmetic operators, conditionals, and repetition in programs.

12C707CF0DB546E98189E677E965906B.description: Individually and collaboratively create, test, and modify a program in a graphical environment (e.g., block-based visual programming language).

B6A03804536A488782FEF3D672A3DA8F.description: Describe examples of databases from everyday life (e.g., library catalogs, school records, telephone directories, contact lists).

D832C44BE42E4FB9A12E998867E0B706.description: Detect and correct logical errors in various algorithms (e.g., written, mapped, live action, or digital).

C0D7D300DBF34C64A39F8557802F83A5.description: Individually and collaboratively create an algorithm to solve a problem (e.g., move a character/robot/person through a maze).

547F08188AC34ED7A70E7DB496CC94E8.description: Use logical reasoning to predict outcomes of an algorithm.

666C18A5E90F45079F33DD78144ABA56.description: Recognize that different solutions exist for the same problem (or sub-problem).

3B4215D319204378A1EBA849811651BA.description: Define an algorithm as a sequence of instructions that can be processed by a computer.

144800E17BD948ACB4874708F4C6877E.description: Make a list of sub-problems to consider, while addressing a larger problem.

E30A4F2E700448249E9FD764453AD790.description: Organize information in different ways to make it more useful/relevant (e.g., sorting, tables).

5ADDFD49D0F747C59224559CA4573B3C.description: Use numbers or letters to represent information in another form (e.g., secret codes, Roman numerals, abbreviations).

DED1873C3B3045A1ADB04112DF8A1460.description: Identify common services (e.g., driving directions apps that access remote map services, digital personal assistants that access remote information services).

4E3A26CF783E4967921675298F97392B.description: Recognize that there are many sources of and means for accessing information within a network (e.g., websites, e-mail protocols, search engines)

BC956C9E413746FD837B70EB47B86F11.description: Define and explain why devices are numbered/labeled in networks (e.g., the World Wide Web Uniform Resource Locator [URL], the Internet Protocol [IP] address, the Machine Access Code [MAC]).

314C39B2F1A04E1592F983269BFF032C.description: Describe the need for authentication of users and devices as it relates to access permissions, privacy, and security.

1C80E040648B4721AF7674B55AD6CD2B.description: Describe how a network is made up of a variety of components and identify the common components (e.g., links, nodes, networking devices).

F867A801A3F642A78EB1EE2FC222DC07.description: Explain how hardware and applications (e.g., Global Positioning System [GPS] navigation for driving directions, text-to-speech translation, language translation) can enable everyone, including people with disabilities, to do things they could not do otherwise.

E1479A30B50843CDAA6D61182C666810.description: Identify and explain that some computing functions are always active (e.g., locations function on smart phones).

7FE5BE6F99D44B5187AE4FDBAEB0F747.description: Describe the differences between hardware and software.

7C1B0944DB1B4F1CBD2A0E6D95CF16CC.description: Identify and solve simple hardware and software problems that may occur during everyday use (e.g., power, connections, application window or toolbar).

16C6F2FE51DF4FB7BB08051A4503673A.description: Demonstrate an appropriate level of proficiency (connect and record data, print, send command, connect to Internet, search) in using a range of computing devices (e.g., probes, sensors, printers, robots, computers).

5E68D923B661496D97FFD436F4F4DD5B.description: Describe the function and purpose of various input and output devices (e.g., monitor, keyboard, speakers, controller, probes, sensors, Bluetooth transmitters, synthesizers).

187799471EC24B10938D0A02032D710F.description: Identify a broad range of computing devices (e.g., computers, smart phones, tablets, robots, e-textiles) and appropriate uses for them.

676B1CD04E3140F6AACB1202E298D8FB.description: Provide basic source information (e.g., Uniform Resource Locator [URL], date accessed) for non-text-based sources (e.g., images, audio, video).

E7B26F535B5F481AB624A52F4B91E811.description: Cite text-based sources using a school- or district-adopted format.

9B9E079DD38945C78E8A59FA98B5E12A.description: Create an artifact that answers a research question and clearly communicates thoughts and ideas.

9027A64668A34E1792978487BE7AFB92.description: Gather and organize information from digital sources by quoting, paraphrasing, and/or summarizing.

EA3C312DDB61401191D765B61251DDC3.description: Evaluate digital sources for accuracy, relevancy, and appropriateness.

E6EFAA95FA9E49D8BCDE277BB7CFD1B5.description: Perform searches to locate information using two or more key words and techniques to refine and limit such searches.

136F01BF842E47598112DCD62F072992.description: Identify digital information sources to answer research questions (e.g., online library catalog, online encyclopedias, databases, websites).

97BB5CAB12714AA69F5C6FC87B307BC7.description: Collaborate through online digital tools under teacher supervision.

1F5974D1BD5D4AB79BF1B94888606C77.description: Communicate key ideas and details individually or collaboratively in a way that informs, persuades, and/or entertains using digital tools and media-rich resources.

72E62959CDA744B598C8D7ACCDD2195F.description: Use digital tools (local and online) to manipulate and publish multimedia artifacts.

A1DFC571755B4F18838E1D3E9F499C5C.description: Navigate between local, networked, or online/cloud environments and transfer files between each (upload/download).

11A373C81C8D4D28AE03F89C48A4B553.description: Type five words-per-minute times grade level (e.g., for Grade 5, type 25 words/minute).

8F80C87048B5436186D72FA98556FCA4.description: Identify the impact of social media and cyberbullying on individuals, families, and society.

B3C4CD5F35E4427982A6C32A1DC4A500.description: Identify resources in the community that can give people access to technology (e.g., libraries, community centers, education programs, schools, hardware/software donation programs).

72DA7DB321EA49F28A402E68A07296DD.description: Use critical thinking to explain how access to technology helps empower individuals and groups (e.g., gives them access to information, the ability to communicate with others around the world, allows them to buy and sell things).

5170CC8533954925B5B23CA2F7946196.description: Define the digital divide as unequal access to technology on the basis of differences, such as income, education, age, and geographic location.

41926FD1DA9449B6AA69F98BF64D65CD.description: Explain why websites, digital resources, and artifacts may include advertisements and collect personal information.

DFD1D94D18E840DF85FBB6C5C2FDC40C.description: Explain the different forms of web advertising (e.g., search ads, pay-per-click ads, banner ads, targeted ads, in-game ads, e-mail ads).

CD07238FFFB34BE1A73DF5422B1D2D3B.description: Explain that laws exist (e.g., Section 508, Telecommunication Act of 1996) that help ensure that people with disabilities can access electronic and information technology.

FA2F3A9B7A6142F082935533B96281F5.description: Describe the purpose of copyright and the possible consequences for inappropriate use of digital artifacts that are protected by copyright.

DE2E5CEC99F443BA80786CA7474E53F9.description: Explain the guidelines for the fair use of downloading, sharing, or modifying of digital artifacts.

01AD01153A184B6589FBC5A8EA4A710F.description: Describe the difference between digital artifacts that are open or free and those that are protected by copyright.

6E79B0729CBD466D87EB55FA74F1CF83.description: Demonstrate responsible use of computers, peripheral devices, and resources as outlined in school rules (Acceptable Use Policy [AUP]).

AAC4F59B640A4187A095C85D1CBD647D.description: Explain that if you encounter cyberbullying or other inappropriate content, you should immediately tell a responsible adult (e.g., teacher, parent).

16A39228E71044D5AAECB6AB7C839A2B.description: Identify different types of cyberbullying (e.g., harassment, flaming, excluding people, outing, and impersonation).

5D358CC1790545CDA576165A27543B79.description: Describe ways to employ safe practices and avoid the potential risks/dangers associated with various forms of online communications, downloads, linking, Internet purchases, advertisements, and inappropriate content within constrained environments.

185B339E51CE4585BDEA652B89DC425C.description: Explain the proper use and operation of security technologies (e.g., passwords, virus protection software, spam filters, popup blockers, cookies).

00111F09AFDA40DB97C181F1F2EDEE7E.description: Identify appropriate and inappropriate uses of technology when posting to social media, sending e-mail or texts, and browsing the Internet.

403B607ECDF24F47AB36472EF32D078A.description: Describe the threats to safe and efficient use of devices (e.g., SPAM, spyware, phishing, viruses) associated with various forms of technology use (e.g., downloading and executing software programs, following hyperlinks, opening files).

40BAEF603F6B4AF5A39A140679D92F5D.description: Describe how to use proper ergonomics (e.g., body position, lighting, positioning of equipment, taking breaks) when using devices.

document.title: Massachusetts Digital Literacy and Computer Science Curriculum Framework

F50E58D4775E4142ABDC91A65F6D5264.description: Form a model from a hypothesis generated from research and run a simulation to collect and analyze data to test that hypothesis.

A375D68F7F234F0C9C4ACD00D8CC94B1.description: Create models and simulations to help formulate, test, and refine hypotheses.

785FA39355DB41AE8649F7B00E41FF47.description: Engage in systematic testing and debugging methods to ensure program correctness.

2F97E7A5A07D4641AB478F7DC68C7D43.description: Use an iterative design process, including learning from making mistakes, to gain a better understanding of the problem domain.

D7FBD4624641487C999A877F3FF7194E.description: Analyze trade-offs among multiple approaches to solve a given problem (e.g., space/time performance, maintainability, correctness, elegance).

F00C58458C3A4D55952FE066720888CD.description: Select the appropriate data structure to represent information for a given problem (e.g., records, arrays, lists).

25D5DF48A107453D89610E40050ABAD2.description: Decompose a problem by defining functions which accept parameters and produce return values.

C425A3B9504B4006B3CB11B8DED75E8D.description: Use a development process in creating a computational artifact that leads to a minimum viable product and includes reflection, analysis, and iteration (e.g., a data-set analysis program for a science and engineering fair, capstone project that includes a program, term research project based on program data).

51B07B7E9F0E46218EFDF5EF8AE9E29A.description: Identify different problems (e.g., large or multipart problems, problems that need specific expertise, problems that affect many constituents) that can benefit from collaboration when processing and analyzing data to develop new insights and knowledge.

291A162AD2C14C88A17F68C646954345.description: Create an appropriate multidimensional data structure that can be filtered, sorted, and searched (e.g., array, list, record).

14CE07EF9161468A9A9906FC7358F7B7.description: Describe how data types, structures, and compression in programs affect data storage and quality (e.g., digital image file sizes are affected by resolution and color depth).

925E1735CA58465CBADC097A6A04C64C.description: Explain the concept of quality of service (e.g., security, availability, performance) for services providers (e.g., online storefronts that must supply secure transactions for buyer and seller).

5D303CE36CF64F5A89A33C3C2A45A65D.description: Compare the value of using an existing service versus building the equivalent functionality (e.g., using a reference search engine versus creating a database of references for a project).

1A0A455781674A648EC8344EE10AD439.description: Apply strategies for identifying and solving routine hardware and software problems that occur in everyday life (e.g., update software patches, virus scan, empty trash, run utility software, close all programs, reboot, use help sources).

82D47B8FCE6A4A96BAE8B00F2DFE9629.description: Select computing devices (e.g., probe, sensor, tablet) to accomplish a real-world task (e.g., collecting data in a field experiment) and justify the selection.

B3F545B3FB4049D2B392100D0D9507E0.description: Gather, organize, analyze, and synthesize information using a variety of digital tools.

357526496C9E4AC4AFED86306F3057FB.description: Evaluate digital sources needed to solve a given problem (e.g., reliability, point of view, relevancy).

198D4660055C4D7592D4E1A6BEC00D1D.description: Perform advanced searches to locate information and/or design a data-collection approach to gather original data (e.g., qualitative interviews, surveys, prototypes, simulations).

EE1C4B4467BE464CAF52ED44737B01B9.description: Generate, evaluate, and prioritize questions that can be researched through digital resources or tools.

C734F41E8B9443A39542A72495D7B558.description: Collaborate on a substantial project with outside experts or others through online digital tools (e.g., science fair project, community service project, capstone project).

B6DFC8D2C4064BACB0056EFE320EC4D2.description: Communicate and publish key ideas and details to a variety of audiences using digital tools and media-rich resources.

6FC3893807A24985A4FF6559B6F302D3.description: Select digital tools or resources based on their efficiency and effectiveness to use for a project or assignment, and justify the selection.

FE50BAB8D3EF4B45AC13028C84633EBF.description: Use digital tools to design and develop a significant digital artifact (e.g., multipage website, online portfolio, simulation).

FBF67844F05245C78553443EE36E26B2.description: Discuss the social and economic implications associated with malicious hacking, software piracy, and cyber terrorism.

A5E66844283B4FB28F95E15D7D7235A8.description: Analyze the impact of values and points of view that are presented in media messages (e.g., racial, gender, political).

43D8592360454E4EA81898D5C0111A58.description: Identify ways to use technology to support lifelong learning.

D095AF6006BD4D79BCF235ECA089A96A.description: Cultivate a positive web presence (e.g., digital resume, portfolio, social media).

A8221E814ABB42E8BCA5A1B6110689B2.description: Analyze the beneficial and harmful effects of computing innovations (e.g., social networking, delivery of news and other public media, intercultural communication).

D568C259753642278E2F946BC35D85B6.description: Describe the role that assistive technology can play in people's lives.

D7DBAB36C3594C049FE22C3D7F7E44D7.description: Discuss the impact of computing technology on business and commerce (e.g., automated tracking of goods, automated financial transaction, e-commerce, cloud computing).

F4828FC9735442A680B936D99163C182.description: Explain the impact of the digital divide on access to critical information.

BAC6CEB207E14C0295789CAC3BE44F11.description: Interpret software license agreements and application permissions.

A79FC8D685C643FDBAF27D194631AFE8.description: Discuss the legal and ethical implications associated with malicious hacking and software piracy.

BA2F2BAD222C4BA0B544677C2E545316.description: Identify computer-related laws and analyze their impact on digital privacy, security, intellectual property, network access, contracts, and consequences of sexting and harassment.

005F91868C9340269AFE0BA4A930B565.description: Apply strategies for managing negative peer pressure and encouraging positive peer pressure.

4AF762AEEAB944AC8990030CA1197732.description: Explain safe practices when collaborating online, including how to anticipate potentially dangerous situations.

1376203F0EEA435595820B719E2DE1DB.description: Evaluate and design an ergonomic work environment.

document.title: Massachusetts Digital Literacy and Computer Science Curriculum Framework

DE108E9C951B4D3F9403C2AE7E5DAE7A.description: Individually and collaboratively compare algorithms to solve a problem, based on a given criteria (e.g., time, resource, accessibility).

6C7A8A3A053E44D7AB896842DA0C6700.description: Select and use data-collection technology (e.g., probes, handheld devices, geographic mapping systems) to individually and collaboratively gather, view, organize, analyze, and report results for content-related problems.

1A10617CD0844EA49AED9FE7B5FEB2D6.description: Perform a variety of operations such as sorting, filtering, and searching in a database to organize and display information in a variety of ways such as number formats (scientific notation and percentages), charts, tables, and graphs.

596C5A52550A40F3BFEF22B75B271455.description: Describe how computers store, manipulate, and transfer data types and files (e.g., integers, real numbers, Boolean Operators) in a binary system.

DA1E95F0186F428C9E64AFAD1C85016A.description: Demonstrate that numbers can be represented in different base systems (e.g., binary, octal, and hexadecimal) and text can be represented in different ways (e.g., American Standard Code for Information Interchange [ASCII]).

FD5EC11CEAB7425E806C2162F06F1559.description: Individually and collaboratively decompose a problem and create a sub-solution for each of its parts (e.g., video game, robot obstacle course, making dinner).

50F5CBEAFA9B41C78334CF149C06E218.description: Use logical reasoning to predict outputs given varying inputs.

68BAD41478A442B5924E27510C7B4CA1.description: Design solutions that use repetition and conditionals.

975F4BC26A5947FBAD313F5455E10E8F.description: Describe how data is abstracted by listing attributes of everyday items to represent, order and compare those items (e.g., street address as an abstraction for locations; car make, model, and license plate number as an abstraction for cars).

29F5BED3FB5344049C0DB03AED21FA17.description: Describe the main functions of an operating system.

84DB801C25E8436EB36EA7D29E19BE43.description: Use digital citation tools to cite sources using a school- or district-adopted format (e.g., Modern Language Association [MLA]), including proper citation for all text and non-text sources (e.g., images, audio, video).

DF48FB0C54FB40229CBE47AFCD4FD169.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

71A8C90940C748E5828AA9D4FD42B6C7.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of how-to books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

4D8395D4B9CF4C269EFEE392EF0FFFE0.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D395084D49244E4CAC5AFDEB6584BEDF.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

B41472F7294E439D805F7B36820DC465.description: Demonstrate the ability to choose and use appropriate vocabulary.

773272F1F6F34FDCB395CDB91B182EB3.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

2947EE7AEBAE4DBB9CCBD944A774ADB5.description: Produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

473FB1C4C1714AA3A6260027CE1116BF.description: For poems, use rhyming words and words that repeat long or short vowel sounds to create structure

E49891A65D0E4D7E8F3CAAD8998DC0D8.description: Write narratives in prose or poem form that recount two or more appropriately sequenced events or experiences, include some details about what happened or was experienced, use temporal words to signal order where appropriate, and provide some sense of closure.

051BA9BB5FA341CDAB3ADE1E14F6F33B.description: Write informative/explanatory texts that name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

FEE7BA53E32D4BD6B7CF6A3252A879A0.description: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

7BFA446B46304A4FB1971896BCF47E07.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

DB1B86E9ADB04414A9EBADF3B79A547F.description: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

E205493F5A824C7090C08434775F4145.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

421F08C5D2984C65A725AD8616959F1B.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

6E3CAD5BC1194C17821C5AFD8A2979C0.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

2D40B8225E694DE094F88204BF3D2DB8.description: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.

111D890A22944D70A995095F1ED7AAA1.description: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.

D629D53D90584E52ABD666EE52F38F91.description: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.

7775ECF16ABE499DB05C4FA22C92A7C6.description: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.

057323CBCD174A489E772060C73C37F7.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

20F4CFE978694956BF716EACC1AE3E53.description: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).

BB369601794040889043A0FFC72F93E6.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.

6D4D67B005F843D1BD1A9E6A74D68BB2.description: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.

F40AD15B6FCF499BB3F212004646C402.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

A243628822994F53A7799862E821CE3F.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

8FC7A754EB8C410599A97D728A2760DB.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

0919267F54AC44069CABE552D050D1FD.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

B668DA43B670447F9729BA3801F30F23.description: With prompting and support, read and comprehend informational texts exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 1.

A26E64AB25764D26B49D3EAB97AF9E61.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

60222FBCB511425A89D1886ECD71B3DD.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

EB2BADE637D44F10899A5258E5BADD2D.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

5D3265D82DDE4A19BD7E18BFBE5BBB67.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

DEC1A34CF45A4982804CE11E2D65CE11.description: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.

7918C185674C4D04BBF9D871861C7C3C.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

823619F20BC149B99AB026BCA53A24EF.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.

E130781E616240198F4A1A155A85DB36.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

172F35CE7ED647F9A7A1EEBECC7B95D2.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

EEAF863E965643038CBD3ABC5338CA7E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

2499422A3C9A4468B059CDBFEED659D3.description: With prompting and support, read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 1.

DAF446793A5F47AFB6A1723029235524.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

F302E6A9E27F4AEBBD6AF60B791CA1CF.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

A0A3D0605A6245FA85D7025740B8E1AC.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

C37A7A00BFD642FDBF168F82C017E97B.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

0244B0F7E8D846719E700E55741B3473.description: Identify characteristics of common types of stories, including folktales and fairy tales.

ADA41631633F40CCA7D8AF536ADCC00F.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

0C1C21CCF8DB408A94DFAE34029EE423.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

919456D9EE734CD589669F3FC60A3224.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

1760F8BBD0A54D028B044CDCDA9CB52F.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

document.title: Massachusetts English Language Arts and Literacy Framework

207C769144C14588A84ACC56733F82E6.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

9E7BE1714EA049C2B0BE4F63048CD1E4.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

FAC549790CC64221BC6EA7E68CDADDDE.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

37A108D645D348689B4CAF4182EA2A24.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

F2EB884F635043FD8DB0EE9368082BB0.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

3B6633C92C1C4F1EB72F5FD5B010FD51.description: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., &, #, *).

70997AB48F344A70BA05F5E4703B0E34.description: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., hr., min., sec.).

9E6D5D9B7C2A4F6C954BB62FB7C0004C.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

2D15EB9ABD5C4B57B553D25088A3F792.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

3160708C8BDA43E9A36372679FD21402.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4DDA926756DF4C5D8B982ACC5884AD85.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

DCD9562647DC4A6FBCA35379C50EC8BE.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting research findings) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

7E1462466453475C9011DBC66FDEB980.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

53C7394E7F6041E1A3534674364018C2.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

2EACBF365B2C46CF8D59FA69D3A45EBD.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

FC096DA64A154BD7A263A8D71975603E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

418174E90B844D80810EE3A7A2650942.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

C41D7239865343B5B913563A8B5A205D.description: Write legibly and fluently by hand, using either printing or cursive handwriting; write their given name signature in cursive.

B3818F3E2B954C85930285936DA6A904.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

0A08952686B04B879B7255CBE11F98D0.description: Form and use progressive verb tenses.

A55360D366FC433482C289672538D759.description: Form and use prepositional phrases in sentences to add more information about qualities such as location, time, agency, and direction.

BF11E55DAC1D430481A5457987AC63BD.description: Use relative pronouns and relative adverbs to add more information about a noun or verb used in a sentence.

83ACFAD0AFB640628F9F3C4C72253CCD.description: Use helping verbs, also known as auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, might, should), to convey various conditions of possibility, likelihood, obligation, or permission, choosing among helping verbs depending on the overall meaning of the sentence.

DD31FC3DDFE74508B3644822812757D2.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., their/there).

9D98AAEC4ED040608A1A95A14B8BE48E.description: Produce complete sentences, using knowledge of subject and predicate to recognize and correct inappropriate sentence fragments and run-on sentences.

19498CE7DCAB475CA667F645704759E4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.

1DD8EBD3BEE142AE9CC74B1A6E0623E6.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting research findings) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

70DCB543699949A0ACEB69A8DF29A418.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

388A0C7D5DB741259DC04810E13D1E33.description: Report on a topic, text, procedure, or solution to a mathematical problem, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace and use appropriate vocabulary.

A6A15B97CBBB41B584C8F19A1DC14CBC.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

C42BB3259C1643E699090CE30434CD75.description: Paraphrase portions of a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

ADFAF0A1458B4DD5A19559F19B7074D4.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

DDAB2795B4594AFD813D66A72DA0EF8A.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

3B407A7228E94A2FA067E219F6DD85F8.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

53321B4B990B456FA81B86BC671A365B.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

8CECA33CC459440D899E5FAB3265A85A.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

2464D37F65DD44D79353298B2EE12778.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1BF07D74143D4078A231BAF77ACB93A5.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support written analysis, reflection, and research, applying one or more grade 4 standards for Reading Literature or Reading Informational Text as needed.

5EE993E53AAF4C65AEA2DE1FCD46E139.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

2D3A311C4C2F4916B6E3914F0D98BA32.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

4864EDED4CB04F0B8EC369B78D9CB040.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

B1F00C68011244AB856968854C378420.description: Use technology, including current web-based communication platforms, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

523A1FE8E56D4B99AEB76D3B38504BA2.description: Demonstrate the ability to use general academic and domain-specific vocabulary appropriately.

957874E6C9534A7FA36D90A21E2CCE72.description: Demonstrate command of standard English conventions.

4056831724FA4245B866F6DBE3D5D729.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

E0E7A55805614361B67296330AFE6DAE.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

14B1A2B5A918494B89CBA65848A4E8AC.description: For poems, use patterns of sound (e.g., rhyme, rhythm, alliteration, consonance) and visual patterns (e.g., line length, grouped lines as stanzas or verses) to create works that are distinctly different in form from prose narratives.

98649910582B4CFF8F2463D9C78D8A4B.description: Provide a sense of closure appropriate to the narrated experiences or events.

8CA9D95A029C4783A2CB451858F567E6.description: Use concrete words and phrases, figurative language such as similes and metaphors, and sensory details to convey experiences or events precisely.

669A4864C8A942C7BBEB39E7B3C01AB2.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage sequence.

4B66ED30F36D4471A488E62DF8661FDE.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences or events or show responses to situations.

FDB9701ED3714109BF3A85254DC8C068.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a speaker, narrator, and/or characters; organize an appropriate narrative sequence.

FD39EE3469E24942A6380CDD8CEB28AF.description: Write narratives in prose or poem form to develop experiences or events using effective literary techniques, descriptive details, and clear sequences.

2B93A4B309964633A1F0DC1294E12BCA.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

E729FB31BBF64CE5816D3ACED89E10ED.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

91E5FA2437394CA7BCC086889DF61388.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).

66F1DC7B2F7549EDA7E14CA8CEAE8205.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

D919B9A8C6964B75A2BBB78613F81D8D.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include text features (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

BD6B344C425F4F0F99A68B5503DB3539.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

B008C37341B643F69F8FB08EC32AF4EA.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

C945B2D61BD94A90842CFB85CB896D5C.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).

1D081DA4743D4B7499E3713C431681FD.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

D37CE700555A48FB82CFCA6F5C5A57C2.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped in paragraphs and sections to support the writer's purpose.

81E01D6FBD014511818C1B9D3A529A1B.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

68C3C4B9E2B34683ADC9137A700D55B7.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

F864B8C21D3547189FF1153A5CBD98FA.description: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

2E31E38FF28D463BA4B3E07755BF80B9.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

89B030ACA5744587B0C7A6340ADE58D0.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

E32D0B2C13A640C7A3D60F4D9F68E514.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

37A309DB814C4F46B9C8C67156BCE0A2.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

2513D096784A4F6DBAD2DC4827B42FF3.description: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, mathematical, and technical texts, exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 4.

2445153F824C4DCC89359BD51F3C9943.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

2C5F84E1C09D4E59B33B01714B9CBA30.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak knowledgeably about the subject.

B83FAF65200F47A4B7F8547DA8BAA0C9.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

A10FE3E5B0414E7A9C54553CD35383B6.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations, or interactive elements on webpages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

024C2574EAAB426C854026531D02EC3A.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

05646D4B97534107906D0595052543B3.description: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

E5A789F21D554F159356DDAAF1D05318.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

F23867C515454720859F94EBA58447D8.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, mathematical, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

85CE586921944D88AA510638160F64AA.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize a text.

6C295D7CEB0F404CB68C3D477E297A9D.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text states explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

0CE03CF3F6904EF8B6FF1F76BA5931A5.description: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 4.

7F77E0B817F6445481243D7054F5BE6B.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

8E5D15E78AEE428D86E6C5763A2DB9C3.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

5FD02970A11E4EDF8F39702686629262.description: Make connections between a written story or drama and its visual or oral presentation, identifying where the presentation reflects specific descriptions and directions in the written text.

B3F9FC5DCF434DDBA24BC66E517BA972.description: Compare and contrast the points of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

6DB386FA211842D9B7FD06452476F3F0.description: Explain major differences among prose, poetry, and drama and refer to the structural elements of each (e.g., paragraphs and chapters for prose; stanza and verse for poetry; scene, stage directions, cast of characters for drama) when writing or speaking about a text.

CA2623FA59AE48A6AF7CF185255A7F31.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean); explain how figurative language (e.g., simile, metaphor) enriches a text.

9A560D03B2424E569004530AFF893665.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

F44B222BC9CC42139FD59C91556BB412.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize a text.

78ED01BE5E0B4DF6BA6145A6E4F0647F.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text states explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text. For example, students read Natalie Babbitt's novel Tuck Everlasting and select paragraphs and sentences in the novel in which the reader is given hints about the mysterious qualities of the spring water that has given eternal life to the members of the Tuck family. They pay particular attention to how Babbitt's use of metaphors and images gives richness to the text. (RL.4.1, RL.4.2, RL.4.4, L.4.5)

document.title: Massachusetts English Language Arts and Literacy Framework

542093A6AC96418BBD3501484BD54EA3.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships.

CFBFB421DA6B4B7883FC4568530E8650.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

BC36DDE737CE427AB00719E29B19378B.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

A9BDDB61674747F79F3D54F6DB42E4B7.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

58C7B185616342ECBE8E1581C0E06D13.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

0A0387297935441BA4C62070BACF688F.description: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., <, >).

0C1490EF44C143F9AED96937AE3651E8.description: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., N, S, E, W on a map).

CB25142BE07645BEBB6E6C84C2DA8246.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

CD480FB81AA0426DAE05609EBA2747CB.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

4E5ABE6960134EC699589AC254380E7C.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

A5D016FA8D47472C94C09639F247296A.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A09E983A555F4D60B0D34C2A8AD75F55.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

33F47FACCF154AC1A4B579D2D174886E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written English.

2BCEF53DC8AB4C17BEA3D5DA5224D558.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

9BC9668C81904642857217CE28FF809D.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

D3FED317EED04281BB1ECB77C01207C5.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

FD4762E8A7844E73BF1D8EBBBF3CBD81.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

37B8B1EA3F124341A532DECFBD8AFB08.description: Demonstrate understanding that numerals used at the beginning of a sentence are written as words and capitalized (e.g., "Three pandas could be seen eating leaves high in the bamboo grove.").

2ECAF622FD284E5191519983086EA8D3.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

5D768DC9085F465281E5ADB01E09314F.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

14496A953DE34C258DF2F69E2AEF464F.description: Write legibly and fluently by hand, using either printing or cursive handwriting.

7147B9F744324209B4BF6CA82D0D0CB4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

42F2CE3AB85148A0A6E43CC3463D9572.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns and the past tense of regular and irregular verbs.

972CD195095E4699B4BA505CCB478761.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs and choose between them depending on what is to be modified and the overall meaning of the sentence.

790C3E03E2D84EDAB6C012AC687A4F33.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

05A80ECAE1614CA283409FDD330180E0.description: Use collective nouns and frequently occurring irregular plural nouns.

8EF2342E0B0B4040B8530C313E2E2E37.description: Use adjectives and adverbs in sentences and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

90D06AD6A92E482A970283F2CA45D5F5.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences and choose among sentence types depending on the meaning to be conveyed.

FFB5D79A4987444E9536740C64767D98.description: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section. AE0832F618BD465488FDC7D166210D84.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

82E429B215564EAC96C3A2E39385A566.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.

D8689F3CBB304A9AB47C2DB76EB1AC43.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

58C5063834DA4656BBB5764628852328.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

0C3FCA47699A42E1890669D052AFDAE2.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

4BBABD9CAD1A4614891EDFAB92BB3811.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

686297D48C1D43C2A69DF7EC4715315C.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

44769CC3E708481FB52A1E6195617B78.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, mathematical ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

DFE5C3E8CA0B44D2B970EE69320EF233.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

2A803692418D4EE1A7B575AD2061AC99.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

1C5FEF14CD754A7792C7F37157D73A75.description: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 2.

285CEDAB352A4F35B89005A3116D6E13.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

89F100988E9D423F86E2D2C048A8890F.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the kindergarten curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

1E65821F50874A6D8A58CE1FE6102E08.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

B49A0F51399B4042B33D680B125CC901.description: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).

A94C5D359CCF4C83B22AFFB39A3EC2DA.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

604F29952D084AA4AA5FBE403F5E1403.description: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/.

A626A557E7824288872BDEBFA323A404.description: Form questions that seek additional information, rather than a simple yes/no answer.

B018C894EE1A45D0AE08944932C7E14E.description: Demonstrate the ability to produce and expand complete sentences using frequently occurring nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, question words, and prepositions; name and use in context numbers 0–100.

14C17AD86649494BA606CC3C91946783.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

A880DA4604864EC4B73E31BF7F40983A.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

21ED3FCA86E34A0CBB4BD97A40DA159F.description: Demonstrate the ability to use vocabulary appropriate for kindergarten.

618A134DECA2413998DB17415BB04F3E.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

64CD31E1BA644DEDAF8C83D2158D8D99.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts). For example, students study the life cycles of plants and animals. Read-alouds from books such as One Bean by Anne Rockwell, From Seed to Plant by Gail Gibbons, and A Tree is a Plant by Clyde Robert Bulla introduce students to core science concepts and vocabulary through illustrations and words. Students draw, dictate, and write observations in science journals. (RI.K.2, RI.K.4, RI.K.7, SL.K.5, L.K.6)

849E32A4903343F69FD827266722B562.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

C6076961AEBD4FA79660F98B36EFD2F4.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

632D9F711CE6440DB8F2E4DE0080B980.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

F1603DAB10254C16A86C1BBC432D50CC.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

728F16B464C1410590BBD1A219E5412F.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

F55C6109237F4C1AA92D45A27C5B1F57.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

document.title: Massachusetts English Language Arts and Literacy Framework

DA8225A13DFA4D7D909C458ADEB066C2.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

5E10D454B824453CAFA1B9F67A2BB07F.description: Integrate multimedia components and visual displays into presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and evidence, and add interest.

8FC6469467474F5C9CC86E59F03E38FC.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with relevant evidence, sound valid reasoning, and well-chosen details; use appropriate vocabulary, eye contact, volume, and pronunciation.

B5A8C44D06874577BA05389E5974A0AF.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and relevance and sufficiency of the evidence and identifying when irrelevant evidence is introduced. For example, after an author of science books on endangered animal species visits their class to talk about her research and writing, students write reports on what she said, summarizing important points and arranging them in a logical order. (WCA.6–8.2, SLCA.6–8.3)

81002BDDD2FB4AD2AAF69020C68D6671.description: Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and evaluate the motives (e.g., social, commercial, political) behind its presentation.

5BBC145D7B5545D7BDDCB8ABCC5B9E0B.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views in light of the evidence presented.

D1E1086B60624117AA0F5A64E3111CD0.description: Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

C8CCD68B9F354C8CAF648314158F3468.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

61C18BBCDF7D40BAA4D7D501B72917FC.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

42F3F03E2BA54816A664372333977F26.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on discipline-specific topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

5D3212F33D0340FA9EDB051612B5965C.description: Speaking and Listening Standards for Literacy in the Content Areas

0A18D3BC18BD4919B1127671139B3E2A.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

3C3F77ED4B784C1F95F8665678B3C063.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, interpretation, reflection, and research.

A6A6045631014B1CA7511D064873408D.description: When conducting research, gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation. For example, in a science unit, students explore ecosystem dynamics as seen through a study of invasive species. They research how invasive species are introduced, the impacts they have on local food webs, and how ecosystems react to invasives. The unit involves reading and research, vocabulary development, models, data analysis and writing. (RCA-ST.6–8.4, WCA.6–8.8, WCA.6–8.9)

4494B13DA2BA44868A810F11E53E1D2C.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration. If you could go back to ancient Greece, would you rather live in Athens or in Sparta? In a paired set of arguments posted on Massachusetts Writing Standards in Action, two students make separate cases for the superiority of Athens and Sparta respectively, supporting their arguments with what they have read about the city states in social studies classes. (WCA.6–8.1, WCA.6–8.7, L.6.3, L.6.6)

For example, in a science unit, students explore ecosystem dynamics as seen through a study of invasive species. They research how invasive species are introduced, the impacts they have on local food webs, and how ecosystems react to invasives. If you could go back to ancient Greece, would you rather live in Athens or in Sparta? In a paired set of arguments posted on Massachusetts Writing Standards in Action, two students make separate cases for the superiority of Athens and Sparta respectively, supporting their arguments with what they have read about the city states in social studies classes. 8FD65FEB9A234661AA08616B92318AB6.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

Given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

7B210567304043D19AA4E95715794EC9.description: Describe the effects of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

4DC3883706BB47639D0AC53373C0EBD9.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations. Given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

A911064347884BC48CE6E3B7AF87B146.description: Parallel lines are transformed to parallel lines.

B38126A7CF684D84854185125B9BCDE4.description: Angles are transformed to angles of the same measure.

7AF70718641A46AFAD76277CA1227E8D.description: Lines are transformed to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

330F311388B943039C9BAF3B0087993A.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

0601A15683344D1E9F0A672C64FB9F20.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

FB883F3A65CE4EA2948A111B0C4C7837.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

4F3B120EA2C74A22AB1E56CF65D65431.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D157089A89D246F4ACCB6E8E406A9F4E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

BB80404FCB06440F97F090D8228D9641.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

FF1A72E425994E01BDFF4E8847F28360.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

44E311AFDDCA4FDE9948DF30A7A8DE8C.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

9A14A6A4700249108CF9DA45C4C193A7.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

DCE9688B810741F1A799602E6D43EB36.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

351D948109C046D181C9CC9849906EF9.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

13B2F4FD93774288BFA41A8704CBC38F.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

1AD8298CDA7B4A14B662B612EDD4318A.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

84D490A4D23E4D4F9D39C8FF74BD79FA.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

7CD109196BC745BD8131DFA6591060CF.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

26C6DB80DA0E46FEB077C5C108AA60C6.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

659B7A6C5A63468BA66FDD67D6816FDB.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

D58C424959EB4F2DA380D9CFEA799B3A.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

2559AF44A97D4F4EAB1C20DF4E947737.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; Generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

6A436346CC654B639895F88D8ABDF83A.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

DE06D4A123014230B1802F645510F472.description: Extend analysis of patterns to include analyzing, extending, and determining an expression for simple arithmetic and geometric sequences (e.g., compounding, increasing area), using tables, graphs, words, and expressions.

0FE5CD1017EE4E9A91D4500FB59AC3E1.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

DA035FE512494099A950BE3B534A65CE.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x ÷ q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

9A110FD5B2B44DB88AEEA0696A6D56FC.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

CCCB4D5A248A4E83B402F23E1E05F77F.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

592EED3AE01B4F4F84789F0204E75EEF.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

9E2753F65C8B4AD0A0B30CA9ADD9FA81.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

C050BA1D126A46B9A460AC5EFFE8CAC4.description: Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

FFB5DE6400744367822A3970299264E2.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

E25ED7FE03F84832AA1049888DCB69B2.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

89D4CB73BFC841418CFBF0458EF1B43B.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

F1DA0355A2D6478BAA5885404C1C9499.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

25D3676EE1F84F778603076156366E56.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

3C90769EE285418390F01A3A521AC96D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide integers and other rational numbers.

40AFBAC39CF44070AA5CCF3A83CF3685.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

9ABFA1FD6C1D41679F7BBCD8A6A36009.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

261B2214F3B642268EDF78EC7DEBD4F5.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

305D830C7DC8464FA1C71F8F6C564E5B.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make zero.

B8ACB08515D14985B42204E1567ED6BD.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract integers and other rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

32C69FE856904AC18887D85E89750AC7.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

9C252FCA09414074867FF719B5A8BECC.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

1FFD3C8A823D444AB2AD1AF9137A84C5.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table, or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

D1103966B6C643DC8BC58B975C3D3ED5.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities measured in like or different units.

2D91EC85C32D494ABD5D39BFE805F0D7.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

D2713E43A7AB49698BE209C2BEA97503.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume, and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

2C0A27666C91472FAF1815247610B49D.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems.

93B09275F96541A98E469C2F68C45A93.description: Understand and describe the relationship among the radius, diameter, and area of a circle.

498B7E2D7415463F83DCB1004105C6EE.description: Understand and describe the relationships among the radius, diameter, circumference and circumference of a circle.

A9F4BC9D7C764B94AB69512CE8947FB0.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, such as computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

AF0746E70F424B04940A4E68EA4E134B.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

6EDB2D2CB17B4236AC80BB795D2A9B26.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A6D12757EA7D4EC3BF974D6E77E0B25C.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
