F9E2FD7B87154D8CA17A4DDF10110A5E.description: Execute a variety of technical elements (e.g., scenic, lighting, props, costume, sound, and makeup) to create a design through rehearsal for a theatrical work.

2598333B20034796B29A8B6E81CAFB2F.description: Use various acting techniques to expand skills and develop character choices in a theatrical work.

235EAEEDCD044B90A9AFA5C519005D77.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation.

C555C1118A2447658960D31587A69398.description: Select, analyze and interpret artistic work for presentation. Envision and describe a scripted character's inner thoughts and objectives related to the given circumstances in a theatrical work.

5DFCEFFA48D54B0A927B1230AE0DE647.description: Apply strategies to overcome creative blocks.

09ADBE6E1A5E47A6A9FF5C053553C136.description: Develop a scripted character by articulating and using the character's inner thoughts, objectives, and motivations in a theatrical work.

CC3C9448BE1C430CA74244F795E77BF5.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work. Utilize personal notes to support performing in roles with extensive verbal lines and performance directions.

33F0408D514E42329F35DDC0D9DA68B6.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work. Generate contextual ideas for a character beyond what is given in the script (e.g., a character's backstory, attitudes, likes, and dislikes) and explain how these ideas connect to other elements in the play (e.g., setting, plot).

ED7BF8DB7C8348B9B3E9A656A9E542DF.description: Music and Dance Connection: Students examine how music and dance influenced the evolution of pantomime. (F.M.Co.11)

326FEE078AD0402F80819E11469A7A87.description: Relate artistic ideas and works to societal, cultural and historical contexts to deepen understanding. Identify the connections between historical and cultural contexts and defining stylistic elements of theatrical movements (e.g., how the existential movement and absurdist theatre are connected).

FBEDA20D6C1D45DBB4EE2898F4D5A558.description: HSS Connection: As they study the Mexican Revolution, students incorporate their own styles when writing and performing a monologue as Pancho Villa.

86F8CB7CC24149FC9845B2BFB102328C.description: Synthesize and relate knowledge and personal experiences to make art. Describe what has influenced changes in one’s own dramatic style and preferences in theatre.

45F01BA048134BE1934ACB00DAAF68ED.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work. Compare and contrast different rubrics or criteria for evaluating theatrical presentations.

E8CA6773CCD84590B5410DC61B567E60.description: Interpret intent and meaning in artistic work. Identify theatrical decisions from a work that connect it to a specific genre or style.

56DB14E50CC647BCA416ACAE38A8AF95.description: Perceive and analyze artistic work. Analyze the style of a playwright and how it manifests in a given theatrical work. For example, examine how a playwright uses character relationships to assist in telling the story.

91912B155A3C4D88A6ECC26F8B49BB18.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work. Describe how decisions about a performance are connected to what the student wants to express, evoke, or communicate.

0556C51E29C743FEB88B380A0A13F6BE.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation. Identify theatrical staging conventions in a scripted theatrical work.

F388A7985E4E4DB78AF12E81875F033D.description: Select, analyze and interpret artistic work for presentation. Identify historical sources that explain drama/theatre terminology and conventions.

87480C929017473DAC2BF367FDE530E2.description: Refine and complete artistic work. Refine and revise character dialogue, stage directions and sensory details of imagined worlds.

CA6F768F460549AAB6B297408BB98DDB.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work. Create an outline for an original scene or short play, including details such as costumes or scenery.

8D3A5A031AC5466EB10206F3806132DE.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work. Create theatrical ideas (e.g., plot, setting, character) that reflect characteristics of different artistic movements.

B14D13A68DB0489FB6E5059AF89F2348.description: Relate artistic ideas and works to societal, cultural and historical contexts to deepen understanding. Explain the relationship between theatre and commercialization or propaganda (e.g., how Agitprop Theatre was used in the Soviet Union, and how it influenced the works of Bertolt Brecht).

ED15A78EF1F240309D838A055D3D0748.description: Synthesize and relate knowledge and personal experiences to make art. Describe how theatre influences one’s understanding of other academic disciplines (e.g., the similarities between character development in theatre and in literature).

07F12191C06249B1A5FD12156A2F427B.description: HSS Connection: Students discuss the merits and criticisms of playwright Countee Cullen’s work during the Harlem Renaissance.

A3DE75BA1DC1476CA5E445B57FEF5D84.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work. Choose and defend criteria for evaluating theatrical work.

AD40454199694BA2BB9F324EFF5BEEF4.description: Interpret intent and meaning in artistic work. Compare and contrast the artistic elements that make contemporary theatre unique (e.g., compare and contrast how a contemporary theatre work is different from a contemporary interpretation of an older work).

2B65AF451FD142EB9A0F74B248505364.description: Media Arts Connection: Students develop a screenplay which they turn into a short film.

38FEE231B94A4BFE9B12CA35E7D85641.description: Perceive and analyze artistic work. Use script analysis to generate ideas about a character who is believable and authentic in a theatrical work.

51CA80D429834D9F98F4E25E4B1F0285.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work. Modify a theatrical performance by anticipating audience responses to better align to student's artistic intent.

D2794FE1F9DA4754B8CAAFC2E63A65A6.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation. Plan an entire theatrical work (including script and technical elements).

DE2FB61FB79945CB8E6E3880F9293BF4.description: Select, analyze and interpret artistic work for presentation. Explore physical, vocal, and physiological choices to develop a performance that is believable, authentic, and relevant to a drama/theatrical work.

7ADABBABACC0464199597F4ED86F12BE.description: Refine and complete artistic work. Use historical and cultural context to structure and refine personal acting choices.

5C52D5B82E6A46FE949912EF6B530B70.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work. Identify different strategies actors use to approach a role (e.g., method acting).

B7CE3164B7904885A386550021ECA22F.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work. Consistently apply research to develop characters that are believable and authentic in a theatrical work (e.g., student listens to recordings of a dialect from a specific place or time-period to develop how a character speaks).

AEA981E0BEA7485299852935A3D093C7.description: HSS Connection: Students analyze the use of propaganda in theatre that resulted from legislation changes during the Reign of Terror.

0ED45FBA33D5489FB26575B8C8F4ABE3.description: Relate artistic ideas and works to societal, cultural and historical contexts to deepen understanding. Identify the historical and cultural contexts that caused a shifting of stylistic elements between theatre movements.

06645DB9109C43B6B2D70D7304EFC8DF.description: Synthesize and relate knowledge and personal experiences to make art. Explain the development of one’s aesthetic vision as an actor and how that is represented in a current role.

D5F52C0D38904CF9A2A444A5791EC428.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work. Identify how bias, culture, and privilege can affect the criteria used to evaluate theatrical work.

6B2DC600C1D1419D9CD0FF199F02BC6F.description: Interpret intent and meaning in artistic work. Analyze the ways one’s own cultural and personal perspectives and biases affect understanding of a theatrical work.

AC0AD75BF8BB49BC81C0969D82DC5DA6.description: Perceive and analyze artistic work. Identify ways a contemporary theatrical work pushes boundaries of a theatrical genre (e.g., comedy, musical).

0FC6B930E4B04710ABFFE1D7E2700C5A.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work. Perform roles that present a range of moods and emotions and causes audience reflection by presenting different styles or viewpoints.

C786BBE3163642D4A6A7275E44651950.description: Music Connection: Students collaborate on the creation of underscoring and source music for the annual play

46A72192A6904856B448FED7AC2D4AFD.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation. Organize and lead the production of a theatrical work.

B112CF31E5334D38B1074B05AA917EDA.description: Select, analyze and interpret artistic work for presentation. Synthesize ideas from research, script analysis, and context to create a performance that is believable, authentic, and relevant in a drama/theatrical work.

82D27EA2FBD340FCAFF2E90A955A6188.description: Refine and complete artistic work. Identify theatrical challenges and reflect upon the advantages and disadvantages of different solutions.

9BEA948B228C45628EC0A002A6D7F950.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work. Document strategies used regularly to organize artistic ideas (e.g., keeping a notebook).

810E054369E14E1D8E34E26900733C38.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work. Generate original ideas in one theatrical area (e.g., acting, production) that integrate aesthetic principles with personal style.

122938F3A1A34019A77C2CDB44BEE1BD.description: Relate artistic ideas and works to societal, cultural and historical contexts to deepen understanding. Explain the relationship between theatrical design and commercialization or propaganda (e.g., how the sets and costumes in a play such as The Lion King contribute to its commercial success).

F5766F8151C04F7F98E2FFAC33F95541.description: Synthesize and relate knowledge and personal experiences to make art. Collaborate on design choices in a drama/theatre work that examines a critical global issue from personal, community, and cultural perspectives.

3AD3A40A7F424BE192C8CF22CACDDCB1.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work. Construct an argument for selecting one criteria over another for evaluating the technical elements of a theatrical presentation.

0C6CF69986B240F0A9127AACB461CBC1.description: Interpret intent and meaning in artistic work. Analyze the ways one’s own cultural and personal perspectives and biases affect one’s interpretation of the technical choices made in a theatrical work (e.g. a student may not personally appreciate the color choices in a production’s costuming that are based on a culture with which the student is unfamiliar).

5DD6166491C14C2EB1075CC25CD0947C.description: Perceive and analyze artistic work. Identify ways a contemporary theatrical design pushes boundaries of theatre.

E10D04F47C9049B9AD54B3151EAD1E66.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work. Create technical theatre elements that actively support the mood and emotions consistent with the student's artistic intent.

29FE871B9C084AC3A59558E0D463EA2F.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation. Organize and lead the production of one technical element (e.g., scenic, lighting, props, costume, sound, or makeup design) in a dramatic presentation.

BB24E9DE985F4824A6492A0D6D033DF1.description: Select, analyze and interpret artistic work for presentation. Explain and justify the selection of technical elements (e.g., scenery, lighting, props, costumes, sound, and makeup design) used to communicate the concept of a drama/theatre work.

18820FF76D7E48EF967C6B231713F0B2.description: Refine and complete artistic work. Identify theatrical challenges and reflect upon the advantages and disadvantages of different solutions (e.g., scenes that move quickly between two different time-periods).

D9757D39247B48AC93FF12DCAD53DB10.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work. Create a complete design and implementation plan for a theatre work that incorporates elements of theatrical design such as sound, lighting, scenery, and costumes.

F6FDA9E18DA1443BBB1AAF83AAE21A7F.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work. Apply research to support development of design ideas (e.g., students research cars from the 1920s to design scenery).

document.title: COMPREHENSIVE HEALTH AND PHYSICAL EDUCATION Grades Pre-Kindergarten to 12

0D160D305CB74AE99B220EB589750CC6.description:
Encourage peers and family to help in the community (e.g., donate food to a food pantry, clean
up litter). [HE]

6CB249D47FE84887AA456022C4992667.description:
Encourage peers and family members to make choices to help protect the environment (e.g.,
recycling, using less water, turning off the lights). [HE]

8DF2684C8E09424DBD067DF0B2723321.description: Identify strategies to minimize impact on the environment (e.g., reduce, reuse, recycle). [HE]

F539FB8E6E90425BA6B69CEB3A4957D6.description: Identify ways that the communities people live in can impact their health and well-being. [HPE]

ADC0E584005448BF8A12AAD1D3E33BAB.description:
Identify the impact of personal activities that contribute, positively or negatively, to the
environment. [HE]

5DCC00D928AD4267B7DBE55D2E2E885B.description:
Recognize how the actions of others can impact physical health (e.g., spreading germs)
and encourage peers to make positive choices about physical health habits and prevention
strategies. [HPE]

3F8683CFECBE497592A68076E319EDC1.description:
Self-advocate in order to have personal health needs met (e.g., needing to wash hands,
asking for sun protection, access to bathrooms). [HPE]

27B97053ACBD4A89A4DE124320A720F7.description:
Describe personal health habits (i.e., brushing and flossing teeth, hygiene, hand washing,
sufficient sleep, sun safety, physical activity, limiting screen time) that can prevent illness
and promote self-care and overall health. [HPE]

21388ABE5B01417DBD7B2FB7A1C69CA8.description:
Demonstrate personal hygiene habits and other behaviors that prevent the spread of
illness (including foodborne illness) and infection. [HPE]

1D2379B19C8241E7B3DF97EB42873A9B.description:
Self-Advocacy and Health Promotion.
Promote personal, family, and community health and well-being.

98F2746DB0404DC787ABC27EC27721EC.description:
Identify trusted adults at home and school (e.g., school nurse, guidance counselor) who can
discuss rules and practices related to medicine use (e.g., only taking medicine with an adult’s
help, only taking prescriptions that are prescribed to you). [HE]

57DE2430EC634D6D982D552E43EFFE48.description:
Explain why it is important to use prescription and over-the-counter medicines correctly and
safely, and the risks of ingesting household poisons (e.g., bleach, laundry detergent) and
incorrectly using household products. [HE]

B01B38273A064F958EC99042132223E2.description:
Demonstrate the ability to access help for self or others (e.g., school nurse, counselors, health
and physical educators) to support physical health and hygiene. [HPE; SE]

32FA0CF40B17464F8DDB2B6DD2571A97.description:
Identify individuals who can assist with health-related issues and potentially life-threatening
health conditions (e.g., asthma episodes, allergic reactions, seizures, concussions). [HPE]

16177D17048C48E983B59202929FC212.description: Identify school and community health helpers and community resources. [HPE; SE]

BAA91709BC504F4A8AED576247FBD50D.description:
Information and Resource Seeking.
Access, evaluate, and use valid and reliable health information, products, services, and
related resources.

3FDAAD7B336644E2A84584183D145D57.description:
Demonstrate strategies that help all students feel welcome and valued as a part of the school
community (e.g., cooperative playing, listening, showing you care, sharing). [HPE; SE]

11D20117CBDD41C79DE3D04252D58216.description:
Articulate and celebrate the individual characteristics that make a person unique, and explain
that how a person views themselves can be influenced by different factors (e.g., peers, media,
culture, family, phase of life). [HPE; SE]

BEF0B8FA46A64A68BB5583C143B9B2C3.description: Describe personal strengths and the ways that those strengths support mental health. [HPE; SE]

AB533E681E384FCDA37DCC839153E2DA.description:
Demonstrate growth-oriented practices by attempting, repeating, and experimenting with a
variety of experiences and activities. [HPE; SE]

28829EF903A84250983EF89CFB351001.description:
Accept failure and demonstrate the ability to persevere despite real or perceived failures. [HPE;
SE]

17B77660DE14490193F5FC98E2CBDFB4.description:
Demonstrate emotional regulation strategies to support mental and emotional health alone or
with support from adults. [HPE; SE]

03728B7A7D8F49A1AEBCB1C395D72095.description:
Explain that emotions are information and that personal emotions may be the same or different
from the emotions of others. [HPE; SE]

43541CCE2F18484BB880AFEC7C56780E.description:
Recognize and accurately label simple emotions (e.g., happy, sad, mad, worried, lonely). [HPE;
SE]

651E3505D3134D6E83F7F492BFD42B57.description:
Self-awareness and Analyzing Influences.
Examine how emotions, thoughts, needs, values, beliefs, and other factors (both internal
and external) influence behaviors and articulate how these influences impact health
behavior and outcomes.

C9A915127FA948D28616A1261F0E04AC.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate manipulative skills in varying environments (i.e.,
underhand and overhand throwing in a non-dynamic environment, catching, dribbling with
hands and feet, bouncing a ball, volleying, striking, rolling a ball in non-dynamic or dynamic
environments, and kicking). [PE]

792E668F11BB40DEB48D2CDE8F03425D.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate stationary body actions in non-dynamic
environments. [PE]

1D823D7664CC4D7FBC1FE0EE2240AE07.description:
Demonstrate stability skills by maintaining balance and transferring weight (one body part to
another) on different bases of support and combining levels and shapes. [PE]

013982CC2BB94009A45B6E33556F969F.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate jumping and landing (i.e., using a variety of one- and
two-foot take-offs and landings, and jump roping skills). [PE]

661054454142482192421B18EE617D48.description:
Demonstrate the ability to engage in rhythmic movement activities (e.g., move in self-space and
general space in response to designated beats or rhythms, drumball, dance). [PE]

D44512EDFFEA4D6BB5D734AC0C4E1F1D.description:
Demonstrate different levels (low, middle and high), a variety of relationships with objects (i.e.,
over, under, around, through), and ability to vary speed and force while traveling. [PE]

4EAE4A6397E24072BB3C2D28F7B2E1C2.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate locomotor movements (i.e., hop, gallop, jog, slide,
skip, roll, and run) and movement concepts (i.e., traveling in various pathways, showing
differentiation of speed) in dynamic environments (e.g., incorporated in a dance or rhythm
activity, applied during a game or activity). [PE]

74B71F190DD044918A3A6C4CE24CD1D9.description:
Movement Skills.
Demonstrate competence in, and knowledge of, a variety of movement forms, motor
skills, physical fitness components, and principles in order to engage in purposeful and
health-promoting physical activity, including sports and games.

F8014F8BF0A34DD4974394A52CFB6327.description:
Identify reasons conflict and disagreements may arise in various situations and strategies for
resolving misunderstandings and managing conflict. [HPE; SE]

E2702BB60CC44E48953FDE8319F96CEF.description: Describe positive qualities in self and others. [HPE; SE]

CBFACD8C728E4534A8BA449B03BA71CE.description: Recognize and appreciate individual differences in others. [HPE; SE]

1C0B87E972DF441BBB192940C8F6FB77.description:
Demonstrate effective listening and communication skills, including giving and accepting a
compliment and feedback, individually and in group settings. [HPE; SE]

3819D719A3E44FCFBA92C9A53C0CCEA9.description: Show respect for the feelings, rights, and property of others. [HPE; SE]

885B803C9ABA41A3A64DD1AB73549A3E.description:
Effectively express needs, wants, and feelings through both verbal and non-verbal actions. [HPE;
SE]

D5DC7108D61645A69A7F4FFE6A636EB4.description:
Identify and practice talking to trusted adults, parents/guardians, and/or family members about
feelings. [HPE; SE]

DB440593AA6E4C9BA1D89EC6851FCD65.description:
Identify and practice strategies to make and keep friends, and develop positive peer
relationships (e.g., identify and acknowledge other people’s feelings, communicate effectively,
ask for help). [HPE; SE]

A46BB038EF9243D6B14C8A90834816E7.description:
Identify reasons why it is important to have positive social relationships (e.g., positive emotions,
support and help, someone to play with). [HPE; SE]

BA279A3FACAD45A085C057F6181745F9.description:
Predict how someone else may feel in a variety of situations and display compassionate and
empathetic behaviors. [HPE; SE]

0D63826F903E4224B75ADFB7D19E4CC5.description:
Demonstrate awareness of, and ways to show respect for, different family structures (e.g.,
families with heterosexual parents, families with same-gender parents, single parent families,
intergenerational families, adoptive families, foster families). [HE; SE]

8EE589128D0A444FBB3A42810A35D006.description:
Acknowledge diversity, including (but not limited to) racial, ethnic, religious, dis/ability and
cultural differences and traditions, and demonstrate respect for others, and demonstrate
empathy and ways to treat all people with dignity and respect. [HPE; SE]

E7F7314A5ED44E929BF2A7218250CF6A.description: Discuss gender-role stereotypes and their potential impacts on people of all genders. [HPE]

3DF136987D6647A396DE5099D174C6E6.description:
Discuss stereotypes, prejudice, discrimination, equality, and inequality and how these can affect
relationships and situations. [HE; SE]

60B8E57B07E34C3C8851A3C8A315E7E4.description:
Recognize the benefits of and strategies for cooperation in a variety of settings (including
physical education). [HPE; SE]

A6B282FB97A443D59EB266FCF1536EDC.description:
Identify groups to which one belongs and reflect on similarities and differences with others.
[HPE; SE]

F5837164506F44EA9D177FB406992C0A.description:
Explain how no one has a right to violate personal boundaries, and demonstrate an appropriate
refusal (e.g., tell a trusted adult, say NO, leave the situation) when someone says or does
something that does not respect personal boundaries. [HPE]

DA70330E594A41B88A6092C7F3073594.description:
Define and demonstrate simple ways to communicate personal boundaries and respect the
boundaries of others, including physical, verbal, sexual, and emotional boundaries (e.g., explain
why it is important to tell others not to touch their body when they do not want to be touched
and why it is important to stop touching someone when they indicate the touch is
unwelcome). [HPE]

ED07A50CE2EA4FDD8864BD036B8947EC.description:
Define bullying and teasing, explain similarities and differences, and how both can be harmful.
[HPE; SE]

EDFEB522A37B4232938E751A3ECD0246.description:
Social Awareness, Relationship, and Communication
Skills.
Enhance relationships, personal health, and the health of others through social
awareness and effective communication.

9125679CD532407CB173EBEE89A8997B.description:
Set a short-term physical activity goal relevant to specific needs and abilities, take meaningful
action toward achieving the goal, and identify people at home or at school who can help when
assistance is needed to achieve the goal. [PE]

974C2E5DDED84F519C2739D901FA170E.description:
Identify opportunities, in and out of the school setting, for safe, active play, and physical activity
for self-expression, social interaction, personal enjoyment and challenge. [PE]

CF1254B753A042A2AE969D81FA073F13.description:
Identify physical activity as a health-promoting habit that contributes to overall health and wellbeing, and list the benefits of these habits on physical well-being (e.g., activities that strengthen the heart and cardiovascular system, contribute to fitness, muscle-building) and mental health
(e.g., stress management). [HPE]

6615880586A94A0F93AA919A1181EE30.description:
Participate safely in a variety of physical education situations, including independent, partner
and group activities, with and without equipment. [PE]

51284E4E5E8A4D38A67525C870325D9D.description:
Exhibit prosocial behavior and contribute to the creation and maintenance of safe, supportive
learning environments. [PE; SE]

820AEFF976664E3AB532D04D6BFEFC3A.description:
Identify and describe strengths and interests related to physical activity and movement skills,
and those for which extra effort and practice is needed to experience success. [PE; SE]

C9D1DF6CCEE54542846EB13328159623.description:
Recognize body responses, physiological changes in their bodies, and emotions during
movement and physical activity. [HPE]

EDC98D41F7A0411AA60EE0EAFE7915DC.description:
Exhibit positive self-concept, self-esteem, and confidence in abilities in a variety of settings,
including practicing new movement skills, demonstrating skills to peers, and participating in
cooperative and competitive games and activities. [PE]

28AA0567D711469A90ABE3B44BA2115C.description: Identify and practice behaviors for personal safety: say no, get away, tell a grown-up. [HE]

053537F43E84480481354D54BFFA7543.description:
Recognize safe, unsafe, and inappropriate touching and demonstrate how to tell a trusted adult
if this happens. [HE]

5061E7C88B3447E08A9FB47E99E57B26.description:
Demonstrate the ability to ask a trusted adult for help (including for problem-solving) in a
variety of situations. [HPE; SE]

859ECAB888844A4EABE9EE7E6853584D.description:
Identify safe adults to confide in and places to go if feeling personally threatened (e.g., someone
says they will hurt or harm you). [HE]

8B89B0686F004E28844D6C86FF7712F8.description:
Demonstrate how to respond (e.g., yell, get away, tell an adult, seek help) and get help in a
variety of emergency situations including when and how to call 9-1-1. [HE]

463A2234A936429FB3DEA4D2F65C5CF3.description:
Provide examples of how rules can keep children safe and identify rules to help children stay
safe in various situations (e.g., related to medicines, playground safety, physical education,
threats of violence, personal space, and boundaries). [HPE]

B0A3A56480A749D184DC10DE332F2BF5.description:
Apply strategies for staying safe in a variety of situations (e.g., on the playground, during
physical education, around water, when using wheeled recreation, as a pedestrian, around
cooking elements or fire, on the bus, when online, around weapons or in situations of gun
violence) and determine when to report unsafe situations to an adult. [HPE]

F4FE32FBCD29430FA97DE7D431942318.description:
Set a simple goal related to physical health habits and monitor progress toward the goal with
assistance from an adult. [HPE]

8CC7DCA966FE4E03AEB084256560250A.description:
Demonstrate independence in health-promoting practices such as hand washing, appropriate
teeth brushing motions, sneezing and coughing into elbow, engaging in physical activity, and
appropriate use and disposal of tissues. [HPE]

057F820F73554E348AD99C426BF574CD.description:
Use medically accurate names for body parts, including genitals when communicating about
their body and physical health. [HPE]

8B47B91334CB4CF391C5315461200958.description:
Explain how a young person can maintain or enhance the health of both their body and
mind. [HPE, SE]

6558DDC5D4F848C9BD147791EFF1EA16.description:
Identify a variety of habits that can promote children’s health (e.g., brushing teeth, proper
nutrition, going to the doctor, getting enough sleep, being physically active, limiting screen time,
washing hands, etc.). [HPE]

0CB62E315CE74C76A2D0F908042E6E34.description:
Identify simple goals for health, physical activity, academic success, and classroom behavior.
[HPE; SE]

26AE5CE32D4B4E11A09C4F7DF3B9FF39.description:
Utilize simple positive self-talk for the purpose of self-motivation and behavior
modification. [HPE; SE]

5B137E1E2D4D4268A675472C299C1E34.description: Identify what it means to be responsible and list personal responsibilities. [HPE; SE]

2BC4FE65ED92465390960B1EA6556549.description:
Define stress and demonstrate strategies for managing stress (e.g., positive self-talk, belly
breathing, talking with a trusted adult, listening to calming music, play, physical activity) alone
or with the support of adults. [HPE; SE]

702DA1877FD74927909607DFE9A002CE.description:
Demonstrate self-control (e.g., delay gratification, wait your turn) alone or with the support of
adults in a variety of typical settings (e.g., on the playground, in the classroom, during physical
education, at an assembly). [HPE; SE]

9A6249E85822433CB5D057BD0E0BC1F8.description:
Self-management and Goal Setting.
Set goals, engage in health-promoting behaviors, and avoid risky behaviors.

B2329F851681494D93E1E82D57C18719.description:
Recognize that media (e.g., cartoons, characters, advertisements, product placement) can
impact food-related decisions. [HPE]

DDDF7884E4C540BE934802F4B6A9954B.description:
Describe how the foods students eat may reflect the area in which they live and/or their cultural
backgrounds, ways students’ families use or produce food, how family meals and food traditions
benefit them, different dietary needs (e.g., food allergies, dietary restrictions) and how they
contribute to nutrition-related decisions. [HPE]

506B167687B04632BA7ACCA3AAE8B0CD.description:
Explain benefits of health-promoting eating choices and habits (e.g., balanced eating, staying
hydrated, eating fruits and vegetables, eating nutrient-rich foods, eating a variety of foods,
limiting foods high in added sugar, awareness of hunger and thirst signals). [HPE]

670E9B34DDBD431685F96904785AFF4C.description:
Explain food and health-promoting eating habits in equitable terms (e.g., all people need food
access, clean water is necessary, grocery stores are important to communities and their health,
access, needs, and preferences vary). [HPE]

AC53AC441AC540F29616A69FA8F1150B.description:
Identify that food is the preferred way of obtaining nutrients (as opposed to supplements) and
provides energy for the body, identify the primary contribution of each food group to the body,
and provide examples of foods within food groups to support informed decision-making. [HPE]

D528CD456F4041D08E4D0E8134D50AEB.description:
Articulate, with adult guidance, nutrition options in common situations, and identify decisions
that can be made independently (e.g., asking for healthier options) or when assistance is needed
(e.g., managing a food allergy). [HPE]

C262F3C787154F3CAF10DC7254347122.description:
Identify situations when a nutrition-related decision needs to be made (e.g., when trying new
foods, choosing snacks and beverages, eating breakfast). [HPE]

0D0EA47C2B8844CCA659724418E1EB64.description:
Decision-making and Problem-solving.
Make health-promoting, informed, responsible decisions and solve problems in a variety
of health-related situations.

document.title: COMPREHENSIVE HEALTH AND PHYSICAL EDUCATION Grades Pre-Kindergarten to 12

B5A7313DBB4D4533B33E16655C0F421A.description:
Propose and support classroom policies and behaviors that promote dignity and respect.
[HPE; SE]

3EC7E73DDFCA4826BB86FAA2F3AE7CCA.description:
Demonstrate ways to treat people – including other students, their family members, and
members of the school community – with dignity, respect, and empathy without regard
to race, color, sex, gender identity, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, disability,
or personal characteristics such as body shape or weight. [HPE; SE]

B864DE30C1A64E6996BE4F378F2BD4F1.description:
Use accurate information when discussing environmental health issues (e.g., littering,
deforestation, recycling, climate change, clean water) that impact people’s health. [HE]

E7B119AB203348509720ABFF01B9C168.description: Describe the ways that rules and laws can affect community health and health disparities. [HE]

9BE3493ED4F44C39BF7362AB0D40114C.description: Describe ways that the community can impact the health of people within that community. [HE]

3E34CF51BF7943CE87BB8F8D42E73727.description: Analyze issues of health inequities and injustices locally, nationally, and internationally. [HE]

A922D3C537B3427EA4616F5CF81938FF.description:
Discuss that people may experience health disparities and health inequities (unfair and
avoidable differences in health) due to factors such as socioeconomic status, disability, race,
ethnicity, and access to resources. [HPE]

0A895E5A52134BF1B41972BDE1F8A511.description: Analyze the relationship between personal health and the health of the community. [HPE]

FADA9D6DA5BA4AD6BADF25A095ABA44D.description:
Self-Advocacy and Health Promotion.
Promote personal, family, and community health and well-being.

EA82B65D72F749F99A948A906AECAFF8.description:
Locate trusted adults (including parents/guardians) from whom to get help if
boundaries are being violated or one is being physically, emotionally, or sexually
harassed or assaulted. [HE]

3060CCFE24284E0CB2A6C1A0B0A761AB.description:
Identify parents, guardians, or other trusted adults (e.g., counselors and other health care
professionals) whom students can ask questions about puberty and adolescent health issues
(including abuse and neglect). [HE]

B64ABBC650D640A8AD3F015BE447E762.description:
Explain the relationship between sexual intercourse and human reproduction, the range of ways
pregnancy can occur, and valid and reliable resources for information or support related to
these topics. [HE]

BE3AA3D9BCCB45779B176029CBF9536E.description: Explain how gender identity and sexual orientation can vary in each individual. [HE]

8A297B4499924F5B9CAD1A574C3E390B.description:
Use valid, reliable, and medically accurate resources (e.g., school nurse, doctor, digital
resources, health teacher, community organizations) to find information about the human
reproductive systems, human sexual development, and the effects of hormones (e.g., romantic
and sexual feelings, mood swings). [HE]

F9A3195AF1CB49AD8120349B47F59F95.description:
Locate resources from home, school, and community that provide medically accurate
sources of information about human sexual and reproductive anatomy, puberty, and
personal hygiene. [HE]

82D5BE4FD2E54356BF8C800212AB6325.description:
Identify characteristics of valid health information, products, and services related to
human sexual and reproductive anatomy, puberty, and personal hygiene. [HE]

A92B3BAA55734EAAAFCB1988EEFAA1C9.description:
Information and Resource Seeking. Access, evaluate, and use valid and reliable health information, products, services, and
related resources.

93F30588FF364532942CF314210EB544.description:
Demonstrate how media, including social media, and technology can influence mental and
emotional well-being (e.g., stress levels, happiness, mood). [HE; SE]

A93294F5859D4EEEB38F72F0747D35F7.description:
Describe how peers, media, family, society, community, and culture can influence ideas about
body image, and the impact on self-esteem and behaviors. [HE; SE]

28AFA74270C5420DB1FA8C8ED73262B3.description:
Describe supports needed to achieve success for a difficult activity or task in varied
contexts. [HPE; SE]

610AC9E993E34E35829BC01939FEF9CE.description:
Identify personal strengths and opportunities for growth and improvement in a variety of
contexts (including physical activity). [HPE; SE]

B55406B3049D41548E61F44168A30479.description:
Describe personal interests and the skills needed to pursue those interests in ways that support
personal growth. [HPE; SE]

4C7B7B262AD1468AAC2D84398D5E1027.description:
Describe personal and cultural identities and assets, their importance and value, and explain
how they support mental and emotional health. [HE; SE]

19DFE26A18CB4246BCBE70D73576E538.description:
Self-awareness and Analyzing Influences.
Examine how emotions, thoughts, needs, values, beliefs, and other factors (both internal
and external) influence behaviors and articulate how these influences impact health
behavior and outcomes.

C2F714FC8A3C4AAA9F5C6CFD0BD7169D.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate manipulative skills with hands in a variety of
situations and tasks (i.e., catching/fielding, sending and receiving an object, obtaining
possession of game object, striking a ball with short- and long-handled implement, kicking,
rolling a ball, volleying, and serving, dribbling, throwing and catching) in a variety of
environments. [PE]

071E72E215CF42099E3D2F1CF311EBC5.description:
Demonstrate the ability to combine locomotor skills, stability/non-locomotor skills (e.g.,
bending, twisting, rising, falling) movement concepts (e.g., levels, shapes, extensions, pathways,
force, time, flow) and/or balance and weight transfer techniques to create and perform a
gymnastic sequence, a jump rope routine, a dance with a group or other cultural and creative
activities independently, with a partner or in a group. [PE]

78D93AEEDE8E4B49B6780A5B00D32121.description:
Demonstrate the ability to combine locomotor (including jumping and landing patterns) and
manipulative skills (e.g., striking, dribbling) in a variety of small-sided practice tasks/games (e.g.,
for execution to a target, to demonstrate control). [PE]

004C7137AEF44B4D8A75F3F69C2C7F91.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate balancing on different body parts, rolling actions,
and weight transfer actions in a dynamic environment. [PE]

7A9FA79998344F99837CB5500A080933.description:
Demonstrate ability to perform various locomotor skills combined with movement concepts
(e.g., moving at different levels, pathways, directions) during dynamic small-sided games and
other athletic and physical activities. [PE]

CC66D592BF3B4B5B85FAF92C0803310E.description:
Demonstrate developmentally-appropriate patterns of varied locomotor skills, jumping and
landing, and step-like actions in a dynamic environment. [PE]

9D1E6F99909D4EDB9A0F6B84527FD43E.description:
Movement Skills.
Demonstrate competence in, and knowledge of, a variety of movement forms, motor
skills, physical fitness components, and principles in order to engage in purposeful and
health-promoting physical activity, including sports and games.

5472A1B87FCE40B88C83330F50C96243.description:
Demonstrate effective refusal of alcohol, nicotine, electronic vapor products, marijuana,
inhalants, and other substances that can negatively impact health. [HE]

631C88598D6A42238F56CC90259AF2D4.description:
Effectively communicate personal feelings or perspectives about substance use and misuse.
[HE]

52A6A83A727A41EBAB220E0A41E18FBE.description:
Analyze data related to use of nicotine, alcohol or other legal drugs that are prohibited for
minors. [HE]

94DFAA080F07450A894D991650E751A1.description:
Identify possible reasons (e.g., media, peer pressure, stress, culture) why individuals might
use legal and illegal drugs and discuss health-promoting strategies to avoid illegal drug use
and prevent unsafe or potentially harmful use of legal drugs. [HE]

172FB37D792541DCBEC0BC0F56A0382C.description:
Distinguish between the use and misuse of legal (e.g., prescription medications prescribed to
you, over-the-counter drugs, and (at a certain age) nicotine, electronic vapor products,
alcohol, and marijuana) and illegal drugs (e.g., prescription medicines not prescribed to you,
cocaine, alcohol and nicotine use before legal age), and identify potential effects of each on
the body. [HE]

4A6F73B155A44C3F81DFD963EBCDC7FC.description:
Describe the benefits of movement and being physically active, especially with others, on
physical, social, and emotional health. [HPE]

A399EB0485F242EBA2C67F982CE00245.description: Identify opportunities and safe places for physical activity outside of school. [HPE]

9F1A18B8641345BA9BE0251AE204D292.description:
Demonstrate strategies for collaborating, working and playing safely and effectively with
others, including perspective taking, in physical education and other physical activity settings.
[PE; SE]

D707DD781359410F8F7B67DC44AD6669.description:
Effectively manage emotions (e.g., anger, frustration, excitement) in a manner respectful to
self and others during physical education and in other physical activity settings. [PE; SE]

CD4857B57D61482D856229BECDC1A065.description:
Identify and describe social benefits gained from participating in physical activity and sports
(e.g., making friends, being on a team, building trust). [HPE]

268587AC2D3F439795900327AA5352F4.description:
Uses communication skills to negotiate roles and responsibilities and to provide peer
feedback in a physical activity setting. [PE; SE]

ABDE788648E04DFC944B65EC7A810C1B.description: Respectfully accepts and implements feedback from the teacher when prompted. [PE; SE]

A71901B61F3B46A5A25FB11926764F7E.description:
Accept, recognize, and actively involve others with both higher and lower skill abilities into
physical activities, in and outside of physical education, and group projects. [PE; SE]

6DF6CDDF638E4A1EAA4CF51AB85FA960.description: Describes why following game rules are important in a physical activity setting. [PE]

302DC3B4A826437BA3E626BD7CA304CF.description:
Recognizes the role of respectful interactions with others when participating in physical
activity. [PE; SE]

12597FF166C24F8F88AB522BE0DBB9B8.description:
Identify signs and symptoms of mental distress in self and others, and how to get help for self
or others. [HE; SE]

86404EA1767044F395AED3FB6F61E7C3.description:
Demonstrate how to discuss mental health and mental health conditions in culturally
responsive ways and in ways that reduce stigma. [HE; SE]

35CF18720ACB4A869D4337900B5CFE42.description:
Demonstrate how to ask for assistance with mental health questions, issues or concerns (e.g.,
challenges with friends, feeling anxious). [HE; SE]

46185A389D144B95937A7C2FF15A966D.description:
Explain the importance of talking with friends, parents, guardians or other trusted adults
about feelings and emotions. [HPE; SE]

6AB5B17574944FE49D445DF36D593C2C.description:
Develop an awareness that emotions may be expressed in different ways (e.g., through body
language, intensity of expression) by various groups and in different cultures. [HPE; SE]

FC7EBE3E3FC24F92BA2B4C592ECA35D9.description:
Describe ways that stereotypes, perceived stereotypes, prejudice, discrimination, inequality
and injustice can impact relationships, and demonstrate strategies to address these factors.
[HPE; SE]

3DAE7CFC018544019F7397B5819B1275.description:
Describe a range of ways people may express their gender and that some people’s gender
identity (how they think about themselves) matches others’ expectations about what their
bodies look like on the outside and others do not. [HPE; SE]

938BA520059043938E286DB6B27BBABC.description:
Describe the differences between assigned sex at birth and gender identity and explain how
one’s outward appearance and behavior does not define one’s gender identity or sexual
orientation. [HE; SE]

8205792A4A2845F689E41E9C3CF68D07.description:
Describe how personal experiences, peers, family, media, society, community, and culture
influence ways people interact in relationships and social situations. [HPE; SE]

349F7B178B3A419F908B68715C9BD55A.description: Identify and practice conflict prevention, management and resolution strategies. [HPE; SE]

388155E309B14E829CD64BC2D5732A66.description: Identify and practice non-violent communication skills. [HPE, SE]

09B6608044C44B47A88573B112664C51.description: Identify and respond to bullying situations in a variety of settings. [HPE; SE]

8AA78F3DEF094EC5B382DC03D2B0A942.description:
Differentiate between conflict and bullying and articulate the importance of the difference to
avoid escalating conflicts into bullying or violence. [HE; SE]

18733602407A4409B55FA11933BC7577.description:
Demonstrate strategies for addressing one’s own feelings and the feelings and perspectives of
others in order to support positive relationships. [HPE; SE]

3D2DAD0D3881424BBB728E115154CEB1.description:
Define and demonstrate ways to determine and respect the boundaries of self and others.
[HPE; SE]

8EEB52964295414F8E2FDE6185DC1EEA.description:
Identify characteristics of healthy and unhealthy relationships with a variety of individuals
(i.e., family, peers, trusted adults, teachers). [HE; SE]

29EC94690BC84AB3BEDC1957A161460B.description:
Social Awareness, Relationship, and Communication
Skills.
Enhance relationships, personal health, and the health of others through social
awareness and effective communication.

05000538E58E4C64B9F16D89DA70C1E9.description:
Identify different physical activities, in physical education class and outside of school, for
personal enjoyment and challenge, independently and with others. [PE]

82758350F4884A60B882139460101979.description:
Recognizes and articulates how physical activity influences physiological changes in their body.
[PE]

785F0FE7158047DF8DCED5CC2D0EA725.description:
Design a simple fitness goal and plan that includes warm-up and cool-down activities, uses
physical activity to enhance personal fitness, and includes resources to assist in achieving the
goal. [PE]

8F7C4F390C6D4F84A614FAE716C883AD.description:
Describe health benefits of regularly participating in physical activity on multiple dimensions of
wellness (e.g., cardiovascular health, fitness levels, muscle strengthening, stress management,
supporting positive mental health). [HPE]

187BE23811434D12B0E069744476CC2A.description: Defines and explains how to implement principles of exercise. [PE]

61AE09272FDA447E85D5999068AE272F.description:
Defines and provides examples of movement activities for developing the health-related fitness
components and for developing skill-related fitness components. [PE]

3401A9D034244770B96129AA1F4CBD02.description:
Demonstrate respect for self and responsible, safe interpersonal behavior (i.e., peer to peer,
student to teacher) that contributes to positive social interaction in a variety of physical activity
contexts. [PE; SE]

23481B36CD8645D6AEE18A26CEA86207.description:
Demonstrate the use of assertive behavior, refusal skills, and actions intended for personal
safety. [HPE; SE]

D40E0F497C03435AB1DEFC1C7EAF1315.description:
Distinguish among safe, unsafe, and inappropriate touch and demonstrate strategies for getting
help including how to tell a trusted adult if this happens. [HE]

44EE14F217DC43DDA4970AC561775B8E.description:
Demonstrate the ability to set and maintain developmentally-appropriate boundaries (including
physical, verbal, sexual, and emotional boundaries) and how to respond if those boundaries are
violated. [HPE]

3691CD1B0949468B9D12FB44ABC33278.description:
Define and provide examples of behaviors that would be considered child abuse and neglect
(including physical, emotional, and sexual abuse), and describe actions and behaviors to take if
feeling threatened by either someone known or not known. [HE]

D3F105FC49F940FFB8C49F6EDBBA9D42.description:
Apply strategies to be and stay safe when using the Internet, and other digital technology,
and social media, including addressing and preventing media overuse. [HE]

0906E41E197D4D188368EA381014B81E.description:
Identify and demonstrate how to contact appropriate resources when someone is poisoned
or injured and needs help (i.e., calling poison control and 9-1-1). [HPE]

3F6E94687CD64053AAF0E6C65776E495.description: Explain safety precautions for playing outdoors in different kinds of weather. [HPE]

1422C0B29A5F4BD49AB001405EE04230.description:
Recognize aspects of the environment (e.g., whether or not crosswalks are clearly marked,
presence of sidewalks, access to healthy foods, access to green space, levels of violence in
a community) that can positively or negatively impact safety. [HPE]

5C41ED3212A248E79A643DE348003342.description:
Describe ways to promote personal safety and reduce the risk of unintentional injuries in a
variety of situations (e.g., at home, at school, during physical activity, around motor
vehicles, around firearms, around water, fire prevention, during a fire, as a
pedestrian). [HPE]

B3F52B86C1804D979F44687ED907B474.description:
Set a goal related to personal health (e.g., tooth brushing, sleep, hydration, ergonomics, sun
safety, limiting screen time, hearing protection, physical activity, wearing protective
equipment), identify resources to assist in achieving it, and track progress toward its
achievement. [HPE; SE]

66C7BA424CDC4D67B81A592A9B7D9499.description:
Discuss influences on and barriers to maintaining or enhancing physical health and hygiene.
[HPE]

209FB2D3F4C741B2B1AE5F631EB8F574.description:
Describe personal behaviors and strategies that promote health and/or avoid health risks (e.g.,
pedestrian safety, sun safety, protecting oneself from infectious diseases, adequate sleep, good
nutrition, ergonomics, protective equipment, appropriate amounts of screen time, hearing
protection, being physically active). [HPE]

7E98477FC38A4C2BAAF6438A7407AFC5.description:
Describe health-promoting behaviors during menstruation, including ways to maintain personal
hygiene, cope with emotional changes, manage pain and identify when help or support is
needed. [HE]

C2C02506DDE2436DB3A8EA5465359DAE.description:
Explain a variety of health-promoting practices to manage the social, physical, and emotional
changes associated with puberty and into adolescence. [HPE]

F4AD648641F64688839855C060D5FBD6.description: Recognize and respect that all bodies are different. [HPE]

92B293D5CA00433894698F45BE4C2DFF.description:
Describe the physical, social, and emotional changes that occur during puberty and adolescence,
how the timing of puberty and adolescent development varies considerably, and the role of
puberty in overall development. [HE]

B3D77D940B504CA3B5D3574095A7FF8D.description: Demonstrate strategies that support a growth mindset in and out of school. [HPE; SE]

B28A622208EB485DB8A41BFCF31D55CA.description: Identify strategies for planning, prioritizing, and managing time. [HE; SE]

5EFA1EEADE03490395892DEDB8CA8497.description:
Demonstrate strategies and behaviors (which may include getting help) to help meet personal
responsibilities and identify strategies to overcome barriers to meeting personal responsibilities.
[HPE; SE]

41E3F35BE7AE4B3FAFAC56BC406131B4.description:
Identify personal stressors and demonstrate effective stress management techniques, alone or
with support. [HPE; SE]

D9ACCD15324446029289017B0C27D57B.description:
Apply self-monitoring strategies, alone or with support, to regulate emotions (e.g., breathing
techniques, appropriate sleep, proper nutrition) in varied settings. [HPE; SE]

CC129B82DDAF43E3B797FBC97C92C0EA.description:
Set a goal to use one or more health-promoting practices or behaviors (e.g., being aware of your
own feelings and the feelings of others, safe online behaviors, engaging in physical activity,
limiting screen time) and track progress towards its achievement in order to maintain or
improve mental and emotional well-being. [HPE; SE]

1B2AB531E07E4461BC3BA62476D02381.description:
Identify characteristics of and practices to support mental and emotional well-being within
various cultures and diverse perspectives. [HE; SE]

61201ED4E5F54C49890655FE6260D6CC.description: Describe and demonstrate strategies for expressing and regulating emotions in healthpromoting ways. [HPE; SE]

56724C6CF1F4415DB091860EF2ABEBA7.description: Identify how a person’s brain and body influence mental and emotional well-being. [HPE; SE]

086EE940B701432F9FB66BC4F3CA0325.description:
Recognize that all feelings and emotions are information that individuals can use to support
mental and emotional health. [HPE; SE]

A2A78603B0974BA48CE34E13F582287F.description: Discuss how feelings and emotions can impact behavior. [HPE; SE]

F775713A4C0F46538BCD6E3D44851B6A.description:
Identify different feelings and emotions (e.g., anger, fear, grief, sadness, anxiety, stress,
hopelessness, gratitude, love, excitement, contentedness, hope, pride, happiness) that people
may experience and how people might express those emotions (including individual and cultural
differences in expression). [HPE; SE]

466C1AB0BDAC48FA8513A3C5E1D0B872.description:
Self-management and Goal Setting.
Set goals, engage in health-promoting behaviors, and avoid risky behaviors.

C6EBEA29DF0245CB82970231E12FC25B.description:
Compare benefits of various physical activities in order to support personal decision-making
related to physical activity. [PE]

C97598549747404E90A3CFB60E3B31A3.description:
Engage in independent and cooperative problem-solving activities while participating in physical
activities. [PE; SE]

E698243F515341F2910298213B05CB3A.description:
Demonstrate effective decision-making skills while engaged in emerging and maturing skill
performance settings (including dance and gymnastics), games, and activities. [PE]

24F0179BEABB4098BB977ECB18CEBD69.description:
Adjust performance of locomotor, manipulative, and stability skills based on environmental and
task constraints and ensure safe physical activity participation of the individual and peers. [PE]

775117DB4B9348C5B054C1D7E0CB1C91.description:
Analyze and modify a movement based on the demands of the task and/or environmental
constraints in dynamic and changing situations. [PE]

49372A0C40B3452ABFFCAAF1415EC999.description:
Apply movement concepts, principles and strategies to avoid objects within dynamic
environments [PE].

E298A2C6BDEA4110941A68A943092894.description: Apply basic offensive and defensive strategies and tactics in a variety of activities and smallsided games. [PE]

901DCE55FED44F0EBBE27C4F2EBA5BD2.description:
Analyze movement situations and apply the appropriate spatial, movement, and strategic
concepts (e.g., force, direction, speed, pathways, extensions) in small-sided practice tasks, game
environments, dance, and gymnastics. [PE]

8ED34B8A050C46CCA1B6A1A593E7099C.description:
List options, predict potential outcomes of decision options, make a health-promoting choice,
and analyze the outcome of decisions in common nutrition situations. [HE]

EDD2AD4D931A46DCBA5E403566AC025A.description: Recognize that individuals have different food related needs, preferences, and traditions. [HE]

082E1C193FF74016ADF5B0B4E1925FF6.description:
Explain a variety of factors that can influence decisions about nutrition (e.g., food during
celebrations, food preferences, media advertising, celebrity endorsements and product
placement, access and availability, financial resources, physical activity levels). [HPE]

D527E1E532E74107940508771E82B6F7.description:
Identify circumstances (e.g., budget, food access and availability, time management) that help
or hinder decisions about nutrition and determine when assistance is needed in order to make a
health-promoting decision. [HPE]

90A8C43431FB4B36AEB8F7F6F1D07AEB.description:
Describe how cultivation, trade routes, and regions affect food supply, and how food production
affects nutrition-related decisions. [HE]

F0343E7EDBCE413A8CF4D9AE01EDD0C1.description: Demonstrate how to use food labels as part of nutrition-related decision-making. [HE]

5A32D05E1B4941EA8F8D079491C19B1D.description:
Discuss the benefits of balanced eating on physical health (e.g., supporting growth and
development, ability to engage in physical activity), social health, and emotional and mental

Explain the role of individual and collective responsibility for maintaining and enhancing
mental and emotional well-being and describe environmental and contextual factors that
affect mental and emotional health and well-being. [HPE; SE]

EEBE76D39E82444295AA3AFFBE464C1E.description:
Self-management and Goal Setting.
Set goals, engage in health-promoting behaviors, and avoid risky behaviors.

7069E38CCF544E6EBFCB3292A09DEDA7.description:
Develop positive norms regarding substance use (e.g., most people (including teens) do not use
illegal drugs, most teens do not use nicotine or regularly consume alcohol, and most teens
refrain from even trying marijuana). [HE]

C5FFE628E66240A691515EDCCB97C3B7.description:
Analyze the potential negative effects of legal and illegal drug use on personal safety, physical
activity, relationships with friends and families, school success, brain development, and
attainment of present and future goals. [HPE]

8BDF71624E84422F8BF315DC4B7DC388.description:
Analyze factors (e.g., personal beliefs, source of substance, purpose of use) that may affect a
decision to use of legal or illegal substances. [HE]

D7BFCB2225C2418EB6F4E7B97019E58F.description:
Access valid and reliable information (from home, school, and community) about legal and
illegal drugs (in regard to age of legal use or type of substance) and use it to understand and
communicate the risks and dangers of drug use and misuse. [HE]

A3DC2C7AF9CD4154B6ADFE16CCCF1F26.description:
Identify circumstances that enable or encourage the use and misuse of legal and illegal drugs (in
regard to age of legal use or type of substance), determine when situations or problems related
to illegal drugs might require assistance, and identify possible options in how to respond. [HE]

193EBECCB95A45C096A34A83577FC192.description:
Thoughtfully apply a decision-making process in situations or to problems related to legal (e.g.,
prescription drugs prescribed to you, over-the-counter drugs, [at a certain age] nicotine,
electronic vapor products, alcohol, and marijuana) and illegal drug (e.g., prescription drugs not
prescribed to you, cocaine) use. [HE]

C6D8256E704A4FDA9563D03EBEA61D67.description:
Describe strategies that can be used to make decisions that adhere to personal values, beliefs,
and limits. [HE]

EBEB5A43F44A44CF9364BA12F9BF9BBD.description:
Explain the importance of, and ways to identify, setting personal limits to avoid unintended
outcomes from risky or unwanted sexual behavior and to make sexual health decisions. [HE]

6823579F707642118F1D6ACCCC88D255.description:
Analyze personal beliefs (including level of readiness) and values related to sexual activity and
sexual health. [HE]

223A2EF380624024BD23C9B4FC12FA81.description:
Articulate the benefits of postponing sexual activity and setting personal limits, including to
avoid early or unintended pregnancy and to reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections,
based on personal beliefs and values. [HE]

BA7E4D5C0F7D4923BA59189C1524F21D.description:
Describe possible short- and long-term consequences (positive and negative) of engaging in
sexual activity and identify ways to avoid negative or potentially harmful consequences. [HE]

3957BE6F70264854A3B3D1A06FEE03D1.description:
Analyze ways to prevent pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including methods
that can be taken before becoming sexually active (e.g., communicating with a partner, HPV
vaccine, contraception). [HE]

9161EC70CB7D41D0A007A40CF0D91F7B.description:
Identify valid and reliable sources of information and resources to inform and support sexual
health choices. [HE]

79C352835BD94A92AF861485C65D746A.description: Apply an effective decision-making process in situations related to sexual health. [HE]

E4E69239FE47454284575F575CA92863.description:
Seek strategies for minimizing barriers and maximizing facilitators (e.g., time, space, physical
abilities, access to equipment, overuse of digital devices) that help maintain a physically active
lifestyle. [PE]

56ED34EDAF274E699EF4F47DAE4138EA.description:
Implement effective offensive and defensive strategies (i.e., creating open space, reducing
space, shot selection, reduce offensive options for opponents using tactics and shots, select and
apply appropriate shot and technique, defensive ready position) during game play for a variety
of games (including net/wall games, target games, invasion games, fielding and striking games,
etc.). [PE]

0190CE58FBB944D887A90661CDDF6ED8.description:
Apply strategies for overcoming individual or group challenges or problems in a physical activity
setting. [PE; SE]

B9D135AE60AD454D8EEE50AE995C1118.description:
Effectively apply team building and problem-solving strategies, in varied contexts, during various
physical activities (e.g., outdoor adventure, cooperative games, team sports, net/wall
games). [PE; SE]

473E2C53832E4E01888A5BAC02DB3735.description:
Demonstrate the ability to use a decision-making process to thoughtfully and effectively
address personal safety in a variety of situations. [HPE]

C1BFDA8B184C4C7092325A137634B058.description:
Analyze barriers that may prevent someone from reporting unsafe situations and child
maltreatment to adults and identify strategies to overcome these barriers. [HE]

62230C7FC1AE4458A03B43D1677027C6.description:
Evaluate a variety of non-violent responses to address conflict and demonstrate the ability to
use these responses to act on health-related decisions. [HPE; SE]

Describe the characteristics of various forms of abuse (i.e., physical abuse, emotional abuse,
psychological abuse, financial abuse, sexual abuse and exploitation), provide examples of
how abuse is used to control an individual, and demonstrate strategies for getting help. [HE]

FF9744CAB1124523A754BB412634CBE7.description:
Demonstrate strategies for keeping oneself safe online and in digital spaces (including
situations that could lead to exploitation or trafficking, and online sexual harassment). [HE]

926E73A76881413CB95E795F51C7FF38.description:
Explain the potential consequences of requesting, sending, or digitally posting sexually
explicit pictures or messages (e.g., on social media sites, chat groups, e-mail, texting,
websites, phone and tablet applications, and other digital forms) and demonstrate the ability
to make health-promoting decisions related to safe and legal activity in online and digital
spaces. [HE]

A97B070A38314D7C88281EDEAB486613.description:
Demonstrate strategies for avoiding situations that may lead to human trafficking and
sexual exploitation and for getting help if concerned about self or others. [HE]

01727B8BB3904B44A2073D521282870C.description:

and warning sign behaviors of exploitation and recruitment of youth. [HE]

CE921CDE40D74F71B13667B8CDAB5FCB.description:
Describe laws (e.g., age of consent laws, child abuse, including sexual abuse, and sexual
exploitation laws, parental notification laws) that relate to young people’s sexual health
and the rights of adolescents to maintain their own health, and how these might impact
decisions related to sexual health. [HE]

2C82FBDF49BE4A6594B38E5389425FCC.description:
Evaluate potential options and consequences for decisions related to personal safety in a
variety of situations (e.g., motor vehicle safety, physical injury, digital safety, threats of
violence, inappropriate touch, physical, emotional, and sexual abuse). [HPE]

3D609C5FA42F4F74A4B55536C6C06E20.description:
Discuss how systemic and other factors (e.g., home rules, school connectedness,
environment, available supports, available equipment, weather, gender-based violence,
racism, and discrimination) help or hinder an individual’s ability to remain safe in a variety
of situations. [HPE]

C5058CBB0E5445098DC09D50437408FD.description:
Describe the role of individual versus shared responsibility in staying safe in a variety of
situations (e.g., outdoor recreation, motor vehicle safety, digital safety, threats of
violence). [HPE]

00F5B7D9CD844E889D9380A7E896F2F2.description:
Demonstrate the ability to apply a decision-making process to decisions related to consent in a

32956929D02F41FBA5A333ADDA6A54D3.description:

BAAF3B540F6C422E94E810B78645044B.description: Identify warning signs of potential danger in a relationship and strategies to get help. [HE; SE]

F148CA75CD5C4C538C5FC340A1B1C2CA.description:

variety of health-related situations.

Select and participate in physical activities that meet a variety of personal needs (personal
goals, strengths, interests, enjoyment, social interaction or self-expression). [PE]

74229D9B802947E3AFCDE0CEE33A9395.description:
Apply movement concepts and principles (e.g., force, motion, rotation) to analyze and
improve the performance of self and/or others in a selected skill or lifetime physical
activities (e.g., yoga, aquatics, biking, rock climbing, dancing, canoeing, weight training, golf,
tennis). [PE]

1138B03FE3424E129E9E66A94F8D9989.description: Set a goal and create a practice plan to improve performance for a self-selected skill. [PE]

18508B9043B64D23AD562CF8F286384C.description:
Create a goal and plan for participating in physical activity to maintain or improve health and
monitor progress. [PE]

6146D0BBAA774591A02232246AEA0D46.description:
Determine a variety of physical activities that can be implemented independently or with
minimal support for the purposes of personal enjoyment or challenge, or to maintain or
improve fitness. [PE]

1006AECC1DBA4C1786CDC5618BC3C676.description:
Apply various methods for monitoring and adjusting workout intensity in order to meet
goals and heart-rate targets (e.g., calculating heart rate by taking their pulse or wearable
monitors, determine intensity using rate of perceived exertion [RPE] scale). [PE]

E71641F8B00B448CB8A7204D33F39023.description:
Investigate relationships among different types of physical skills and activities with personal
interest, social interaction, and self-expression and enjoyment and impacts on fitness,
nutrition, and multiple dimensions of health. [HPE]

98DAE96783A8488280F18BF5B41C3FEB.description:
Evaluate risks and safety factors that might affect physical activity choices and preferences
throughout a person’s lifespan. [PE]

226F6A6D8E134D0C9F51C309AEFB3BFC.description:
Employ effective self-management skills to analyze and overcome personal barriers and
appropriately modify physical activity patterns to maintain or enhance health. [PE; SE]

FFDD1C8F6A1E446CAB3B3B4DC49232FD.description:
Discuss the benefits of a physically active lifestyle across multiple dimensions of health and
across a person’s lifespan. [HPE]

91FCBF4A4C554E99855EBA09209567B8.description:
Assess personal strengths and interests and how they influence engagement in physical
activity. [HPE; SE]

A46B3E846247443DB0576B8CB889634B.description:
Demonstrate proficiency in Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and the use of Automated
External Defibrillators (AEDs). [HPE]

E63659E2B7184F7299E6FA614E45635A.description:
Demonstrate strategies for asking for assistance or providing support for self and peers when
faced with unsafe situations. [HPE; SE]

CDFF83E7177744D58D7E8CA318721F4C.description:
Evaluate personal responsibility in and the consequences related to pressuring someone for
sexually explicit pictures, sending sexually explicit pictures or messages by email or cell phone,
or posting sexually explicit pictures on social media sites (e.g., chat groups, email, texting,
websites, phone and tablet applications). [HE]

56C169443D6345A4B93A2263D0DBB704.description:
Evaluate ways and demonstrate strategies to reduce risk and stay safe, follow laws, and act
respectfully in physical and digital settings. [HE]

C881988073DB449D8FA7F6D25158909F.description:
Demonstrate strategies, including risk reduction strategies, that can help avoid or address
situations related to sexual exploitation in physical and digital settings. [HE]

6ABB80368DB84A3B94E22726CB50A310.description:
Explain human trafficking and sexual exploitation and identify recruitment tactics used to exploit
vulnerabilities and recruit youth. [HE]

7B6B2655CAFC48449779A3F6587FAC22.description:
Describe external factors (such as social determinants of health) that can affect health and one’s
agency in addressing health. [HPE]

2564834A2F4A4B3D93FE757846AB3E06.description:
Examine and describe signs, causes and symptoms of menstruation- related health conditions
(e.g., endometriosis, fibroids, premenstrual syndrome and polycystic ovary syndrome) and
explain strategies to manage and reduce discomfort. [HE]

3E949FEAE15647D6AB6C5E7DECFCE7B2.description:
Demonstrate strategies to self-advocate in healthcare settings (e.g., getting questions answered,
seeking clarity of medical instructions, seeking a prescription refill). [HE]

AD5E8ECA4A8D48BAB8A03308A4FED445.description:
Create a plan that develops agency related to individual ownership of one’s health and health
care (e.g., locating a health care provider, scheduling appointments, taking medication properly,
seeking support for medical issues). [HPE]

78D73924D9A34535A48F456D4B7D6CF9.description:
Develop a plan and implement strategies based on an identified need or want to attain a goal
that improves physical health. [HPE]

2794264F05B94BD1BEF8EFD81F47C18F.description:
Implement a plan to achieve a nutrition-related goal, monitor progress, and adjust as needed.
[HPE]

E5101CC8C6674B75B496C4FEFDF4B627.description:
Analyze barriers (e.g., finances, food availability and access, social norms, media) to succeeding
with a personal nutrition-related goal and identify supports to help overcome those
barriers. [HPE]

6C6CFC8564964717B7C1CDA14F44B50B.description:
Develop short- and long-term nutrition goals that build on strengths and address areas for
improvement. [HPE]

82F78C0229CF414D92FEE9EEF86C6373.description:
Compare and contrast various factors (e.g., culture, media, peers, portion sizes) that influence
nutrition-related beliefs and behaviors and analyze the ways that these factors are impacting
personal beliefs and behaviors. [HE]

99E0F8551C2A45E1847AB4E285B60131.description: Assess personal nutrition-related practices using dietary guidelines of their choice. [HE]

8DF8970194E84365A6A55B526123B041.description:
Demonstrate how to comparison shop for foods, including comparing nutrient density, unit
pricing, food packaging, and prices of foods in various forms. [HE]

D8ED2D214AFC4E17A1113D1444FCD9BF.description: Describe common safe food storage and preparation practices. [HE]

0B91026350964BC3825EFC3629330148.description:
Analyze the physical, mental, social, economic, and academic benefits or consequences of
various dietary habits or behaviors. [HPE]

78DE154446BC4A77837FC6B7FF9DF33A.description:
Compare and contrast various dietary guidelines and practices from different sources, locations,
and cultures (e.g., USDA Guidelines, Harvard Healthy Eating Plate, Mediterranean Diet, food
guidelines from different countries and cultures). [HE]

7D298691F7364B91A49230D61F382637.description:
Set personal short- and long-term mental and emotional health-related goals and create and
execute a plan for monitoring progress. [HPE; SE]

6884C1A4C0CC4BED915D7B32EE886827.description: Apply strategies that support a growth mindset including in challenging settings. [HPE; SE]

B22797277F314152A603CAD057D69E71.description:
Set a goal, create a plan, monitor progress, and celebrate success for plans that maximize
efficiency and minimize stress. [HPE; SE]

6441D43254DE44BFABE8BB5386D8AEA8.description:
Assess health practices and overall health status across multiple dimensions of wellness (e.g.,
physical, emotional, financial, cultural, sexual, intellectual, occupational, spiritual,
environmental, social). [HPE]

34F54ABB7EBC4810AAE1035A6882F18D.description:
Apply strategies, including developing protective factors and personal assets, to support positive
mental and emotional well-being. [HPE; SE]

44FDDCCA821541EFB231457CD23CBAE7.description:
Apply coping and stress management techniques to manage a variety of stressors (i.e., school,
personal life, relationships) and create a long-term plan for stress management. [HPE; SE]

0B3D081ED8C74DE9AC3F215E08E6CABC.description:
Apply strategies to appropriately respond using different levels of emotions in routine
interactions. [HPE; SE]

FDDF06264D0442A09DA0B68EC380196E.description:
Self-management and Goal Setting.
Set goals, engage in health-promoting behaviors, and avoid risky behaviors.

73F3360BB5A546D184A57FE67E241E1B.description:
Employ self-management skills to act on health-promoting decisions about legal drug use (e.g.,
prescription drugs prescribed to you, over-the-counter drugs, and [at a certain age] nicotine,
electronic vapor products, alcohol, and marijuana). [HPE; SE]

CB5458F3908C45B391ACA4A945D0774B.description:
Analyze the potential short- and long-term impacts (including addiction) of legal (e.g.,
prescription drugs prescribed to you, over-the-counter drugs, and [at a certain age] nicotine,
electronic vapor products, alcohol, and marijuana) and illegal drugs (e.g., prescription drugs not
prescribed to you, cocaine) on multiple dimensions of health (e.g., physical, mental, emotional,
social, intellectual) and on other health risk behaviors (e.g., sexual activity, impaired
driving). [HPE]

11FC3FE6ED0344D69F19ACAB2410D274.description:
Evaluate situations and how various internal and external factors (e.g., peers, media, social
norms, corporate practices) influence substance use and misuse. [HPE]

63F31EF7011E4C97A75E43776A40EACB.description:
Reflect on personal beliefs, choices, and values compared to cultural, community, and societal
norms around substance use and misuse. [HPE]

B06CBC4156484B81B2A2D5FB0257F5A3.description:
Demonstrate the ability to work cooperatively to problem solve/make decisions on how to
proceed in physically challenging situations. [PE; SE]

E09C4E18AAF242DFBC105259B3D38F26.description:
Solve problems and think critically in physical activity settings, both as an individual and in
groups. [PE; SE]

9A774EA2034F4405ABFF31EEAD3E3457.description:
Modify group activities or behaviors to accommodate for individuals with lesser or greater
skills or specific needs. [PE; SE]

B59F317B50784F09A9A68D743113B8CA.description: Evaluate opportunities and barriers for physical activity in a variety of contexts. [HPE]

104CDBA598E746B097FC62B70C826FC1.description:
Choose an appropriate level of challenge to experience success through participation in a
self-selected physical activity. [PE]

05149ED96EDF48ECB24F078F50D284CE.description:
Identify snacks and food choices that help and hinder performance, recovery, and
enjoyment during physical activity. [HPE]

7FC2640E6B65457DA749CA095E140E8F.description:
Demonstrate the ability to apply a thoughtful decision-making process to maintain or enhance
relationship health including the decision to leave or seek help in an unhealthy relationship.
[HPE; SE]

C4C8E5BE9B2C4DE7BE4A8D157BF1943D.description:
Examine the complexity of, and discuss considerations related to, the decision to leave an
unhealthy relationship, developing a safety plan to recognize and get out of any future unsafe or
unhealthy relationships, and determine situations when adult and/or professional support is
needed. [HPE; SE]

BCC913E1D7514066AA93EFC1FED8BE8E.description:
Evaluate effective strategies for dealing with difficult relationships with family members, peers,
and partners and demonstrate the ability to use these strategies to make health-promoting
decisions regarding difficult relationships. [HPE; SE]

951C6CAAE8BC4F1EA2DC1132898938E8.description:
Explain age of consent laws and why it is an individual’s responsibility to obtain consent, verify
that all sexual contact is consensual, recognize that consent must be asked for and verbally
given, that it cannot be given if under the influence, and that it can be taken away at any point
(i.e., someone can say yes and change their mind, or say yes to certain things but not
others). [HE]

0C4C75171F2F40369B0B9E54CA132C71.description:
Discuss different forms of abuse in relationships including emotional abuse, sexual abuse,
domestic violence, dating violence, gender-based violence, sex trafficking and exploitation, and
available supports and resources for getting help if in an abusive or exploitative
relationship. [HPE; SE]

F2817828F55941689D668B9F2599304A.description:
Describe the cycle of violence in relationships and discuss strategies for getting help and leaving
an unhealthy, violent, or exploitative relationship. [HPE; SE]

04D9CC75E7AF40988E426C030A68F8ED.description:
Analyze the role of individual versus shared responsibility in building and maintaining healthy
relationships. [HPE; SE]

8543D69D75E5426DAECCF1FC7B50DBDF.description:
Analyze the benefits and risks of various ways people express feelings within relationships (e.g.,
words, acts of kindness, hugging, holding hands, kissing, sexual behaviors, jealousy,
manipulation) and describe the characteristics of effective expression of feelings and emotions
within a health-promoting relationship. [HE; SE]

D43F620583484762B433E9911B393E45.description:
Examine, compare, and contrast aspects of various personal relationships, including
characteristics of healthy and unhealthy family, peer, romantic (dating), and/or sexual
relationships. [HPE; SE]

E10C42E4A3974E73A4E9E40F0422EE3B.description:
Evaluate readiness, options, and their respective consequences regarding sexual activity in
consensual relationships including abstinence, postponing sexual intercourse, engaging in safe
sex practices (e.g., using condoms and other barriers, using birth control). [HE]

7BE1BBD3950340DFB74798A48C80E0C1.description:
Explain the importance of STI (including HIV) testing and counseling if sexually active on shortand long-term health, identify where to get tested, and why it is important to proactively discuss
STI status with a sexual partner. [HE]

A7C08757A70446F8992425DC124BB757.description:
Analyze factors that contribute to behaviors that increase the risk of pregnancy, HIV, and other
STIs. [HE]

DC22E747E619485DB1CEA6FA71E826A1.description:
Discuss reasons for why it is wrong to trick, threaten, or coerce another person into sexual
activity. [HE]

496FB05F7AB645F7A1D51C4EA7D16654.description:
Demonstrate the ability to apply an effective decision-making process in situations related to
sexual activity and sexual health. [HE]

0122C04BB870422F98E223A4B3E14656.description:
Decision-making and Problem-solving.
Make health-promoting, informed, responsible decisions and solve problems in a variety
of health-related situations.
