Use a combination of
dictating and drawing to tell a story.

CA354A3BEB284C7C9C67DF914FAE487D.description:
Use a combination of
drawing, dictating, and writing to
compose informative/explanatory
texts that name and supply some
information about the topic.

A986FBBFB9BA44EBBC69302F209E4284.description:
Use a combination of
dictating and drawing to supply
information about a topic.

2570B76D7BAD42F6A269DEE315409D48.description:
Use a combination of
drawing, dictating, and writing to
compose opinion pieces that tell a
reader the topic or the name of the
book they are writing about and state
an opinion or preference about the
topic or book (e.g., My favorite book
is . . .).

9713885D12B44E2C900721332D062AB3.description:
Dictate words to express a
preference or opinion about a topic
(e.g., “I would like to go to the fire
station to see the truck and meet the
firemen”).

DF4B3D825D9343F49C66C15792A75204.description:
Read early-emergent-reader
texts with purpose and
understanding.

22B40B776C7A499A99B408D2A3AD3369.description:
See K standard (Begins in
kindergarten or when the individual
child is ready.)
Activities included here are meant to
build a foundation for the K
standard.

6C94EA65B76642AA8A940C719B9DBBF8.description:
Distinguish between similarly
spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

53AF88F460E244E7B5549F1BEE8B5906.description:
Read common high-frequency
words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you,
she, my, is, are, do, does).

2F96DE289466463BA7A3FBC5773449F6.description:
Associate the long and short
sounds with common spellings
(graphemes) for the five major
vowels.

586FDD9A09BE47D089C0547E5D41EF28.description:
Demonstrate basic knowledge of
one-to-one letter-sound
correspondences by producing the
primary sound or many of the most
frequent sounds for each consonant.

01AE662145B94A8EBFA0444FABDB548A.description:
Know and apply grade-level
phonics and word analysis skills in
decoding words.

15FF0791185B43D789C73ABA05FA4BD5.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or when
the individual child is ready.)

7138BF6F4113486791736056BD5703DC.description:
Recognize their own name and
familiar common signs and labels
(e.g., STOP).

EA97CE5ECDD649CE9D5FEBA3F292B51D.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or when
the individual child is ready.)

9C8A27BC498748539F1D7D54EAB217ED.description:
Link an initial sound to a picture
of an object that begins with that
sound and, with guidance and
support, to the corresponding printed
letter (e.g., link the initial sound /b/

support, to a printed or written “B”).

1A5862E92F1246D19A95E050F87BE826.description:
Demonstrate beginning
understanding of phonics and word analysis skills.

7D797A5E5C3D4CE88BD6A4124CDA89A9.description:
Add or substitute individual
sounds (phonemes) in simple, onesyllable words to make new words.

78C579072E534EA99A9F43C3A0EE59C4.description:
Isolate and pronounce the initial,
medial vowel, and final sounds
(phonemes) in three-phoneme
(consonant-vowel-consonant, or
CVC) words. * (This does not
include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or
/x/.)

0B66428A1E664031901B0D5670F3D40F.description:
Blend and segment onsets and
rimes of single-syllable spoken
words.

8BE12A3F87434817AED7E7B03C928E0D.description:
Count, pronounce, blend, and
segment syllables in spoken words.

713144F8A59E474DB8EFA06F704CFA3B.description:
Demonstrate understanding of
spoken words, syllables, and sounds
(phonemes).

DE296F76E31B45BEA88EF4BCB6014849.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or when
the individual child is ready.)

05870C9D697A420999ADE62E83E1A95D.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or when
the individual child is ready.)

CDE7EFDDCB88473FB7569E2C1EA1BA37.description:
Identify the initial sound of a spoken word and, with guidance and
support, generate several other words
that have the same initial sound.

7206D7BBB3B146688FD9ADA8CB8250C9.description:
With guidance and support,
segment words in a simple sentence
by clapping and naming the number
of words in the sentence.

F8020DC780BC42219BCEF4D7B1D5FB56.description:
With guidance and support,
recognize and produce rhyming
words (e.g., identify words that
rhyme with /cat/ such as /bat/ and
/sat/).

5A122C0EAC604D5281A770CAE93D601E.description:
With guidance and support,
demonstrate understanding of spoken
words, syllables, and sounds
(phonemes).

B8E01E11115F48E8B2455E3EDB3FA602.description: Recognize and name all upperand lowercase letters of the alphabet.

66EAE37715594542A2B12EB19133CE81.description:
Understand that words are
separated by spaces in print.

7214D47A23BB4C619C4EB48DAE9CB298.description:
Recognize that spoken words are
represented in written language by
specific sequences of letters.

85B66490F630497D99E383505A1D918F.description:
Follow words from left to right,
top to bottom, and page by page.

6DFFB05587664D4B82664917EA3F13F7.description:
Demonstrate understanding
of the organization and basic features
of print.

F902B3F1347749DDBDCC45014DF20BB0.description:
Recognize and name some
uppercase letters of the alphabet and
the lowercase letters in one’s own
name.

6E83EAFE452949ABACF1D94DE03C9F7B.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or when
the individual child is ready.)

8A822BED744F4E48A98B3AC683DDD9B6.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or when
the individual child is ready.)

F0670D4D88EE42048BA5E53C8FA30119.description:
Handle books respectfully and
appropriately, holding them rightside-up and turning pages one at a
time from front to back.

1542D874C03A407EA95903249D46A0CA.description:
With guidance and support,
demonstrate understanding of the
organization and basic features of
printed and written text: books,
words, letters, and the alphabet.

BF0F73CC583848EA8E56D2C56D55DE1D.description:
Actively engage in group
reading activities with purpose and
understanding.

E0B0A2E0526A4EB4A3959FA5DA967AF6.description:
Listen actively as an
individual and as a member of a
group to a variety of age-appropriate
informational texts read aloud.

B18086028E46453596F19718A8806880.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7CE8997946CB41F4B3FAADA9EA71456A.description:
With prompting and support,
identify basic similarities in and
differences between two texts on the
same topic (e.g., in illustrations,
descriptions, or procedures).

992358E0ABAF4B47AD31A214AF358BB4.description:
With prompting and
support, identify several books on a
favorite topic or several books by a
favorite author or illustrator.

B4BA07A5EB0442AEBE9EEBA506AE29A0.description:
With prompting and support,
identify the reasons an author gives
to support points in a text.

77D331E133644FBBAE27D77AD5F0F562.description:
(Begins in kindergarten or
when the individual child is ready.)

2FB48A878CE44ED0AEB7ADA6DE268820.description:
With prompting and support,
describe the relationship between
illustrations and the text in which
they appear (e.g., what person, place,
thing, or idea in the text an
illustration depicts).

A58101DCA98C4AB3812AE482CEDF0421.description:
With prompting and
support, describe important details
from an illustration or photograph.

A4AEAC1731AA4E7EA7D265CDDAC340E7.description:
Name the author and
illustrator of a text and define the
role of each in presenting the ideas or
information in a text.

38F0A92A9ED141ED9D8FA2AF05725160.description:
With prompting and
support “read” illustrations in an
informational picture book by
describing facts learned from the
pictures (e.g., how a seed grows into
a plant).

4831AF14F5644204AA621AAF542D11F9.description:
Identify the front cover,
back cover, and title page of a book.

9C8C548E9EDD45E9A7ED635CAEA9ADE5.description:
Standard begins in
Kindergarten or when the individual
child is ready.

7497DF9252C84F0B8F4ACE4A970FCCA2.description:
With prompting and support,
ask and answer questions about
unknown words in a text.

82522705D5D04732AA35B943B69FA649.description:
With prompting and
support, ask and answer questions
about unfamiliar words in an
informational text read aloud.

01648E2F3E46445AAE05B81D54B21101.description:
With prompting and
support, describe the connection
between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in
a text.

435A540249B546819E0E7A2DD4541F49.description:
With prompting and
support, represent or act out concepts
learned from hearing an
informational text read aloud (e.g.,
make a skyscraper out of blocks after
listening to a book about cities or,
following a read-aloud on animals,
show how an elephant’s gait differs
from a bunny’s hop).

D0C8D1287BCE40558A3CA739D6FCB4C0.description:
With prompting and support,
identify the main topic and retell key
details of a text.

61C7371A229347A1A88040C9C312DB82.description:
With prompting and
support, recall important facts from
an informational text after hearing it
read aloud.

56C819EE1EDF4416ADA5906958C34BEF.description:
With prompting and support,
ask and answer questions about key
details in a text.

B6212C7122424D74A486EB02847FB43E.description:
With prompting and
support, ask and answer questions
about an informational text read
aloud.

A76F4ED9E2AA40D48CE841F6F999B6E9.description:
Actively engage in group
reading activities with purpose and
understanding.

3EC054998813444FAFEE4C4ADCDDBE68.description:
Listen actively as an
individual and as a member of a
group to a variety of age-appropriate
literature read aloud.

With prompting and
support, compare and contrast the
adventures and experiences of
characters in familiar stories.

DADEA0B12CEC43FF895A157543A62055.description:
With prompting and
support, make connections
between a story or poem and one’s
own experiences.

6170BE9FD7D146C0B41F634D73C8FBDE.description:
Describe the relationship
between illustrations and the story in
which they appear (e.g., what
moment in a story an illustration
depicts).

8AB99E30EDE8478A8E1B7A441EA530B3.description:
With prompting and
support, make predictions about what
happens next in a picture book after
examining and discussing the
illustrations.

8A63F45A51EF49CF9163DBDA56AEC70A.description:
With prompting and
support, explain that reading the
cover or title page is how to find out
who created a book; name the author and illustrator of a book and define
the role of each in telling the story.

077E32B498EB436D8F79C8ECCF78152A.description:
With prompting and
support, “read” the illustrations in a
picture book by describing a
character or place depicted or by
telling how a sequence of events
unfolds.

0F457B1E37424B06B68EC82149BC02C1.description:

of texts and characteristics of their
structure (e.g., story elements in
storybooks; rhyme, rhythm, and
repetition in poems).

784E826339B44E6188DCF6FA344A8F0B.description:
Show awareness of the
rhythmic structure of a poem or song
by clapping or movement.

0029C31F74604ED49BAE7B6ABCB996E7.description:
Ask and answer questions
about unknown words in a text.
(See kindergarten Language
standards 4–6 on applying
knowledge of vocabulary to reading.)

64397172E5CE49B98F131F6FDF609043.description:
With prompting and
support, ask and answer questions
about unfamiliar words in a story or
poem read aloud.
(See Language standards 4–6 on
applying knowledge of vocabulary to
reading.)

18AFCF2E98E746298ED65AE54977C933.description:
With prompting and
support, identify characters, settings,
and major events in a story.

0EF80FAEE1CB4F219707867D93C24F39.description:
With prompting and
support, act out characters and events
from a story or poem read aloud.

E6813D1BD1854FCE8423B59B62042161.description:
With prompting and
support, retell familiar stories,
including key details.

66B204722158443182BC74A32E45042E.description:
With prompting and
support, retell a sequence of events
from a story read aloud.

D513CBE1D079434C86DE7D5BB44518C1.description:
With prompting and
support, ask and answer questions
about key details in a text.

0C9A3E73A8B649ACA8097B9550088E07.description:
With prompting and
support, ask and answer questions
about a story or poems read aloud.

standardSets.title: Mathematics
standardSets.subject: Guidelines for Preschool and Kindergarten Learning Experiences (2019-)

Compose simple
shapes to Form larger
shapes. For example,
"Can you join these two
triangles with full sides
touching to make a
rectangle?"

50E87325259140A182CBD83E11FBB9E4.description:
Model shapes in
the world by building
shapes from
components (e.g., sticks
and clay balls) and
drawing shapes.

3AE123D1EF6740EDB1DE5F7F9F4BF78B.description:
Analyze and
Compare two- and
three-dimensional
shapes, in different sizes
and orientations, using
informal language to
describe their
similarities, differences,
parts (e.g., number of
sides and
vertices/"corners") and
other attributes (e.g.,
having sides of equal
length).

C0813306827E43E298B28679612981EB.description:
Identify shapes
as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat"
or three-dimensional,
"solid").

E681C06C25E24D9E9F20DE72C785F399.description:
Create and
Represent threedimensional shapes
(ball/sphere, square
box/cube, tube/cylinder)
using various
manipulative materials
(such as popsicle sticks,
blocks, pipe cleaners,
pattern blocks).

FEE58DD4BD2F48EAB6301A3BDCB04432.description: Analyze, Compare, Create, And Compose Shapes

778D71C757D74776BCF4C478E707D01E.description:
Correctly name
shapes regardless of
their orientations or
overall size.

E0BB8DBB3C4A48FDAA318A4D9976A695.description:
Identify
various two-dimensional
shapes using appropriate
language.

CF9B3CA3B9D14D2CBC60783A3DAB44F8.description:
Describe objects
in the environment
using names of shapes,
and Describe the
relative positions of
these objects using
terms such as above,
below, beside, in front
of, behind, and next to.

390D0C2D674D4A089F3EC1DBE80EC0CB.description:
Identify
relative positions of
objects in space, and use
appropriate language
(e.g., beside, inside, next to, close to, above,
below, apart).

3DC8582BE1644FA2819B2678DC8E6D5C.description: Identify and Describe Shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles)

81C249A7050E4AD0A12B2AF915716AEB.description:
NO Standard
for working with
money.

EABE91A004EF43C68D53ED0DD15C5728.description:
Recognize
that certain objects are
coins and that dollars
and coins represent
money

2D88E1B3FF0845F690D0F04A5259E9F4.description:
Classify
objects into given
categories; count the
numbers of objects in
each category and sort
the categories by
count for category
counts up to and
including 10.

1ACA1AB36F7D40E28B53D6792F38E924.description:
Sort,
categorize, and classify
objects by more than
one attribute.

D4279C0440B54ACFA59DFE201FEFF884.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category

Directly
compare two objects
with a measurable
attribute in common, to
see which object has
"more of"/"less of" the
attribute, and describe
the difference. For
example, directly
compare the heights of
two children and
describe one child as
taller/shorter.

A0FB05CD613A45A5BE2D0BEFEE228E73.description:
Compare
the attributes of length
and weight for two
objects, including
longer/shorter, same
length; heavier/lighter,
same weight; holds
more/less, holds the
same amount.

9FB61E36791B4243BD4FF27D8E970AE9.description:
Describe
measurable attributes
of objects, such as
length or weight.
Describe several
measurable attributes
of a single object.

A1E3F10C977B4EFBB41C5DAA29A16AC8.description:
Recognize
the attributes of length,
area, weight, and
capacity of everyday
objects using
appropriate vocabulary
(e.g., long, short, tall,
heavy, light, big, small,
wide, narrow).

Compose and
decompose numbers
from 11 to 19 into ten
ones and some further
ones, e.g., by using
objects or drawings, and
record each composition
or decomposition by a
drawing or equation
(e.g., 18 = 10 + 8);
understand that these
numbers are composed
of ten ones and one,
two, three, four, five,
six, seven, eight, or nine
ones.

6DBE74764D8A48E4BE61F3B904B0CBFD.description: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value

774B09A092AC4240A9629298868D4A7B.description: NUMBER AND OPPERATIONS IN BASE TEN (NBT)

7A4FAC76734745EB9A512CC2DF039950.description:
Fluently add
and subtract within 5
including zero.

For any
number from 1 to 9, find
the number that makes
10 when added to the
given number, e.g., by
using objects or
drawings, and record the
answer with a drawing
or equation.

D3C7EA1DB1BE4339A2CC6920F9794787.description:
Decompose
numbers less than or
equal to 10 into pairs in
more than one way, e.g.,
by using objects or
drawings, and record
each decomposition by a
drawing or equation
(e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4
+ 1).

E213272063E148F1B3BB387AAAE62407.description:
Solve addition
and subtraction word
problems, and add and
subtract within 10, e.g.,
by using objects or
drawings to represent
the problem.

84539324C35A4A9B95F53BFE4CAD27DC.description:
Represent
addition and subtraction
with objects, fingers,
mental images,
drawings, sounds (e.g.,
claps), acting out
situations, verbal
explanations,
expressions, or
equations.

9A61050729784C819F68243B6AE2D2DD.description:
Use concrete
objects to model realworld addition (putting
together) and
subtraction (taking
away) problems up
through five.

numbers between 1 and
10 presented as written
numerals.

whether the number of
objects in one group is
greater than, less than,
or equal to the number
of objects in another
group for groups with
up to ten objects, e.g.,
by using matching and
counting strategies.

0A94E0EDF579473AA30468180D8DD9DA.description:
Count to
answer "how many?"
questions about as many
as 20 things arranged in
a line, a rectangular
array, or a circle, or as
many as 10 things in a
scattered configuration;
given a number from 1-
20, count out that many
objects.

035CE002F7034485805447FF4DC1ACC6.description:
Use
comparative language,
such as more/less than,
equal to, to compare and
describe collections of
objects.

224E7B7D946B465D9CC78B3000266BCE.description:
Understand that each
successive number name refers to a
quantity that is one
larger.

E30755A9668A45B981A8E236693E70D5.description:
Understand that the
last number name said
tells the number of
objects counted. The
number of objects is the
same regardless of their
arrangement or the order
in which they were
counted.

AB4DCF5FB1634EC6AF48FC9D8B745989.description:
When counting
objects, say the number
names in the standard
order, pairing each
object with one and only
one number name and
each number name with
one and only one object.

4B8BA373B8F840DC8420C855344E0015.description:
Understand the
relationship between
numbers and quantities;
connect counting to
cardinality.

7A3514B4383E4B62A1EE0FF70A414C8A.description:
Count many
kinds of concrete
objects and actions up to
ten, recognizing the
“one more”, “one less”
patterns, using one-toone correspondence, and
accurately count as
many as seven things in a scattered
configuration.

23A3553B9F674D27BDFE0C574EB6D966.description:
Write numbers
from 0 to 20. Represent
a number of objects
with a written numeral
0–20 (with 0
representing a count of
no objects).

90540FB3A6FD462987D647A8F22C3B72.description:
Understand
the relationships
between numerals and
quantities up to ten.

B7BE4DBE2D144168A0D58B2A6DC1D4BB.description: Count to tell the number of objects

19B3A72B04674E5A93F0AA4F550B08D8.description:
Count forward,
beginning from a given
number within the known
sequence (instead of
having to begin at 1).

800FDD67E7BA4CE6A222B1DC47BA0D97.description:
Count to 100 by
ones and by tens
Recognize the “one
more” and “ten more”
pattern of counting.

F3A4831B02EE45A999CB024FA5CF4D8D.description:
Listen to and
say the names of
numbers in meaningful
contexts.

26C5B0D4A0CD4C989E8510F1AA349EBF.description: Know number names and the count sequence

standardSets.title: Science and Technology/Engineering
standardSets.subject: Guidelines for Preschool and Kindergarten Learning Experiences (2019-)

Connect daily
experience and investigations to
demonstrate the relationships
between the size and shape of
shadows, the objects creating the
shadow, and the light source.

Investigate
sounds made by different objects and
materials and discuss explanations about what is causing the sounds.

identify ways to manipulate different
objects and materials that make
sound to change volume and pitch.

design and build a prototype of a
structure that will reduce the
warming effect of sunlight on an
area. *

determine that sunlight warms
materials on Earth’s surface.

Through
experience, develop awareness of
factors that influence whether things
stand or fall.

different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the
motion of an object.

Using evidence,
discuss ideas about what is making
something move the way it does and
how some movements can be
controlled.

Recognize
through investigation that physical
objects and materials can change
under different circumstances.

between the properties of an object
and those of the material of which it
is made.

natural and human-made objects to

objects based on observable physical
characteristics, uses, and whether
something is manufactured or occurs
in nature.

Investigate and
communicate the idea that different
kinds of materials can be solid or
liquid depending on temperature.

and investigate the differences
between liquids and solids and
develop awareness that a liquid can
become a solid and vice versa.

Use observations
to recognize differences and
similarities among themselves and

standardSets.title: Comprehensive Health
standardSets.subject: Guidelines for Preschool and Kindergarten Learning Experiences (2019-)

C65F5FCB17BF4F22877F913A6E0F7552.description:
Community and Public Health. Students will learn the influence of social factors on health and contribution of public health and gain skills to
promote health and to collaborate with others to facilitate healthy, safe, and supportive communities.

AF71373AF9FE4EB98008B1EE3F84E750.description:
Ecological Health. Students will gain knowledge of the interdependence between the environment and human health and acquire skills to care for the
environment.

1AA2C6164AAF4BDCA7E933CC4C4B3146.description:
Consumer Health and Resource Management. Students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to obtain, manage, and evaluate resources to
maintain physical and mental health and wellbeing for themselves, their families, and their communities.

08517A872C9F4CC5949AFE3E98D8198F.description:
Violence Prevention. Students will learn how their actions affect others, understand the power that positive character traits can have in violence
prevention, gain skills to report incidents of violence and hurtful behavior to adults in the school and community, avoid engaging in violence, and
identify constructive alternatives to violence, including how to discourage others from engaging in violence.

4480E43158484EE3A7DB61F3645AE00E.description:
Tobacco, Alcohol and Other Substances. Students will acquire the knowledge and skills to be competent in making health-enhancing decisions about
the use of medications and avoidance of substances, and in communicating about substance use/abuse prevention for healthier homes, schools, and
communities.

79090969112140EF8CE69B7EE9CEDDB1.description:
Safety and Injury Prevention. Students will gain the knowledge and skills to administer first aid and carry out emergency procedures, including
cardiopulmonary resuscitation, avoid, recognize, and report verbal, physical, and emotional abuse situations, and assess factors that contribute to
intentional and unintentional injury, including motor vehicle accidents, fire safety, and weapons safety.

083D1C9B2B5F4B78BA24F0D9458AD16C.description:
Disease Prevention and Control. Students will learn the signs, symptoms, and treatment of chronic and communicable diseases, and gain skills
related to health promotion, disease prevention, and health maintenance.

43FFA67DD22B4955ADFAE7DC26CD9143.description:
Reproduction/Sexuality. Students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to make effective personal decisions that promote their emotional,
sexual, and reproductive health.

E71E5F85F9D04A87B1E48D3886BE8CA0.description: Nutrition. Students will gain the knowledge and skills to select a diet that supports health and reduces the risk of illness and future chronic diseases.

6B69AE880B80471FBB9ED782BBFA8475.description:
Physical Activities and Fitness. Students will, by repeated practice, acquire and refine a variety of manipulative, locomotor, and non-locomotor
movement skills, and use principles of training and conditioning, learn biomechanics and exercise physiology, and apply the concept of wellness to
their lives.

8965C52B7049459C8A77B9CC3E13E03F.description:
Growth and Development. Students will learn the basic characteristics of physical growth and development, including body functions and systems
throughout the life cycle, and acquire skills to promote and maintain positive growth and development.

standardSets.title: The Arts
standardSets.subject: Guidelines for Preschool and Kindergarten Learning Experiences (2019-)

0C98B7E638A5464191C13455C429547F.description:
Critical Response. Students will describe and analyze their own work and the work of others using appropriate visual arts vocabulary. When
appropriate, students will connect their analysis to interpretation and evaluation.

90B240155CA7475D838CD1DA24BFCF4C.description:
Drafting, Revising, and Exhibiting. Students will demonstrate knowledge of the processes of creating and exhibiting their own artwork: drafts,
critique, self-assessment, refinement, and exhibit preparation.

E64014FFBBDA4920B71D8CC9E6D430C1.description:
Observation, Abstraction, Invention, and Expression. Students will demonstrate their powers of observation, abstraction, invention, and
expression in a variety of media, materials, and techniques.

94D3DB0C5408464F969B11AC26D48259.description: Elements and Principles of Design. Students will demonstrate knowledge of the elements and principles of design.

F748EB9347774BAAA9281D3ADDFB8182.description: Methods, Materials, and Techniques. Students will demonstrate knowledge of the methods, materials, and techniques unique to the visual arts.

F93990D5944F4E9C8F3A9F62CB93600C.description:
Critical Response. Students will describe and analyze their own theatrical work and the work of others using appropriate theatre vocabulary. When
appropriate, students will connect their analysis to interpretation and evaluation.

8E76BE7B235B4FD0B6FB1DE697109903.description: Technical Theatre. Students will demonstrate skills in using the basic tools, media, and techniques involved in theatrical production.

1FE3388EF664482F9F5E85D55BE8E29A.description: Directing. Students will rehearse and stage dramatic works.

47FCE544DEE24A1CA59C4F22A1DEFB91.description: Reading and Writing Scripts. Students will read, analyze, and write dramatic material.

AD5A1297BDF342F0A9114DD9A87C19ED.description: Acting. Students will develop acting skills to portray characters who interact in improvised and scripted scenes.

32464D0E4C3F4343AC4154E105DC79BE.description:
Critical Response. Students will describe and analyze their own music and the music of others using appropriate music vocabulary. When
appropriate, students will connect their analysis to interpretation and evaluation.

7A21E99772594916B3A78D479350974D.description: Improvisation and Composition. Students will improvise, compose, and arrange music.

169FBD48920B468A96B348E443068BF1.description: Playing Instruments. Students will play instruments, alone and with others, to perform a varied repertoire of music.

24A8C96CF2F34C85B195B901E78E591C.description: Reading and Notation. Students will read music written in standard notation.

F15CFEC3FC4147B797CA500C495B4D84.description: Singing. Students will sing, alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

922DF68354C740DE9B22E6F62FED89FA.description:
Critical Response. Students will describe and analyze their own dances and the dances of others using appropriate dance vocabulary. When
appropriate, students will connect their analysis to interpretation and evaluation.

ACB2718C65A84562A6D21EA05D47EC43.description: Performance in Dance. Students will rehearse and stage dance works.

9E8BF4336BBD4168A844390346A2686F.description: Dance as Expression. Students will demonstrate an understanding of dance as a way to express and communicate meaning.

FBA824BB4671434299E03CF7A8664BA4.description: Choreography. Students will create movement compositions based on choreographic principles, processes, and forms.

5EEA05A17FEB4E71B4C2B6986B2A8E90.description: Movement Elements and Dance Skills. Students will identify and demonstrate movement elements and dance skills.
